News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

Sports.title: Forget £117million Morgan Rogers – Chelsea’s best summer signing could be off the pitch with Austin MacPhee grab
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S signing of the summer from Aston Villa isn’t Morgan Rogers, it’s their set-piece coach – Austin MacPhee.

And Villa supporters may well be more gutted about losing the man whose face they emblazoned over that of Christ the Redeemer than their biggest attacking threat.



New Blues set piece coach MacPhee, much like Arsenal‘s Nicolas Jover, is part of a new generation of coaches who are becoming equally as important as the players in the starting eleven – if not more so.

And, like Jover, he’s justifying his level of influence with undeniable results.



Last season, Aston Villa scored 29 set-piece goals – the joint-most across Europe alongside Arsenal – and in the last three seasons, a total of 74 dead-ball situations ended up with the ball in the back of the net.

That would probably explain the prominence of “Austin MacPhee, Ole, Ole” being sung in a Brummie accent by the Holte End on numerous chilly nights at Villa Park.



Much like in Arsenal’s title-winning season, set-piece goals at Villa Park had form for being celebrated with a little extra vim than those scored from open play – all down to MacPhee’s efficiency, creativity, and lovable character.

46-year-old MacPhee, born in Kirkcaldy, Scotland, rocks long Blonde hair and his unique aesthetic will certainly stand out on the touchline as something of a love-child between an Aussie surfing champion, retired drummer, and Jesus Christ – hence the Christ the Redeemer memes on social media.

His playing career was short-lived, playing in his youth for Forfar Athletic until he was 20, when he moved to the USA to play college soccer with Wilmington Seahawks.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He spent one year with Romanian club Dacia Unirea Brăila before finishing his career in Japan – so his footballing education is cultured to say the least.



As a coach, he held head coach and assistant head coach roles with Cupar Hearts, Cowdenbeath, St Mirren, Northern Ireland, and Hearts before his niche talent of working specifically with set-pieces was unearthed.

After leaving Hearts, MacPhee joined Midtjylland in the Danish league as a specialist set piece coach, then moving on to Villa Park where he really made his name as a set-piece king.

A goal from a corner in Villa’s Europa League final win wrote his name into the Villains’ history books before Chelsea paid an undisclosed fee to bring him to Stamford Bridge.

It will have been nowhere near the £117m they paid for Rogers, mind.

Arsenal laid the blueprint last season, in how set pieces can be the difference between winning the Premier League and falling short.



Chelsea, it seems, are looking to follow it, and know they need to improve in terms of defending set pieces in particular.

The Blues, in a season that saw three different head coaches in the dugout backed by former set-piece coach Bernardo Cueva, scored 21 goals coached by the Portuguese specialist, though they conceded 19 – Aston Villa conceded three less with 16.

Arsenal conceded just eight.



In terms of attacking, it is MacPhee’s creativity that sets him apart from others who also play his role.

Goals from set-pieces for Villa last season came with astonishing variety – some being played short, some going straight in, and multiple players playing various different roles to confuse the opposition.

The Europa League final against Freiburg was a perfect example, as was Morgan Rogers‘ stunner vs Liverpool earlier on in the season.

Unai Emery hailed him as a “Fantastic creator”, and his ability to connect with players was praised by Portugal head coach Roberto Martinez in an interview with The Atheltic, where he said: “He’s got a real knack to connect with the player and that’s what makes him so good at his job.”

He will have to pick out the tactical minds in Xabi Alonso‘s Chelsea side who can best play specific roles such as being a blocker, the initial taker, the crosser, and the finisher of the opportunities that will come for the Blues.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Perhaps Marc Cucurella will be sorely missed in that sense for his tactical nouse, while keeping someone like Enzo Fernandez could be paramount to success next season, with Reece James‘ deliveries being some of the best in the league.

If the Blues and MacPhee can get it right, with only one game a week and plenty of time in midweek to work on their set-pieces in comparison to last season, there could be a Christ the Redeemer mural with MacPhee’s face on it at Stamford Bridge before you know it.

Sports.title: Former Chelsea and AC Milan star Alexandre Pato ‘closing in’ on takeover of League Two club after failed Colchester deal
Sports.content:
EX-CHELSEA ace Alexandre Pato is set to take over Northampton as part of a consortium.

Pato, 36, rolled credits on a 17-year career in 2023 after stints with the Blues, AC Milan and Brazil.



And now the former forward is following in the footsteps of other ex-sports stars like Manchester United legend David Beckham and NFL great Tom Brady by crossing over to club ownership.

According to the BBC, the Brazilian’s Sports Alpha Capital group is set to buy a majority stake in Northampton.



It is understood Pato is involved with the consortium but is not the one fronting it.

Northampton chairman Kelvin Thomas confirmed last month a “well-funded” group’s proposed investment was “pretty much agreed”.



This comes after Pato’s consortium was in discussions about taking over Colchester earlier this year.

However, Sports Alpha Capital decided to pull out of a potential deal for the League Two outfit following initial talks.

Pato now looks set to take over Northampton after a disappointing campaign that saw them getting relegated to the fourth tier.

The Cobblers finished bottom of the League One table last season.

Pato rose to prominence in 2007 at Milan where he amassed a total of 63 goals and 18 assists in 150 appearances throughout a six-year run with the Serie A giants.

The ex-Villarreal star then underwent half a season on loan at Chelsea in 2016 where he only registered two appearances and one goal on his debut across all competitions.

Pato also got 10 goals and two assists in 27 caps with Brazil from 2008 until 2013.

Sports.title: Why are clubs starting their Carabao Cup campaigns on a weekend?
Sports.content:
CLUB football is finally back!

The Carabao Cup first round begins today with fixtures scheduled across the next four days.



Clubs from the Championship, League One and League Two get their campaigns underway as managers get one final look at their sides before league action starts next week.

Fans might be surprised to see Carabao Cup fixtures scheduled over the weekend instead of midweek.



SunSport brings you the reason behind the early start to the competition.

Why is Carabao Cup starting on a weekend?

The Carabao Cup gets underway on Thursday, August 6, with first round ties running until Monday, August 10.

The competition usually begins on a midweek date following the opening round of EFL fixtures.

League One and Two teams were unhappy their seasons kicked off on the first weekend of August last year because it did not allow them enough time to get transfer business done before the campaign began.

With the season starting later than normal because of the World Cup in the USA, Mexico and Canada, the EFL were keen to take away some strain from fixture congestion to make up for the later start.

The Carabao Cup starting a week before the league season allows players more rest than in other seasons.



Teams can end up playing three times in quick succession as the first round is traditionally in the middle of two league fixtures.

Sports.title: England STILL on course to boycott World Cup as shamed Fifa told ‘conditions have not been met’ over reversal
Sports.content:
ENGLAND are still on course to boycott the World Cup, despite Fifa’s hated bid to sell off the World Cup collapsing.

Gianni Infantino plunged world football into chaos last week with his plot to create, and sell off a chunk of, a new Fifa subsidiary in charge of money-making assets including the World Cup.



Uefa nations vowed to boycott Fifa competitions unless the project was dropped.

Infantino’s plot subsequently collapsed on Friday night.



But Uefa have now confirmed that its conditions for dropping its boycott have not yet been met by Infantino and Co.

A spokesperson told Sky News: “Uefa’s associations were very clear about the conditions attached to the non-participation in Fifa competitions.



“First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

“These conditions have not been met. In addition, Uefa made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency. That position holds.

“Yesterday’s announcement that some people employed by the Fifa president (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing.”

Infantino yesterday apologised for his hated plot to sell the World Cup.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But the 56-year-old vowed to stay on and fight for his job, rather than resign as Uefa would like.

In a joint letter signed by Infantino and secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, senior officials said: “We sincerely apologise for these errors and commit to them not happening again.

“We acknowledge that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.

“With this in mind, we will conduct a necessary review, and a report will be presented to the FIFA Council at its next scheduled meeting.”



The statement also contained a strongly worded warning after confidential details of the proposal were leaked.

It said: “With the project withdrawn, Fifa will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation.”

But in spite of the apology, Fifa covered bases as they defended the legality of their actions.

They wrote: “Everything that was done, was done in full compliance with the Fifa regulatory framework.”

The letter also added unanimous backing for Infantino from Fifa’s senior leadership following a meeting in Rabat, Morocco.



They detailed how the president, secretary general, and administration spoke with “one voice and working as one team”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

According to The Guardian, Uefa are set to form a commission in order to evaluate Fifa’s World Cup plot.

The move comes amid concerns that Fifa were set to flog future World Cup profits for “below the market rate”.

Sports.title: Football club SUSPENDED by National League with opening fixtures postponed just hours before season starts
Sports.content:
EBBSFLEET UNITED have been suspended by the National League amid serious financial concerns.

The Kent side, who compete in the National League South, were reportedly issued a winding-up petition by HM Revenue & Customs earlier this year.



A National League Committee has decided to suspend Ebbsfleet pending further review.

The sixth-tier side will have until 5pm on August 18 to prove that they can meet their financial obligations for the campaign ahead.



Ebbsfleet’s situation will then be reviewed again by the National League’s Compliance and Licensing Committee the following day.

The Committee’s decision has led to Ebbsfleet’s first three games of the season being postponed.



Josh Wright’s side had been due to begin their season this Saturday with a trip to Slough.

Further games against Folkestone Invicta and Chelmsford City have also been KO’d.

Pending the result of the review, Ebbsfleet could return to action at home to AFC Totton on August 22.

A National League statement read: “The National League’s Compliance and Licensing Committee convened on 5 August 2026, following recent correspondence and information relevant to the club, to further consider ongoing issues regarding Ebbsfleet United FC and its financial position.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“The club, which competes in the National League South, has previously been found in breach of National League regulations and is under embargo.

“One significant issue is settlement of PAYE liabilities dating back to April 2026, which led to HM Revenue & Customs reportedly issuing a winding-up petition against the club.

“The Committee considered ongoing non-compliance, in particular under Appendix H of the National League Financial Reporting Initiative.

“Appendix D Clause 4.3 of the National League Financial Reporting Initiative relates to a club’s ongoing obligations in relation to its financial position.



“The Committee determined that these obligations are not met to its satisfaction, specifically regarding the club’s ability to meet its financial obligations throughout the 2026/27 Season.

“Following careful consideration, the Committee has taken the decision under applicable regulations to suspend Ebbsfleet United FC, with a review to be undertaken by the Committee on 19 August.

“As a result of suspension, at this time, the club will not be able to fulfil the opening three fixtures of the coming Season.

“A detailed letter has been issued to the club today, setting out the Committee’s decision. Ebbsfleet United FC has until 5.00pm on Tuesday 18 August to provide satisfactory evidence that its obligations have been and will be met in accordance with applicable regulations.

“The club remains subject to embargo until such time as the Committee is satisfied that relevant matters have been resolved.



“Opponent clubs for the first three published fixtures have been informed of the decision. Others have also been informed, including the Independent Football Regulator.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ebbsfleet responded with a statement of their own, calling the decision “extremely upsetting” and asking for “understanding” while their ownership situation is resolved.

They concluded: “Everyone has worked so hard and completed an excellent pre-season and we look forward to this being rectified and demonstrating the results of that hard work throughout the season.”

Sports.title: Man Utd tell at least three academy stars they can LEAVE permanently as four are made untouchable
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have told at least three youngsters they can leave the club permanently this summer.

And the Red Devils are open to loan offers for virtually their entire Under-21 squad.



Only a select group—including Shea Lacey, Jack and Tyler Fletcher, and 15-year-old JJ Gabriel—are strictly off-limits.

Dan Gore is the latest player facing a permanent exit from Old Trafford, alongside Harry Amass and Toby Collyer.



Like Collyer, Gore was left out of the squad that travelled to Stockholm for the 2-1 pre-season friendly win over Atletico Madrid.

The midfielder instead captained United’s Under-21s in their 1-0 defeat to non-league Altrincham Town on Friday night.

Left-back Amass, 19, is set to be sold for around £6million this summer, with several Championship sides interested.

A new loan is unlikely as United have allowed the clock to run down on Amass’ contract, which was signed in 2023 and expires next summer.

Gore, 21, had two individually successful loan stints with Rotherham United, but the club were relegated from League One at the end of the season.

His only senior appearance for United was against Crystal Palace in the League Cup in September 2023.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Newly promoted Hull City hold an interest in re-signing 22-year-old Collyer following his injury-ravaged loan there last season.

Midfielder Jacob Devaney is another who could go out this summer but United are looking at a loan move for him. Striker Chido Obi also has an uncertain future.

Obi is open to a loan, but United will only sanction a move that guarantees him regular playing time.

New midfielder Cristian Orozco, 18, is likely to stay in-house while he is assessed, gets used to the UK and takes English lessons.



Meanwhile, goalkeeper Radek Vitek is set to become the club’s third sale of the summer after United agreed an up-front £7m fee with Middlesbrough, in a package that could rise to £14m in add-ons related to appearances.

Vitek is the latest to depart, following Rasmus Hojlund and Tyler Fredricson, who moved to Napoli and Lausanne-Sport, respectively.

Meanwhile, Lacey will look to build on last season’s first-team breakthrough alongside the Fletcher twins, while Gabriel is closing in on his senior debut.

Sports.title: Arsenal files: Ethan Nwaneri facing uncertain future, newbie in stands for Real Betis clash & Heinze letting off steam
Sports.content:
ETHAN NWANERI is being tracked by RB Leipzig.

The Arsenal midfielder, 19, faces an uncertain future this summer after spending the second half of last season on loan at Marseille.



SunSport has reported previously how Borussia Dortmund are keeping tabs on the situation.

And it is understood that RB Leipzig are another side paying close attention to Nwaneri’s movements.



The German side have the Arsenal wonderkid on their long list of targets for this summer’s transfer window.

The club is renowned for developing young talent and has an impressive track record of bringing players through.



The Gunners are yet to decide if they will cash in on Nwaneri, who signed a five-year contract only 12 months ago.

The midfielder has stiff competition for minutes at the Emirates, especially as Arsenal are set to sign Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes.

That could force Nwaneri to look for opportunities elsewhere and another loan has not been ruled out.

A permanent sale would significantly boost the Gunners’ finances, though, as the teenager is an academy product, meaning he counts as pure profit on the club’s books.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

TEEN SPIRIT

FUTURE star Victor Ozhianvuna was in the stands at the Aviva Stadium as Arsenal took on Real Betis in Dublin last night.

The 17-year-old watched from the sell-out crowd as Arsenal were thumped 3-1 by Betis.

Ozhianvuna penned a pre-contract with the Gunners last October and will officially join the club in January once he has turned 18.

The highly-rated midfielder currently plays for Dublin-based club Shamrock Rovers, where he has already made over 30 league appearances despite his age.



His move to North London is the most expensive transfer in League of Ireland history, pocketing Shamrock Rovers £1.7m.

Ozhianvuna is one of a host of exciting youth arrivals that Arsenal feel can help push their academy to another level.

The Gunners have already signed Ecuadorian twins Holger and Edwin Quintero and are close to completing the signing of Cardiff City teenager Axel Donczew.

Arsenal are also hoping to finally snap up Blackburn wonderkid Igor Tyjon this summer, having pursued the 18-year-old for over a year.

TENSIONS ARE HEI

GABRIEL HEINZE was so worked up after Arsenal’s 4-1 pre-season win over Girona that he had to warm down on an exercise bike.



The Gunners coach is known for intense work ethic and fiery personality, and clearly doesn’t let that guard down for pre-season.

After Arsenal’s win out in Spain, Heinze was spotted using the players’ warm-down bikes to blow off some steam.

The Argentine was locked in an intense conversation with Mikel Arteta while he used the bike, making for an unusual post-match moment.

YOUR NUMBER’S UP

BRUNO GUIMARAES may have a battle on his hands to try and secure his favoured No39 shirt ahead of his £75m move to Arsenal.



The Brazilian midfielder has always worn the number 39 on his back as a homage to his father.

The number matches that of the dispatch cab – 039 – driven by his father, Dick Gomez, in Rio de Janeiro.

However, during Arsenal’s pre-season tour, youngster Louie Copley has been donning the No39 shirt.

And Guimaraes may have to see if he can pinch the number off the 19-year-old if he wants to keep his tradition going.



Highly-rated defender Copley was forced off with what appeared to be a serious injury during Arsenal’s 3-1 defeat to Real Betis on Wednesday night.

NEW ARRIVAL

ARSENAL have continued to bolster their medical department by hiring two new physios for the academy.

Sanchez-Jeremiah Davis has joined the club after previously working with Crystal Palace.

He announced the news via his Instagram account, therastaphysio, writing: “Thrilled to announce that I’m joining Arsenal FC as Academy Physiotherapist!

“Proud to be part of The Culture Club — The Champions of England — and excited for what’s ahead in this next step of my football physiotherapy career.



“Grateful for the opportunity and ready to get to work.”

Omar Mahgoub is also joining the academy setup after previously being across London at Brentford.

MODEL PROFESSIONAL

NONI MADUEKE has been swapping the training pitch for the studio as he featured in a modelling campaign for Adidas and retailer ASOS.

Madueke, 24, modelled a new collection of Adidas Originals menswear for the campaign, which launched last week.



The England star was the face of the campaign and had his pictures plastered all over the ASOS website.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Madueke is yet to return to pre-season training following his effort at the World Cup with the Three Lions.

The tricky winger is due to get back on the pitch in the coming weeks alongside Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Ebere Eze, Mikel Merino and David Raya.

Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s desperate tactics fail as UEFA confirm World Cup boycott STANDS

UEFA previously announced plans to boycott future World Cups in the wake of Gianni Infantino's botched plans to sell off stakes in FIFA tournaments to private investors

View Image FIFA chief Gianni Infantino is still under significant pressure (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

UEFA have dropped a bombshell on Gianni Infantino by confirming their boycott of future tournaments still stands, with the beleaguered FIFA chief clinging onto his position.

‌



Infantino was forced to withdraw plans to sell off future FIFA tournaments to private investors following a furious backlash from football federation's, the vast majority of whom condemned the plans. UEFA provided the strongest rebuttal, insisting it's nations would boycott the next World Cup if the plans were not abandoned.

‌



And they have reaffirmed that European nations will not participate in FIFA's events if their conditions following the scandal are not met, including assurances that such a plot would never be concocted again, after it emerged Infantino retained the 'full sport' of FIFA's board on Wednesday night.

‌



A UEFA statement shared on Thursday afternoon read: "UEFA's associations were very clear about the conditions attached to the non-participation in FIFA competitions.

Fight to oust shameless Gianni Infantino is just starting - UEFA must not let up READ MORE :

Argentina announce national holiday to celebrate England win as Falklands banner plan emerges READ MORE :

"First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

‌



"These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.

"Yesterday's (Wednesday) announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."

UEFA's latest public attack on Infantino means the significant heat which has been on the Swiss executive in recent weeks is unlikely to subside anytime soon.

Sports.title: Mo Salah is taking a step down with Turkey move but it is about more than just money
Sports.content:
Mo Salah is taking a step down with Turkey move but it is about more than just money

Jamie Carragher has said he was surprised by the Liverpool legend's switch to Trabzonspor but Super Lig clubs are spending big and attracting some top talent

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah has signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor (Image: OZAN KOSE, AFP via Getty Images)

As usual, Jamie Carragher makes a very valid point when he suggests that Mohamed Salah is still good enough to be playing in a competition of a higher standard than the Turkish Süper Lig.

‌



Salah is certainly good enough to still be a major performer in the Champions League but will have to be content with playing in the Europa League next season, assuming Trabzonspor negotiates the qualifying round.

‌



Let’s face it, Salah is still good enough to be playing in the Premier League but you can assume that prospect was contractually removed when the player and Liverpool agreed to part ways a year early. Anyway, Salah probably could not countenance playing for another Premier League club. Not yet, anyway.

‌



But there must have been interest from some blue-chip Champions League clubs in a 34-year-old all-time Premier League great who, by his standards, had an average time of things last season but was still one of Liverpool’s better performers. Which is why the obvious conclusion is that Trabzonspor are paying fantastic wages.

Jamie Carragher criticises Mohamed Salah's Turkey move after Liverpool exit READ MORE :

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

That will certainly be the case. The marquee Turkish clubs - Istanbul’s big three, Galatasary, Fenerbahce and Besiktas, plus Trabzonspor - are spending big on players and contracts despite being burdened with heavy debt.

Salah will be playing in a league that will feature the likes of Victor Osimhen, Leroy Sane, Ilkay Gundogan, Leandro Trossard and Nathan Ake this coming season. And there will probably be more to follow.

‌



But it will take many more recruits of that quality to make Turkish club football a major force in European football. Since Galatasaray won the UEFA Cup in 2000, only one Turkish side has reached the semi-finals of a major UEFA competition.

View 3 Images Leandro Trossard left Arsenal for Besiktas earlier this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Opta currently ranks it as the 14th strongest domestic league in world football, behind national competitions in countries such as Denmark and Poland. According to Opta, England’s Championship is stronger.

‌



That would seem to be stretching it a little but there is no doubt, of course, that Salah is taking a significantly-sized step backwards in terms of the overall quality of the league he is operating in. But aside from the considerable financial attraction - his deal is said to be worth around £14million a year - perhaps Salah just wanted a different experience.

For sure, the Premier League is ultra-competitive and generates enormous interest. Stadiums are full and it is a commercial behemoth.

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah was greeted by thousands of Trabzonspor fans when he arrived at the airport (Image: Hakan Burak Altunoz/Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



But sometimes, it feels a little bit too sanitised, a little bit too polished, a little bit too commercial. Tunnel clubs for wealthy fans, hospitality takeovers. And to be honest, even on the pitch, everything has become a little sanitised. Very good but not as edgy as it once was.

Perhaps Salah fancied something a little more visceral, a little more unpredictable, a little more volatile (a lot more volatile), a little more raw. He might have just fancied the cash, of course, but maybe that was not the be-all and end-all.

Yes, you might have expected him to rock up in Serie A but he has made a fascinating decision late in his career. And it will be fascinating to see how it works out.

Sports.title: 7 transfer targets Arsenal could miss out on with Vinicius Jr set to stay at Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Arsenal excited their supporters by making it known they wanted to sign Vinicius Junior this summer, but with the Brazilian star set to sign a new contract with Real Madrid, their interest will come to nothing.

Fresh from winning the Premier League, Arsenal made the ambitious attempt to try and lure one of the world's most exciting players to north London. Knowing Vinicius had entered the final year of his contract, they were willing to make him their highest-paid player.

It was a measure of their upward trajectory in recent years under Mikel Arteta's management that Arsenal thought they had a chance. The possibility of replacing Leandro Trossard with Vinicius on the left wing was certainly an enticing one.

Arsenal forced Real to act, with the Spanish giants increasing their offer to Vinicius to sign a new deal. It now appears very likely that Vinicius will stay with Real and enjoy a status close to Kylian Mbappe's.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

That leaves Arsenal needing to consider alternatives. Julian Alvarez is another high-profile target for sporting director Andrea Berta, who has good connections with Atletico Madrid, having left the Spanish side to join the Gunners. But it is believed that Alvarez has his heart set on a move to Barcelona, not a return to the Premier League.

And it is a similar case with other attackers. Yan Diomande was the hottest name on the market earlier in the summer following a stunning debut campaign at RB Leipzig which caught Arsenal's eye. Now, with the haggling done, Diomande is heading to Real Madrid for a club-record fee of €135million (£115.7m).

Liverpool pulled out of the race for the Ivory Coast international when Leipzig's asking price became clear. Andoni Iraola's side are understood to be pursuing Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola instead. He could end up costing over €100m (£86m).

‌



View 3 Images Julian Alvarez is wanted by Arsenal, but he prefers a move to Barcelona (Image: Europa Press via Getty Images)

HAVE YOUR SAY! Which attacker should Arsenal sign this summer? Comment below.

Arsenal considered Barcola, but are understood to be unwilling to go near PSG's valuation. The French giants are reportedly moving for Ajax's Mika Godts as a replacement for Barcola, landing another player who was on Arsenal's radar.

The Gunners also saw an offer rejected by Juventus for Kenan Yildiz earlier in the summer, with the Italian side unwilling to even consider selling the Turkey international, according to football.london.

‌



Arsenal are among the sides with an interest in Marcus Rashford but, as desperate as they are to offload his £325,000-a-week wages, Manchester United don't want to sell to a Premier League rival. That could change as the window winds down, but Arsenal can hardly afford to play the waiting game.

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford's situation doesn't make doing a deal easy for Arsenal (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

While there are still 26 days until the summer transfer window closes on September 1, Arsenal have so far made little progress in their efforts to seal the blockbuster deal they crave for an attacker. The arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, in a £75m transfer from Newcastle, is imminent, and Christos Tzolis has made an impact in pre-season following a £34m move from Club Brugge, but there is still work to be done.

Arteta has publicly stated Arsenal's ambition this summer. "We are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear," he said in a post-match press conference after facing Girona.

‌



"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else. And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing, we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do."

Their ambition is not in question, with Vinicius and Alvarez clearly fitting the bill as elite-level targets. But that ambition has to be married with realism, because it won't count for anything if they end up empty-handed.

Sports.title: Argentina announce national holiday to celebrate England win as Falklands banner plan emerges
Sports.content:
Argentina announce national holiday to celebrate England win as Falklands banner plan emerges

Argentina beat England in the World Cup semi-finals this summer and controversy followed after players celebrated with a banner referencing the Falklands War

View 3 Images Argentina players celebrated with the banner following the win over England (Image: MB Media, Getty Images)

The Argentine Football Association has earmarked July 15 as National Football Teams Day. The date has been selected in part to commemorate the country's World Cup semi-final victory over England this summer.

‌



It's also emerged that the controversial banner displayed after the game, which backed Argentina's claims to the Falklands, is to be given to Argentine veterans of the conflict. It was on July 15, in Atlanta, that Lionel Scaloni's side dashed England's dreams of reaching a first World Cup final since 1966 with two late goals in a 2–1 victory.

‌



Argentina ultimately lost the final to Spain, 1-0. At a meeting of their Association and Professional League Executive Committee, which was led by Claudio Tapia, the president of the AFA, the organisation decided to mark the day.

‌



A statement said: "The tribute is not solely for that milestone achieved by the senior national team. The recognition is, of course, also for each and every one of the national teams - youth, men’s and women’s - that train day in and day out at the Lionel Andres Messi complex with the hope, joy, and responsibility of defending the national colours."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

England told they must BOYCOTT 2030 World Cup in response to Gianni Infantino plan READ MORE :

A permanent day to remember the victory came as defeating the Three Lions “set the whole country alight, with people flooding the streets in pure celebration," according to the statement.

‌



Argentina's actions in the aftermath of the final whistle led FIFA to open disciplinary proceedings against the country after players unfurled the banner that read: "Las Malvinas son Argentinas." That translates to The Malvinas (the Spanish name for The Falklands) are Argentine.

FIFA say breaches include the use of discriminatory chants and gestures, misconduct, security and protocol failures and the display of inappropriate messages.

View 3 Images England were beaten by a late Argentina comeback in the semi-final (Image: AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

‌

The Falklands are a British Overseas Territory located in the south-west Atlantic Ocean. They are the subject of a fierce dispute between the two nations.

In 1982, Argentina invaded the islands, leading to war. The conflict spanned 74 days and led to the deaths of 655 Argentine and 255 British soldiers, while three people who lived on the islands also died.

‌



The banner was handmade from a bed sheet with the slogan written in black paint. It was passed to former Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez, Tottenham defender Cuti Romero and ex-Spurs player Giovanni Lo Celso, although all the majority of the Argentinian players lined up behind the banner's message.

The banner's creators are reportedly members of a group from Villa Luro, a district of Buenos Aires. According to a report via InfoBae, they managed to smuggle the flag into the stadium in Atlanta by concealing it in their underwear.

View 3 Images Argentina's banner caused a stir (Image: Shaun Botterill, Getty Images)

‌



The DIY flag has since inspired imitations in stadiums across Argentine football, with some clubs, such as Ferro Carril Oeste, adopting the typeface and showing off a version of their own.

It's been claimed the controversial banner is in "good hands" after being kept by Patricio Auber, who accompanied the team delegation to the World Cup. The flag now is said to reside in the country and will soon be handed over to Argentines who fought in the Falklands conflict.

Sports.title: Fight to oust shameless Gianni Infantino is just starting - UEFA must not let up
Sports.content:
In case you are interested, the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) game in Rabat’s Al-Madina Stadium on Wednesday night produced a 2-1 win for Zambia over Malawi. Alas, Nigeria’s 6-2 victory over Egypt in Rabat’s Olympic Stadium meant Zambia have not qualified for the knockout stages, having been pipped on goals scored.

It was quite a dramatic denouement to Group C but the headlines were all about one man in the stands for the Malawi-Zambia game. Sat next to Mattias Grafstrom, FIFA’s general secretary, was Gianni Infantino, brazening it out after receiving support from a meeting of as many of the organisation’s management board as could be bothered attending.

Outside of Africa, the WAFCON is unlikely to get extensive coverage but the point is that Infantino was a major distraction from what should have been the main attraction. The football.

And that, apart from a myriad other things, should tell him that hanging on to power is doing the game a disservice. The FIFA statement released on Wednesday night, and signed by Infantino and Grafstrom, refers to the ‘successful delivery of the FIFA World Cup 2026’.

‌



And to the extent that it happened and a lot of people watched it, they are right. But when players and fans should be reflecting on the kaleidoscope of emotions felt in the wake of a great tournament, they are instead occupied by Infantino’s sell-off scheme, the subsequent backlash and the ramifications of him staying in power.

If you operate on an ‘every cloud/silver lining’ basis, then it spares some nations a bit of soul-searching into their World Cup performances. For example, we are now more concerned about what the Football Association is going to do about Infantino rather than what it is going to do about an extravagantly-paid manager who completely blew it at the crucial moment.

View 3 Images Spain's magnificent achievement has been overshadowed by the controversy generated by Gianni Infantino (Image: Evrim Aydin/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel can thank Infantino for taking away some of the heat. But Infantino’s ill-fated, money-making project has significantly coloured how we now look at World Cup 2026 and its compelling characters on the field of play.

‌



The heroics from Vozinha, the Cape Verde keeper? The brilliance of marquee players such as Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi? Erling Haaland announcing himself on a World Cup stage?

The continuing thrill provided by Lamine Yamal? That epic Mexico-England game in the Azteca? Memories fade but these have been banished in an instant by Infantino’s behaviour.

It now feels like World Cup 2026 was just a sales pitch from Infantino to billionaire private investors. World Cup 2026 goes down in immediate history as the World Cup that was a test drive for private ownership.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino's behaviour has relegated the players' deeds to World Cup sub-plots (Image: Justin Setterfield, Getty Images)

‌



It goes down as a grand finale to an Infantino plot. That plot was foiled and assumptions that Infantino would have no choice but to resign now look decidedly misguided.

Which means the fight to force him out is only just starting. It is a fight that should be led by UEFA, whose nations contributed so much to World Cup 2026, only for their efforts and achievements to be subsequently overshadowed by Infantino’s secret proposals.

There can be no letting up. When one administrator is throwing shade over the brilliance of footballers - whether that be at the World Cup or WAFCON - he simply has to be forced out.

Sports.title: Barcelona join Real Madrid in race to sign Rodri as Man City's transfer stance becomes clear
Sports.content:
Barcelona join Real Madrid in race to sign Rodri as Man City's transfer stance becomes clear

Manchester City star Rodri has found himself at the centre of a battle between Barcelona and Real Madrid for his services this summer after a stand-out performance at the World Cup

View 3 Images Rodri is being chased by Spain's biggest clubs (Image: Getty)

Manchester City's chances of keeping star player Rodri this summer have taken a blow after Barcelona joined Real Madrid in trying to sign him. Rodri is in the final year of his contract with City and it is looking increasingly likely that he will be tempted back to Spain.

‌



As revealed by Mirror Football, City are desperate to keep hold of their key midfielder, with new manager Enzo Maresca wanting to build his team around him. However, Rodri has given no indication that he wants to sign a new contract and recently spoke of a desire to return to play in his native Spain.

‌



Real Madrid made their interest known last month and had been confident of striking a deal for the World Cup winner. But the introduction of Barcelona into the situation could change things.

‌



Barca have decided to join the race after learning that Frenkie de Jong will be sidelined for a long period with a knee injury. While they would need to sell players to create space for the 30-year-old, they hope the presence of many of his international team-mates could aid their pursuit.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

Manchester Evening News reports that City would only sell for a fee which reflects Rodri's status as one of the world's best midfielders. He won the Ballon d'Or in 2024 and has just captained his country to their first World Cup in 16 years while being named Most Valuable Player.

‌



City have splashed out £116million to sign Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest this summer and are also in talks to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille. But they are under no illusions over Rodri's importance to the side, given his pedigree and experience.

Yet with less than 12 months remaining on his contract, City have to be realistic. With Rodri having openly stated a desire to return to Spain, where he previously represented Villarreal and Atletico Madrid, they could be forced to cash in now, rather than risk losing him for nothing next summer.

View 3 Images Rodri is in demand after lifting the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“Would I like to play in Spain again, in La Liga, in Madrid? I would like to return, yes, obviously,” Rodri said while on international duty in April.

“Having played for Atletico before would not prevent me from playing for Real Madrid … there are other players who have done that before. Maybe not direct transfers, but eventually. You can’t turn down one of the world’s best clubs.”

He added: “I have one year left on my contract. There will come a point where we will have to sit down and talk.”

‌



View 3 Images Enzo Maresca wants to keep Rodri

Maresca has tried to calm speculation over his key player, who is yet to join up with his team-mates for pre-season, having undergone a minor surgery on his back and been given an extended break following his World Cup heroics. “It’s just about speculation at the moment,” Maresca said in Hong Kong earlier this week.

“Rodri had the surgery last Monday; everything was fine. Now, some days off and he’ll be back with us when he finishes his holiday.”

Article continues below

Asked if there had been any contract talks with director of football Hugo Viana, Maresca added: “As I said, the main focus for him when the season finished was the FIFA World Cup. Now, he is enjoying some rest after that and we didn’t have any conversations just focused on Rodri.”

Sports.title: UEFA boycott of FIFA tournaments still stands as Infantino stays on
Sports.content:
UEFA's boycott of FIFA tournaments still stands, with under-fire FIFA president Gianni Infantino remaining in his position.

On Wednesday night, Infantino had "full support" of FIFA's management board despite being forced to abandon his plan to sell stakes in a company to run the World Cup to private investors.

The Swiss' plan was rejected by three continental confederations before it was withdrawn and led to UEFA threatening to boycott FIFA competitions until it was scrapped - a position which European football's governing body doubled down on on Thursday.

A UEFA statement said: "UEFA's associations were very clear about the conditions attached to the non-participation in FIFA competitions.

"First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

"These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.

"Yesterday's (Wednesday) announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."

More to follow...

Sports.title: Parker claimed failed drug test was caused by cocaine use of nutritionist
Sports.content:
Former heavyweight world champion Joseph Parker claimed a failed drugs test that resulted in him being suspended from boxing was caused by exposure to cocaine being used by his nutritionist, according to UK Anti-Doping (UKAD).

Parker returned an adverse analytical finding (AAF) for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine, during a routine UKAD test shortly after his surprise defeat to Fabio Wardley in London on October 25 last year.

The New Zealander, who has throughout the saga denied taking any prohibited substance, announced on Wednesday that his suspension, which could have lasted as long as two years, had been lifted and that he would be "back in the ring soon".

On Thursday, UKAD officially confirmed Parker was free to resume his career as details of the case were shared, which included the 34-year-old's explanation for the adverse finding.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Joseph Parker’s heavyweight clash with Fabio Wardley at The O2 arena. (Credit: DAZN)

A UKAD statement said: "On 6 March 2026, Mr Parker provided UKAD with evidence claiming that the AAF was the result of his exposure to cocaine used by the nutritionist he had employed in preparation for the bout on 25 October 2025.

"The nutritionist stated that he was a regular user of cocaine and had used cocaine daily in the week leading up to the bout.

"Between 14 April 2026 and 3 June 2026, UKAD requested further information from Mr Parker in relation to his explanation for the AAF. Amongst other matters, Mr Parker stated that he had first worked with the same nutritionist in April 2023."

UKAD explained that a decision had been made to impose a three-month period of ineligibility, which it already considers served, because an independent scientific expert was satisfied that any ingestion of cocaine had occurred out of competition, and therefore in a context unrelated to sporting performance.

Image: Fabio Wardley forced a finish in the 11th round with Parker.

The statement said: "On 15 June 2026, UKAD received an independent scientific expert opinion from its instructed expert, which concluded that Mr Parker's ingestion of cocaine most likely took place out of competition (i.e. before 11:59pm on 24 October 2025).

"On 22 June 2026, UKAD confirmed to Mr Parker that in light of the opinion from its expert, it was satisfied that any ingestion of cocaine occurred out of competition and for that reason would have been in a context unrelated to sport performance.

"Consequently, UKAD lifted Mr Parker's Provisional Suspension on that date (allowing him to resume his participation in sport with immediate effect) and proposed a three-month period of Ineligibility (deemed served) by way of sanction for his Anti-Doping Rule Violation."

The scientific expert believed it possible that Parker's administration of cocaine "may have occurred" from contamination, but also said they could not exclude the possibility the finding had arisen "as the tail end of the administration of a larger pharmacologically active dose of cocaine."

With the UKAD report, the scientific expert said: "It is also my opinion that Mr Parker's administration of cocaine may have occurred orally from food contaminated with cocaine by his sports nutritionist who has admitted being a user of cocaine giving rise to the finding of benzoylecgonine in Mr Parker's urine Samples.

Parker lost his world title to Anthony Joshua in 2018, but went into his fight against Wardley in arguably the best form of his career.

After a punishing loss to Joe Joyce in 2022, Parker won his next six contests prior, picking up statement wins over Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang, as well as winning the WBO Interim strap.

He was due to challenge then-IBF belt-holder Daniel Dubois in February, only for Dubois to fall ill just days before the fight was meant to take place.

Parker put his position as the WBO mandatory challenger to undisputed champion Oleksandr Usyk on the line by taking the fight against Wardley, but it was a gamble that backfired.

Sports.title: Why Jimenez’s Wolves return means so much to fans
Sports.content:
The most romantic signing of the summer came early. Raul Jimenez is back at Wolves. And for the club's supporters, they are not so much welcoming back a former favourite but revisiting a chapter of their own lives. For a generation, Jimenez is the Wolves No 9.

He was the striker who arrived just when Wolves were rediscovering themselves. Promotion became Europe. The best came to Molineux and were beaten. Now, he is returning with Wolves at a low ebb. But this second coming has rejuvenated the club.

The evidence has been overwhelming since Jimenez's signing was confirmed after three seasons away. It was not just the emotional announcement video, although that certainly captured the imagination, instantly transforming the mood after relegation.

You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enable Twitter cookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can change your settings at any time via the Privacy Options Unfortunately we have been unable to verify if you have consented to Twitter cookies. To view this content you can use the button below to allow Twitter cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

Consider the social media numbers. Since signing for Wolves, each of the club's top 10 most engaged posts have been about Jimenez. The club has been blown away by the response across platforms. Their most engaged Instagram post anyone can remember.

And that is just social media. Out in the real world, Jimenez shirts are everywhere. Not Wolves shirts, Jimenez shirts. For the pre-season friendly against Real Sociedad, where his name was chanted even in his absence, there were Mexico tops - home and away.

Inside the club shop, the Jimenez jersey is outselling last year's most popular player by more than 250 per cent. You probably need to go back to Steve Bull to find a figure so beloved by the supporters but the shirts did not have names on the back in those days.

None of which should come as much of a surprise. Jimenez's name has been sung regularly by supporters in recent seasons and it had little to do with the hope that he would come back. He, along with others, had come to symbolise what had been lost.

It was a lament to Wolves' decline, sometimes accompanied by another chant aimed at owners Fosun. "You sold the team, now sell the club." But when Fulham visited Molineux in the final home fixture of last season, the tone became more celebratory.

It was only after that game that Jimenez revealed to a local journalist that there had been talks over a deal to bring him home. The giddiness that greeted that revelation helped make it happen and sustained supporters in the wake of a miserable relegation.

If all this still seems a bit much for a player who scored 40 Premier League goals for Wolves, the context is key. Jimenez was the club's top scorer as the club finished in the top seven in consecutive campaigns for the first time since Stan Cullis was in charge.

Image: Raul Jimenez's Premier League goal map during his career in England

You have to go back to 1989 to find a Wolves player who has beaten Jimenez's 27 goals in the 2019/20 season. That was Bull, the folk hero of all folk heroes, in the third tier. To find a player doing it in the top flight you are going back to 'King' John Richards in 1973.

Jimenez's 40 goals are more than anyone else has scored for Wolves in the Premier League era. It is 57 in all competitions and those other competitions are all part of the story. He scored at Wembley, not just away to Tottenham, but in an FA Cup semi-final.

More than that, he is the club's top scorer in a single European campaign. That is about the memories as much as the numbers for the fans who travelled. Two goals away to Crusaders in Northern Ireland. Two goals away to Pyunik Yerevan in Armenia.

Jimenez scored home and away against Torino, a trip that fans talk about to this day. He scored home and away against Slovan Bratislava. He scored in the torrential rain in Braga, another adventure still sung about by Wolves supporters. This stuff matters.

Image: Raul Jimenez celebrates scoring for Wolves against Man Utd in the FA Cup in 2019

It was later that year that Jimenez suffered a fractured skull in a collision with David Luiz away to Arsenal. The silence in the stadium was eerie enough during that period of the pandemic. That day it took on a more ominous tone. A sickening blow in every sense.

The road back was long and arduous, the scars mental and physical. Jimenez arguably never did recapture his best form in a Wolves shirt. He is yet to score a headed goal for the club since. That could soon become another cathartic Molineux moment to relish.

But if the injury hampered his performances on the pitch, it only solidified the bond with the club off it. Jimenez and his family have been open about how much the support that they received meant to them. The emotions of that experience have led them back here.

Image: Wolves favourite Raul Jimenez is back at Molineux after three years away

And this is a family move. Daniela, Jimenez's wife and mother to his two children, has long embraced the city, endearing herself with her efforts to repeat the 'Wolves Ay We' mantra. The pair even did the gender reveal of their second child on the Molineux pitch.

That first exit, after Jimenez had fallen out of the first-team line-up under Julen Lopetegui, never did feel like a satisfactory ending for such a hero. He was crying that day against Everton in May 2023, saying his goodbyes after being an unused substitute.

This is a chance to correct that and to underline Jimenez's status as a figure woven into the emotional architecture of the club. That Diogo Jota, his old strike partner, is no longer with us only adds poignancy. All parties are determined to cherish this reunion.

Image: Raul Jimenez is Wolves' top Premier League goalscorer from his first stint

Can he still deliver? There will be optimism based on a World Cup in which he found the net three times in four games. Jimenez looked sharp enough this summer to suggest that he is still close enough to his best to cope with the demands of the Championship.

Jimenez is the bookmakers' favourite to be the competition's top scorer. So reliable from the spot - he has scored more Premier League penalties than anyone else with a 100 per cent record - he is surely a safe bet for at least 20 goals this season if he can stay fit.

Whether he will receive the service required to fire Wolves back up is another matter. Under new coach Cesar Peixoto, there is still uncertainty over the makeup of the squad and the ability to implement a shift in style. Success is far from guaranteed.

But, in a way, all of that is to miss the point. Bull himself spent 10 long years playing for Wolves in the second tier without achieving the promotion that his efforts deserved. He still garnished his legend during that decade, plundering goals and making memories.

Bull stayed. Jimenez has returned.

And Wolves have their No 9 back.

Sports.title: Bethell to miss Pakistan Test series as Pope recalled
Sports.content:
Jacob Bethell will miss the entirety of England's upcoming Test series against Pakistan, while Ollie Pope and Brydon Carse have been named in the 16-man squad.

England are preparing to return to action following their series defeat to New Zealand and the departures of head coach Brendon McCullum and captain Ben Stokes.

Joe Root, reinstalled as skipper following Stokes' international retirement, will lead a team seeking to turn the page on a difficult spell on and off the field.

England's new head coach Stephen Fleming will not take charge until after the three-match series, which begins at Headingley on August 19, live on Sky Sports Cricket.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England have made multiple changes to their side following the departure of Ben Stokes

Bethell sustained a knee injury during England's ODI series against India in July, causing him to miss The Hundred.

He will remain sidelined for the Pakistan series, with Essex wicketkeeper Jordan Cox replacing him at No 3, having made his Test debut earlier this summer.

Pope, formerly vice-captain under Stokes, and Carse return to the Test squad for the first time since England's dismal Ashes tour of Australia last winter.

Surrey wicketkeeper-batter Pope was dropped following England's third Ashes Test against Australia after he averaged 20.83 runs across three Tests.

Carse returns after he was forced to withdraw from this year's IPL after sustaining a hand injury.

England men's national selector Marcus North explained Harry Brook was also due to stay as Root's vice-captain and hailed his leadership qualities as "incredibly important".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook is due to remain as Joe Root's vice-captain for the upcoming series

North added England had identified Sam Curran as a player who could fill the gap left by Ben Stokes, and that he would have been selected for the squad had he been fit to play.

Dan Lawrence has also been recalled to the side two years after his last Test appearance and is expected to bat at No 6.

"Lawrence returns following an exceptional season so far with Surrey and we believe he has the right level of experience, maturity and skill to complement our middle order," North said.

On the inclusion of Cox, North added that it was a "massive opportunity" for the Essex wicketkeeper-batter.

Image: Jordan Cox has been recalled to the England men's Test squad

"This is a guy that's put in consistent performances at domestic level. In his first one or two seasons at Kent, he was opening the batting in the County Championship," he said.

"We wouldn't be putting this guy at three if we didn't feel he was capable of fulfilling that role. He's got plenty of character about him. He's a huge competitor, and is quietly confident. We're looking at it with quite an excitement of how Jordan takes on that opportunity."

Fleming played key role in squad selection

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New England Test coach Stephen Fleming will not take charge until after the three-match Test series

North confirmed that incumbent head coach England coach Fleming was heavily involved in the discussions as selectors attempted to ensure their philosophies were aligned moving into the future.

"As far as the dynamics of selection, it stayed consistent in terms of our system and process that we go through in terms of the wider people that influence that; Troy Cooley, David Court, Ed Barney, myself, Keesy [Rob Key], the captain, the coach," North said.

"So, there's lots of information that gets provided as part of the process. None of that's changed.

"Stephen Fleming was involved. From the moment he was appointed, he was someone that I rang and had very lengthy conversations with.

"We've got to make sure that our selection and our philosophies and thoughts around that are absolutely aligned with Stephen's. It would make no sense for us to move forward through this series and have that be contradicted to where Stephen sees us as a team moving forward."

Sports.title: McKenna wants to unify at 160lbs, and then fight at heavyweight!
Sports.content:
Aaron McKenna is not short of ambition. The Irish middleweight fights for the world title this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

But his plans do not finish with Etinosa Oliha and the IBF belt this weekend. He wants to "clean up" the division, go undisputed and eventually finish his career as a heavyweight.

It sounds preposterous for an albeit tall, but fairly scrawny 160-pounder. McKenna, though he says it with a smile, sounds serious that this is his long-time vision.

"That's something we talked about a lot, finishing up at heavyweight. I'm six foot three now and I have a very long reach as well. My body's the type of body that could fill out easily enough as well weight-wise," McKenna told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna and Etinosa Oliha both refuse to back down as they face off ahead of their IBF middleweight title fight in Dublin on Saturday

"Once I'm done at 160lbs, take over 168 and then 175. But by the time I finish out, I plan to have at least one fight at heavyweight.

"In the heavyweight division now, sometimes it just takes good footwork and boxing to beat them. It's different from the heavyweights back in the day."

McKenna, it's safe to say, has an eerie confidence in himself. His first task is to become a world champion against a dangerous opponent on Saturday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna talks up his IBF world middleweight title fight in Dublin where he takes on Etinosa Oliha. Ahead of the bout live on Sky Sports, Andy Scott talks to the Irishman

"He's a very good fighter, 22-0, strong, he'll be game and any man that's fighting for world titles is going to be giving it their all," McKenna said of Oliha. "I know what I have to do.

"I'm more than ready for it," he added. "It doesn't matter what he brings, whether he comes forward, whether he goes back, I'm ready for everything. I've trained for every style possible my whole life. Whatever he brings, I'm just focused on what I'm doing and what I'm going to do in there."

This, he insists, is the start of a charge through the middleweight division. He wants to take on the other champions. Carlos Adames, the WBC titlist and Denzel Bentley, the new WBO belt-holder, will be in his sights.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of his IBF world middleweight title fight against Etinosa Oliha, Aaron McKenna claims he's the best middleweight in the world

"The middleweight division, it's been dying for years now. The last two big fighters in it were Canelo and GGG [Gennady Golovkin], so I kind of want to bring big-time boxing in the middleweight division and bring it back to life," McKenna declared.

"I've done a lot of sparring with [Adames] back in Robert Garcia's gym back in 2019. I was 19 at the time and he was mid-20s. I had no problem with him.

"He doesn't like my style of fighting. When you put it on him, he kind of doesn't like that sort of stuff.

"[Bentley] would be another good fight. He's a world champion now, so if he wants to take the fight, I'd definitely take it because the name of the game is to unify, become the best in the division.

"But all I'm focused on right now is this Saturday. I have a job to do with Oliha and that's becoming world champion and I will become world champion."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna talks about his unlikely friendship with Kendrick Lamar after meeting at a training session with his brother

What could be next?

McKenna's manager Mike Borao told Sky Sports: "Obviously the focus right now is squarely on this Saturday for Aaron McKenna - he has to get past Etinosa Oliha first before anyone starts mapping out the future.

"That said, Denzel Bentley is a very intriguing possibility. Aaron is the type of fighter who goes out there and delivers for the fans, and few things light up a boxing crowd quite like a proper Ireland vs UK showdown.

"Bentley does have a tough mandatory in Yoenli Hernandez waiting in the wings, though, so it will be interesting to see how things develop.

"In any event, Aaron McKenna has a very exciting future with endless possibilities on Zuffa Boxing."

Sports.title: 'Relieved, excited, and energised!' - Parker's plans revealed after drug ban lifted
Sports.content:
Joseph Parker is 'relieved' after a ban was lifted for a failed drug test and he will return to the ring this year, says manager David Higgins.

The New Zealander returned traces of cocaine in a UK Anti-Doping test on the day of his defeat by Fabio Wardley in October, but Parker denied taking any banned substances and the British Boxing Board of Control confirmed the suspension has been lifted.

Parker's manager Higgins is planning the next career move for the former WBO world heavyweight champion, who could fight twice before the end of 2026.

Image: Joseph Parker has started preparing for his next fight

"A combination of relieved, excited, and energised," said Higgins when asked about Parker's current mindset.

"Joseph is champing at the bit to get back into the ring. He was up early to go for a run this morning.

That 11th-round stoppage loss inflicted by Wardley stopped Parker's charge towards another world title, but Higgins is 'supremely confident' that the Kiwi can become champion again.

Sports.title: Salah joins Turkish side Trabzonspor
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah has joined Turkish Super Lig side Trabzonspor on a free transfer.

Salah has signed a two-year deal following his exit from Liverpool at the end of last season after mutually agreeing to terminate his contract a year early.

The decision ended a nine-year spell at Anfield, cutting short the terms he had agreed in April 2025, after a difficult season that saw him dropped and publicly fall out with then-Liverpool head coach Arne Slot.

One of Liverpool's greatest players, Salah lifted seven major trophies during his time on Merseyside and left as the club's third-highest goalscorer, netting 257 in 442 games.

The 34-year-old has long been a target for clubs in Saudi Arabia, and that appeared to be Salah's most likely destination when he delivered a bombshell interview after being dropped at Leeds last season. It was less than three years ago that Liverpool rejected a £150m offer from Saudi club Al Ittihad for Salah.

Why has Salah picked Trabzonspor?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol discusses why Mohamed Salah has decided to move to Trabzonspor from Liverpool and why the Turkish club ticked lots of boxes for the forward.

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"The deal makes financial sense for him. There are reports in Turkey that he will be paid around £15m a year. The tax environment in Turkey is very favourable to professional footballers as well and he's going to play in a league that has a lot of big games and passionate supporters.

"He's also got the prospect of playing European competition. There's a good chance Trabzonspor will be playing in the Europa League next season.

"It ticks a lot of boxes for him. He had lots of other options as well."

Carragher questions Salah move

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher:

"I never believed he was going to go to Saudi, because number one, he's too good for that. I think he can be playing in Serie A. Turkey for me feels a level too low.

"I was convinced he'd end up at AC Milan or Juventus or somewhere like that; maybe his wages were a problem. Looking at him, I don't know him; I have never spoken to him.

Image: Salah's numbers through the years

"But he's like Ronaldo, he's so driven, his numbers mean so much to him. I thought, he can still do this in Turkey by the way, but I thought he'd want to play at a real prestigious club.

"Obviously his wage demands have put a few people off but I thought he might almost curb those demands a little bit to almost get a better club.

"To go to an AC Milan or Juventus or whoever it may be, play at the San Siro, still playing in big games, still playing in Europe. Turkey just feels like... I just think he's better than that."

Sports.title: Joe Ward: The unluckiest man in Irish boxing
Sports.content:
Joe Ward had the world at his feet. He was an amateur boxing sensation, he had a golden future laid out before him. Until disaster struck, over and over again.

In 2011 Ward made history, becoming the youngest Irish boxer to win a gold medal at the senior European Championships.

Even at that early stage hype was building for what Ward could accomplish at the London Olympics. But at the 2012 qualification event, tucked away in Trabzon in Turkey, the teenage Ward lost a contentious decision to the host nation boxer.
