"My main goal was always to get to the Olympics in London. Trabzon just wasn't to be, as you know. It felt like we won the fight and we just didn't get the decision," Ward told Sky Sports.

He regrouped and made the 2016 Olympics his target. He reached the Rio Games, only to crash out at the first stage as the referee gave him two baffling points deductions, tipping the three-round amateur bout in his opponent's favour.

"It was one of these things that was out of my control," Ward reflected. "I picked up two public warnings, where I was still winning on the scorecards but because of the warnings I was beaten on a 3-2 split decision. Definitely at that time I was very disheartened.

"I was kind of saying to myself: 'Am I ever going to get that little bit of luck?' But again after a few weeks you just regroup and go back to the gym."

Image: Ward was a superstar of Irish amateur boxing

He won three European golds in all and a cluster of World Championship medals.

"It's not an accident to be consistently winning," he said. "You have to have something a little bit special about you. I believe so."

But an Olympic medal could have taken put him on a completely different trajectory. That was something he was denied.

"I kind of always focus on the future," he reflected. "Sometimes you can overthink about what's gone. It's not going to change anything.

"I've always loved boxing and loved being around it and it's something that gave me huge opportunities in my life, to travel the world and meet so many great people. For me I just don't think there's anything else.

"It's something that I love doing."

Eventually, in 2019, he turned professional. He had his first pro fight at Madison Square Garden in New York, it was all set up for him. Then painful disaster struck.

In the second round his knee dislocated and collapsed beneath him. His debut could scarcely have been gone worse.

"You kind of question it sometimes," Ward said. "It could have happened somewhere else but I believe everything happens for a reason. It was out of my control. It was one of these freak accidents that happen. Obviously it was devastating when it happened, I was very upset.

"Mentally you don't want to leave the game, you always want to be involved. Sometimes injuries can stop that from happening, I was hoping that that my knee wasn't going to stop me continuing chasing my goals and my career. It was good that everything worked out well with the operation and they said there were no more issues."

The business of boxing can be unforgiving. Opportunities dried up, but Ward stayed patient, fought on and now on Saturday, live on Sky Sports, he takes on hard-punching, undefeated light-heavyweight contender Artjom Kasparian in Dublin.

Image: Ward fights Artjom Kasparian on Saturday live on Sky Sports

"There's no point getting in there to take easy fights," he said. "It's an opportunity to step up and fight decent fighters and move on and challenge myself to see how far I can really take it. I really believe in myself, I can go all the way.

"That's the key, just getting the opportunity, getting the right fights at the right time. It felt like that never happened over the last couple of years."

He believes all that misfortune, the bad luck that has shrouded his talent, will now help him.

"Things will change, you will get a bit of luck along the way," Ward said. "That makes you a stronger person. I feel like that will give you the extra edge then when something happens in a fight or a moment where you just need something different. That will always flash back - look, I've been through it all and now I can fight through this.

"The most important thing as a fighter is to still believe in yourself, still stay focused, still keep in the gym, keep learning. Doors will open for you, opportunities will come.

"I've had a lot of ups and downs in my career but looking back I'm grateful for opportunities and grateful for what I've achieved. I just stuck at it and here I am still going strong, still believe in myself, believe I'm probably the best I've ever been physically, mentally. So I'm excited."

Watch Joe Ward vs Artjom Kasparian this Saturday live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: Uefa planning to check if Infantino tried to sell stakes in World Cup on cheap
Sports.content:
Uefa is planning to commission an independent valuation of Fifa’s World Cup sale plans after concerns that Gianni Infantino agreed to sell the tournament’s future profits to a private equity firm at below the market rate.

The European governing body is unmoved by the written apology issued by Infantino to Fifa’s 211 member associations on Tuesday after crisis talks in Morocco. It will continue to push for his removal, with its tactics including further scrutiny of a proposal the president belatedly conceded was “a mistake.”

The Fifa Forward Enterprise plan that was abandoned after four days last week involved a 21% stake being sold to Thrive Capital for $4.2bn. The US private equity firm is led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Uefa played a key role in Fifa’s U-turn, which was triggered by all 55 member associations threatening last week to boycott the World Cup and other tournaments, and is now seeking to establish how the $20bn valuation of Fifa’s commercial assets was worked out.

Uefa has spoken to several market analysts seeking opinions regarding an independent valuation and a formal study is likely to follow once the storm surrounding Infantino’s immediate future has passed.

Last week, the Fifa sales deck circulated details that did not contain any information of the valuation process or any evidence of a competitive tender. “We need to find out if they were selling the World Cup at a knockdown price,” a source with knowledge of Uefa’s plans said. “How did they get to $20bn? Was it a robust process?”

Fifa’s revenues for the four-year cycle that culminated in this summer’s World Cup were $15bn, leading the market analysts to suggest that $20bn was a low valuation, particularly as the proposal did not appear to include any provisions to prevent expansion and the creation of new tournaments.

View image in fullscreen The US private equity firm that was interested in acquiring a stake in the World Cup plans is led by Joshua Kushner (right), the brother of Jared Kushner, Donald Trump’s son-in-law. Photograph: TheStewartofNY/GC Images

“The World Cup is the only genuinely global mass entertainment event so an increase of $5bn on current revenues seems low to me,” the source said. “This looks like a low-ball offer. The obvious financial upside of further expansion that the investors would demand – more teams, more regular World Cups, more Club World Cups – is not priced in.”

Uefa has also called for a thorough review of Fifa’s governance, as well as threatening them with legal action. Fifa is attempting to put on a united front despite scathing internal criticisms of the sell-off plan from leading figures including the secretary general, Mattias Grafström, the chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, and Arsène Wenger, head of football development.

Infantino appeared alongside Grafström at a Women’s Africa Cup of Nations group game between Malawi and Zambia in Morocco on Wednesday after attending crisis talks in Rabat. That was followed by Fifa issuing a statement saying the president retained the “full support” of the organisation.

Such apparent support indicates there will be no further dissent from within Fifa and the push for change will have to come from outside the organisation.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: How to fix Fifa: what can be done to salvage football’s beleaguered governing body?
Sports.content:
1) Split the governing body up

How can an organisation that runs the biggest sporting event in the world also be the one that sets the rules for the entire game? We saw the reality of such a conflict at the recent World Cup as Fifa ran roughshod over its rulebook – be it over the length of suspensions or the duration of half-time – in an attempt to generate more attention for its competition. One person with extensive knowledge of the inside workings of Fifa puts it like this: “They have shown that they will bend the rules to make them more money. This is a big conflict of interest. Not only should the commercial and the regulatory parts of Fifa be separated, but so should the development part and possibly one or two others as well.”

According to Miguel Maduro, a former chair of Fifa’s governance committee and now one of the leading critics of the organisation, the creation of different corporate entities – even if they ultimately came under its umbrella – would allow for different priorities to take hold. “There would have to be a Chinese wall between these entities and they would have to have different incentives,” he says. “Those who are seeking to maximise commercial income should not be dependent on the regulatory rules and those working on the regulatory side should not be influenced by commercial considerations.”

One insider notes that Gianni Infantino’s aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme would have created such a separation “but for completely the wrong reasons”.

2) Introduce external regulation

The least sexy word in sport might be necessary if a new Fifa – answerable to nobody bar the courts – is to be expected to follow its new rules. “Change needs to be imposed from the outside. It won’t happen from the inside,” says Maduro. He shares the belief with other critics that it would be necessary to create a new equivalent to Wada, the global anti-doping body. It would hold sporting organisations to account on rules related to governance.

“There’s so much money swirling around in football it could easily be funded,” says one Fifa-watcher. The question is under whose auspices the new body would be created. “One way is to do something at the level of the EU,” Maduro says. “Other countries could join, perhaps the UK for example, and that could then evolve into a world sports agency that would exist to review ethical issues and compliance of the sports associations.”

In this context it is perhaps worth noting that Uefa, which is leading the protests against Infantino’s FFE plan, has in recent years been moving closer to Brussels. Meanwhile another body, the European Leagues, has called on the EU’s executive, the European Commission, to intervene over another Infantino plan: to expand the World Cup from 48 to 64 teams. The commission, it said, “should take the necessary action to protect fair competition and ensure compliance with the principles already set out by the court of justice of the EU”.

3) Defang the president

As has been proven by the FFE affair, where the whole scheme was apparently devised without the knowledge of anyone outside Infantino’s office, Fifa’s president has too much power. “The president was not supposed to control the administration, but then he began to control the administration,” Maduro says. “Then the Fifa council was supposed to control the president and be involved in the real big decisions outside the congress, and they weren’t. At the political level itself you need checks and balances.”

One suggestion on limiting executive power would be to remove the president’s power to determine funding. The governance expert Mark Pieth has an alternative proposal, one he says was once mooted by the president of Uefa, Aleksander Ceferin. It would see the heads of Fifa’s six continental confederations taking turns at being president.

“It’s not an outrageous idea,” Pieth says. “I am Swiss and it happens in my country. Seven ministers take turns being the president, but their tenure lasts one year and it’s clear who the next president is because they go around in order. The effect is nobody gets really powerful. Then you ask yourself, well, why would a Fifa president need power anyway? He’s there to organise matters.”

View image in fullscreen Uefa’s Aleksander Ceferin (left) once floated a plan for heads of Fifa’s six continental confederations to take turns at being president. Photograph: Fernando Calistro/AP

4) Greater transparency

For campaigners looking to hold Fifa to account over the world body’s existing commitments, such as human rights, a lack of transparency over decision-making and the existing appeals process are longstanding frustrations.

Equally, what Fifa does with the money it generates and distributes to its member associations can be opaque. Nick McGeehan, the director and co-founder of the not-for-profit Fair Square, has frequently come up against the limits of transparency within Fifa. “Where are the audited accounts?” he asks.

“Fifa have a development budget that is equal to many big development agencies, but not only is there no needs analysis in terms of how that money is distributed but there is literally no evidence of any audits. Go on their website and you can find all sorts of data about what money is spent, but if you actually wanted to verify what that money is being spent on, it’s impossible.”

McGeehan notes that greater transparency would also involve engaging more with the media. “It seems like Infantino only calls a press conference once every four years,” he says. “It shows an authoritarian state-style distrust of the media and a concomitant lack of transparency.”

5) Rethink development

“Fifa is a not-for-profit organisation – the money it makes is reinvested in football.” This phrase has become something of a mantra under Infantino and following the $15bn (£11.2bn) generated by this year’s World Cup, each member nation can expect to receive $8m between 2027 and 2030. But not only is there a lack of scrutiny over how the money is spent, the nature of the distribution itself is questionable.

“It’s an issue that one country, one vote is combined with giving everyone the same amount of money,” says the Fifa-watcher. “The money is distributed in proportion to votes, which is completely wrong because Montserrat and Gibraltar have very different needs to Nigeria or India. It’s amazing that he didn’t look to even try and tweak that.”

With money neither distributed according to need nor determined by strategic goals to grow participation in the game, Fifa is undermining its own aims, the critic says. “If Fifa were to be judged on results, then football is more Eurocentric now than it was 20 years ago. You can expand the World Cup, that’s easy. They claim it’s development but if you get into the nitty-gritty it can be a negative. Associations spend all their money on the men’s national team, on a European coach, and there’s nothing spent on the grassroots or technical development.”

View image in fullscreen The recent World Cup generated $15bn but there is a lack of scrutiny over how the money gets spent. Photograph: Hannah McKay/Reuters

6) Switch the electorate

The steady funnel of funds shared with associations big and small has kept Infantino popular with his electorate, the heads of his 211 member associations. A change in who gets a say in Fifa’s decisions might be another way to achieve more effective governance.

“When I am at a Fifa meeting and I look around the table, I see very few people who have direct experience of either playing the game, or being a coach or an executive at a club,” says one senior football figure. “I see very few people who actually understand the day-to-day of football.”

The overwhelmingly male makeup of the Fifa electorate is another fact at glaring odds with the real world, while supporters are, as ever, not invited to the party. Ashish Prashar, a political consultant who regularly engages with Fifa on the game’s social responsibilities, says: “What we need is confederations to get together and form a new entity to solidify the game with the values that serve the people. The biggest item for that entity must be fan ownership of the game. The World Cup and its surrounding events should involve the public in its decision making whether that’s fan groups, fan ambassadors or elections for fans.”

For Maduro, a change in the electorate could then unlock further progress. “Currently you have voting syndicates at Fifa, which creates a huge degree of voting control,” he says. “You need to force new mechanisms of representation, and be creative in finding solutions to bring in people that have so far been absent. If you create a diverse electorate that, by itself, will create a mechanism of checks and balances that can help to lead to better decision-making in the interests of football and all its stakeholders.”

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Barcelona keen on Rodri as Real Madrid talks with Manchester City star stall
Sports.content:
Barcelona are considering whether to challenge Real Madrid’s attempt to sign Rodri from Manchester City, but have been frustrated in their efforts to persuade Atlético Madrid to sell Julián Alvarez.

While City have not given up hope that Spain’s World Cup-winning captain will sign a new contract after he entered the final year of his deal, they are thought to be willing to allow him to leave for about £60m. Despite weeks of talks with Rodri and his representatives, Real have yet to reach an agreement and Barcelona are hoping to take advantage.

Barça have registered an interest in signing the 30-year-old, who won the Golden Ball for the World Cup’s best player, after their midfielder Frenkie de Jong suffered a knee injury that is expected to rule him out for several months.

Real – who have agreed a club record fee of £115m for RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande – are also in negotiations with Vinícius Júnior over a lucrative contract extension to ward off interest from Arsenal. They may have to offload players first if they are to sign Rodri as well. Aurélien Tchouaméni and Eduardo Camavinga are possible departures, with Manchester United having been linked with the France midfielders.

Rodri has had minor surgery on his back and will miss most of City’s pre-season programme. They have signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and remain in negotiations with Lille over a deal for the 18-year-old Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

After Robert Lewandowski’s departure, Barcelona have targeted Alvarez all summer, but Atlético continue to insist the Argentina striker is not for sale at any price. Barça’s sporting director, Deco, was in the Spanish capital to meet Alvarez’s representatives on Wednesday. All eyes will be on whether the 26-year-old former City forward will return to pre-season training on Monday or attempt to force through a transfer. Arsenal also retain an interest in him.

Ferran Torres – who scored the winning goal for Spain in the World Cup final against Argentina – has entered the final year of his contract at Barcelona and said he is waiting for them to begin talks over extending his deal. “All I know is that I have to be in training for Barcelona on 12 August. Let’s see what happens.” Asked what Barcelona needed to do to keep him, he said: “Show me they want me, come to negotiate.”

Sports.title: ‘Fifa Super League’: Infantino discussed having governing body’s name on European breakaway
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino held talks about rebranding the ill-fated European breakaway competition the “Fifa Super League”, with negotiations going as far as the term sheet for an agreement that would have changed the face of European football.

The term sheet, whose full contents can be revealed for the first time, is dated October 2020 and proposes renaming any new competition under Fifa’s branding. It outlines the extent to which Infantino’s administration were implicated in a scheme that caused widespread revulsion among fans and excluded clubs in April 2021. It also reveals that Fifa was prepared to sideline its member associations in pushing plans to cut back the number of international windows and outlines how global football’s governing body would have been given special governance and political rights with a “golden share”.

In a week when football is reeling from the fallout after Infantino scrapped his plan to sell chunks of the World Cup to private investors, the document shows Fifa’s leadership was deeply involved in another attempt to put the sport’s major competitions under corporate control. It sets out a partnership of at least 12 years between Fifa and the Super League and proposes a joint venture that would have run its commercial operations.

The document also proposes that an iteration of Fifa’s expanded Club World Cup, referred to as the “global club competition”, would be held annually over an enshrined three-week period and tied directly to the Super League. That tournament would have been a straight knockout competition rather than the group-based version that relaunched in 2025. While the term sheet states that the new tournaments would have to be passed by Fifa’s annual congress and the Fifa council, federations around the world are understood to have been bypassed in the plan’s formation.

Infantino was among a number of Fifa staff involved in the project and is understood to have been fully aware of its progression. The term sheet says the founding clubs “want to agree the terms of a partnership” between the Super League and Fifa, leading to the creation of the two competitions. It follows an initial proposal to Fifa by the breakaway clubs, also seen by the Guardian, that sketches the framework for a potential agreement. While non-binding, a term sheet is generally the precursor to a definitive contract and suggests discussions between Fifa and the Super League’s creators were nearing a conclusion at the time.

It is unclear whether Infantino and Fifa progressed their role in the project beyond the term-sheet stage. After a version of the scheme was infamously launched without Fifa’s direct involvement in April 2021, ultimately scrapped following large-scale protests, Infantino addressed Uefa’s congress in Montreux saying his organisation could “only strongly disapprove the creation of the Super League”. Multiple sources have stated that an earlier conversation with the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, convened by a third party, hastened Fifa’s president distancing himself from the new venture. Infantino is understood to have told associates afterwards that he had no wish to work against football’s institutions.

Yet the evidence of Fifa’s outline agreement with the Super League, coupled with Infantino’s disastrous Football Forward Enterprise scheme, casts doubt on that assertion and suggests multiple attempts to reshape the game without consulting its most important stakeholders. The league would have contained 15 permanent members and five clubs qualifying from existing competitions. It also commits to creating a women’s equivalent, using the same clubs, by an unspecified date. The term sheet refers to Fifa under the name “WO1”, which is also the name used in the British army for a high-ranking officer.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino later changed tack in relation to a European breakaway. Photograph: Louisa Gouliamaki/Reuters

In a section outlining the agreement’s key components, it says the Super League “is open to discuss naming the competition WO1 SL”. It also confirms Fifa would be “granted a preferred equity stake in the Super League”, which would give it decision-making capability on format changes, calendar alterations, distribution of solidarity money and the appointment of a chief executive for the competition.

Senior figures within European football are understood to have been shocked by the plan to drastically shrink the number of international windows, squeezing them into two fortnight-long spaces each year. Member associations, many of whom are being courted for support by Infantino as he battles to save his tenure this week, may have lost the commercial opportunities available from added visibility for their national teams and found themselves at the behest of a privately run club competition.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A separate point in the earlier proposal also notes “reduction of leagues” as a point for discussion. The term sheet states that “a new international match calendar” devised by Fifa, the Super League and “other relevant stakeholders” would be reviewed and implemented with Fifa’s agreement.

Clubs participating in the Super League would have been required to join the World Football Club Association (WFCA), which was a short-lived representative body launched by the Real Madrid president, Florentino Pérez, in 2019. Real were key drivers of the Super League scheme and only closed the door on the project when announcing an agreement with Uefa in February this year.

Fifa’s close proximity to the Super League proposal adds to the growing number of privately backed ventures brought to the table by Infantino during his 10-year reign. In 2018 he pressed the case for a $25bn offer from SoftBank, the Japanese institution, to create an expanded Club World Cup and global Nations League. Close allies within Fifa are understood to have cautioned him against the plan, which failed to gain support after opposition from Europe.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah to earn upwards of £14.5m per season in two-year Trabzonspor deal
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah has signed a two-year deal with Trabzonsporand the Egypt forward will receive €17m (£14.5m) a season.

The ⁠announcement to ‌the Turkish stock ‌exchange came ​as Trabzonspor fans prepared to head to the club’s stadium for a ceremony to mark the 34-year-old’s former Liverpool player’s signing on a free transfer the day after ⁠Salah arrived in Istanbul in the team’s kit.

Salah will receive a 20% share from products sold ‌under his name, plus conditional bonuses each season.

Salah left Liverpool after nine years, having scored 257 goals in 442 appearances, winning the Premier League twice and the Champions League. His output waned last season and he was left ​on the bench in European games, leading to a public disagreement with Liverpool’s then manager Arne Slot.

Sports.title: Two Iranian female footballers granted Australian citizenship after protest
Sports.content:
Two former Iranian footballers said on Thursday they were proud to have been granted Australian citizenship after being called traitors at home for refusing to sing the national anthem before a game.

Fatemeh Pasandideh and Atefeh Ramezanisadeh were members of a group of seven from Iran’s delegation who asked for Australia’s protection after the protest during the women’s Asian Cup in March.

Their demands for protection were an embarrassment for Iran’s leaders, and were lauded by the US president, Donald Trump, but five changed their minds and returned home. Pasandideh and Ramezanisadeh stayed, however, and were granted Australian citizenship at a ceremony on Wednesday, overseen by the minister for home affairs, Tony Burke.

“Yesterday was a truly special and unforgettable day for me. I feel proud and deeply grateful to become an Australian citizen,” Ramezanisadeh said.

“After everything we’ve been through and all the challenges we faced, this moment means more than words can express,” Pasandideh said.

A week after seeking asylum, the pair were pictured smiling and training with Brisbane Roar, who on Wednesday congratulated them. “What they have been through since February is more than most people deal with in a lifetime,” a spokesperson said.

“To see them arrive at this point is something everyone here at Brisbane Roar is glad to have had a small part in. Queensland is their home now. If they ever want to pull on a training top and come back out with us, the door will always stay open.”

Sports.title: Argentina commemorate win against England at World Cup 2026 with special day
Sports.content:
Argentina’s World Cup semi-final win over England last month is being commemorated by the country’s football association, the AFA, which has established 15 July as National Football Teams Day.

“The date was chosen to commemorate Argentina’s historic victory over England in the World Cup semi-final,” an article on the AFA’s official website stated after a meeting of its executive board on Wednesday. “Lionel Scaloni’s team was trailing the English side by a single goal, but with goals from Enzo Fernández and Lautaro Martínez, they turned the game around, sending the entire nation into a frenzy of celebration.

View image in fullscreen Lautaro Martínez scored the late winner for Argentina in the World Cup semi-final against England. Photograph: VCG/Getty Images

“But the tribute isn’t just for that milestone achieved by the senior national team. The recognition, of course, also extends to each and every one of the national teams [youth, men’s and women’s, futsal, beach soccer, and field football], who train daily at the Lionel Andres Messi training complex with the hope, joy and responsibility of representing Argentina.”

Fifa has opened disciplinary proceedings against the AFA over the displaying of a banner by players at the end of that match proclaiming the Falkland Islands belonged to Argentina.

Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina are also being investigated by Fifa over their involvement in the brawl that followed the 1-0 defeat by Spain in the World Cup final. The team’s assistant coach, Roberto Ayala, is also being investigated in relation to that incident.

Sports.title: One potential breakout star for each Premier League club this season
Sports.content:
Arsenal: Marli Salmon

Dowman is old news by now, so we’re going to look at someone four months older than him. Much like the fish of the same name, Salmon has risen quickly. The defender became the fourth-youngest player to represent Arsenal last season when he came off the bench against Club Brugge in the Champions League in December at the age of just 16 years and 102 days.

Salmon made four appearances for the first team last season, while also featuring 14 times for their Under-21s in Premier League 2. He won an impressive 71.8% of his duels in PL2 (56 of 78); of defenders to contest at least 50 duels, only two players had a better success rate. Salmon – who can play right-back or centre-back – has signed a pre-agreement to commit his future to the club when he turns 17 later this month, and it would not be surprising to see him given more opportunities by Mikel Arteta.

Aston Villa: Brian Madjo

Aston Villa signed Madjo from Metz in January for about £10.5m but were not able to register him. He is available now and has been involved regularly during pre-season. The giant 17-year-old centre-forward’s movement and power are reminiscent of Erling Haaland.

He has caught the eye in Villa’s recent friendlies, scoring four times. Pre-season only counts for so much, of course, but you can only score against what’s in front of you.

Bournemouth: Veljko Milosavljevic

After the departure of Marcos Senesi, Bournemouth have a position in the centre of defence up for grabs and Milosavljevic could be the man to claim it. Milosavljevic joined the club last summer from Red Star Belgrade. Although he didn’t feature prominently, making just seven appearances in all competitions, the 19-year-old is clearly a promising defender.

He made more clearances than any other Bournemouth player on his Premier League debut in September, before going on to make his full international debut for Serbia in October. Marco Rose may want more experience at centre-back, especially given how youthful some of Bournemouth’s other defenders are, but Milosavljevic will hope to take another step forward this season.

Brentford: Antoni Milambo

Milambo had a difficult introduction to English football last season. Signed from Feyenoord for around £21m last year, he suffered a season-ending ACL injury on international duty in October. He was obviously set back but will be confident he can force his way into Keith Andrews’ thinking this term.

He became Feyenoord’s youngest ever player in 2021, when he made his debut as a 16-year-old, but Milambo rose to prominence in 2024-25 as a forward-thinking, box-to-box midfielder who was technically good and could be a threat in attack. No other Eredivisie player under the age of 21 bettered his 14 goal involvements in all competitions that season. He could be a dynamic asset in the very useful midfield Andrews has built.

Brighton: Zadok Yohanna

Yohanna will need a little patience as he’s still quite raw but, if he is given opportunities at Brighton this season, he will catch the eye. The 19-year-old Nigerian has joined from AIK for around £21.5m, a record sale for Swedish football, despite playing just 13 league games for the club. It was enough to convince Brighton, who have been impressed by his direct style and fearless dribbling.

A left-footed winger who plays on the right side of the attack, Yohanna was attempting more dribbles per 90 minutes than any other player in the Allsvenskan this year before his move was confirmed in June. He also tallied the most take-ons driving into the box (six), take-ons in the box (15) and the joint-most take-ons followed by a shot (three), despite playing significantly fewer minutes than many other players. His end product needs work, but he will get bums off seats.

Chelsea: Reggie Watson

Chelsea always have a conveyor belt of young talent waiting for a chance – the issue is many seem to get lost in the crowd. But, after losing Rio Ngumoha to Liverpool a couple of years ago, the club have apparently made a greater effort to keep hold of emerging homegrown talents, and one of those they were especially keen to tie down was Reggie Watson.

A towering defensive midfielder, Watson, 16, has impressive physical attributes but is also tidy on the ball, appears to have good spatial awareness and plays with considerable personality for one so young. It’s easy to see why he’s been tentatively compared with Rodri.

Xabi Alonso has also spoken about being “really impressed” with his impact in pre-season. Given the uncertainty around other midfielders – such as the fitness issues of Roméo Lavia and Dário Essugo – Watson could get minutes this season.

Coventry City: Kai Andrews

With survival being the name of the game for Coventry City season, giving minutes to young players may not be Frank Lampard’s top priority. There is one youngster who could force his way into Lampard’s plans, though: Andrews. The 19-year-old midfielder made 10 appearances for Coventry last season before joining Hibernian on loan.

While Andrews failed to make his mark in Scotland, he ended the campaign on a high as he made his first start for Wales in a friendly against Romania. He acquitted himself well in the match, making nine passes in the final third, the third most of any player, and winning two fouls. Andrews will need to decide whether to stay at Coventry and fight for a place or go out on loan for regular minutes.

Crystal Palace: Joél Drakes-Thomas

Drakes-Thomas became Crystal Palace’s youngest Premier League player last season and will hope to play a more prominent role this campaign. The wideman made his Palace debut in the Conference League when he was just 16 years old and he shone against Finnish side KuPS. He attempted seven crosses during the match, the most of any player, and he created two chances, the joint-most. The appointment of Pierre Sage has signalled the start of a new era at Selhurst Park, and Drakes-Thomas has the ability to be a figurehead of any future success.

Everton: Tyrique George

George looked promising at Chelsea, but his first few months at Everton after initially joining on loan in February were something of a settling-in period, as he started just one game for David Moyes’ side. With a full pre-season under his belt, George could burst into life this season.

Quick, dynamic and eager to run at full-backs, the 20-year-old could be the one to benefit most from Jack Grealish returning to Manchester City after his loan. George has started three of Everton’s four pre-season friendlies in the absence of Iliman Ndiaye, who is reportedly the subject of interest from abroad. With Grealish gone and Dwight McNeil dropping down the pecking order, George has a big opportunity.

Fulham: Farhaan Ali-Wahid

The 19-year-old will be hoping to make his debut for Fulham this season, having already impressed for their Under-21s. He signed his first professional contract with the club last summer and went on to score 10 goals in PL2. The left winger also added seven assists, proving he can create as well as find the net himself.

Only Chelsea’s Shumaira Mheuka (19) and Liverpool’s Kieran Morrison (18) recorded more goal involvements than Ali-Wahid (17) in the PL2 last season, while just 10 players created more chances from open play than his 26. He was nominated for the PL2 Player of the Season award and the new Fulham manager, Álvaro Arbeloa, has been picking him in pre-season.

Hull City: Charlie Hughes

Hughes was Hull’s defensive lynchpin last season. The 22-year-old centre-back started 36 games in the Championship and played every minute of their successful playoff campaign. He has a remarkable willingness to put his body on the line. Last season, he made 1.54 blocks per 90 minutes, the most of any regular player in the Championship. He also made more clearances per 90 minutes (7.62) than any of his teammates (1,000+ mins). Hull may struggle in the Premier League, but Hughes could be a diamond in the rough.

Ipswich Town: Tudor Mendel-Idowu

Mendel-Idowu, who spent most of his youth development at Chelsea before a year at Anderlecht, was snapped up by Ipswich in the summer of 2024, though he is yet to make his first-team debut. The winger is an intelligent fellow; he appeared on a TV show called Child Genius when he was eight years old and went on to become a King’s Scholar at Eton College.

He has not only thrived in academia, but also on the pitch. He recorded 15 goal involvements in 17 PL2 games for the Ipswich’s Under-21s last season (nine goals, six assists); only three players managed more in the league. On top of that, only three players created more chances from open play than his 33, and just two won possession in the final third more than him (21).

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Leeds United: Jayden Lienou

Chances were at a premium last season for young players under Daniel Farke. The youngest player to play for Leeds was 21-year-old Facundo Buonanotte, who had already made his debut for Argentina, and even he only played a fleeting role in the second half of the season.

But Lienou may just be winning Farke’s trust. The 18-year-old defender started all but one of Leeds’ PL2 games last season and won possession 5.4 times per 90 minutes, the second most in the side. He was the only youth-team player to feature in Leeds’ first three pre-season games, and he was called into the senior Wales squad by Craig Bellamy in June, showing he is impressing coaches for both club and country.

Liverpool: Trey Nyoni

With a new manager comes a new opportunity to impress, and Trey Nyoni has taken that chance in pre-season. The midfielder had to be patient after joining Liverpool from Leicester in 2023. Arne Slot gave him limited minutes last season, with Nyoni making 14 appearances in all competitions, only two of which were starts, both in the League Cup. With Andoni Iraola now in the dugout, the 19-year-old has been able to stake his claim and has been Liverpool’s standout midfielder in pre-season.

One of the most impressive aspects to his game is his verticality. Nyoni wants to get the ball forward as often as possible, though he’s not careless in possession. In his three friendlies this summer in the US – against Sunderland, Wrexham and Leeds United – Nyoni attempted 154 passes, completing 141 of them (92%). Just looking at forward passes, he completed an impressive 44 out of 54 (81%). With Curtis Jones potentially leaving, and most of Liverpool’s transfer funds seemingly going on attackers, the path may open up for Nyoni.

Manchester City: Ryan McAidoo

McAidoo has shone in City’s extremely competitive academy. The winger impressed in the PL2 last season, with only Reigan Heskey (15) registering more goal involvements than him (12) for City. McAidoo made his first-team debut last season, and he marked the occasion by scoring the ninth goal in City’s 10-1 drubbing of Exeter City in the FA Cup.

More recently, the 18-year-old caught the eye with his one-v-one ability in City’s pre-season friendly against Inter. He also had the second-most touches in the opposition’s box (13). Enzo Maresca raved about McAidoo’s performance, calling him “the type of winger I love”.

Manchester United: JJ Gabriel

Gabriel is undoubtedly the biggest hope in Manchester United’s academy. He apparently nearly left at the end of the 2024-25 season until senior club figures stepped in and his reputation has only continued to grow since. Then, aged 14, he had already become the youngest player to represent United’s Under-18s, scoring twice on his debut. After turning 15 in October, he was soon involved in first-team training.

Nevertheless, his focus remained the Under-18s, for whom he scored 23 goals – a tally bettered by only one player – in the 2025-26 U18 Premier League campaign, winning the competition’s Player of the Season award.

A skilful attacker who can play out wide or through the middle, Gabriel is brave, expressive and confident. He showed these traits when he came on as a late substitute in United’s pre-season friendly against Atlético Madrid at the weekend.

The record for youngest Premier League player is out of reach, but Gabriel has a good chance of becoming United’s youngest player in the Premier League; that honour currently belongs to Angel Gomes (16 years, 263 days).

Newcastle United: Park Seung-soo

For all the good he did at Newcastle, some supporters think Eddie Howe could have done more to bring young talent through. Now he’s gone and Newcastle are in a transition period, several of their young players will fancy their chances of stepping up. Park, 19, is one of them. The South Korean left-winger was signed last summer and spent the season adapting to English football in PL2. He averaged 4.7 dribble attempts per 90 minutes in that competition and caught the eye with his energetic displays and tidy footwork.

With Anthony Gordon gone, there may well be chances available on the left flank, especially if new signing Bazoumana Touré does not get off to a flying start. Park has impressed in pre-season and a step up to top-flight football might not be far down the line.

Nottingham Forest: Kalum Thompson

Thompson signed for Nottingham Forest from Northern Irish club Linfield last July and, despite being 16 at the time, he went on to spend the majority of 2025-26 playing for the club’s Under-21s. The left winger was the youngest player to feature for Forest Under-21s last season and yet only four players – three of whom are now 20 – tallied more minutes than him (1,090).

The 17-year-old won the club’s scholar of the year prize at the end of the season. A tricky and purposeful player, Thompson’s 4.7 dribble attempts per 90 ranked highly in the PL2 and his six goal involvements were the most of any Forest player.

Sunderland: Nilson Angulo

Although Angulo reportedly cost £15m in January and is already 23 years old, he just about fits into the potential breakout player category. After joining from Anderlecht, Angulo’s impact at Sunderland wasn’t exactly explosive. There were flashes of his flair but he was clearly still pretty raw.

Nevertheless, those first few months gave him time to adapt and, after a fairly encouraging World Cup with Ecuador, he’ll now hope to kick on. He has the ability and he has an athletic build which should help him once his game has been refined a little more.

Sunderland will hope the Angulo of Anderlecht comes to the fore a little more this season. Prior to his move last season, he’d attempted more dribbles (111) than any other player in the Belgian Pro League, while only Christos Tzolis (17) – now at Arsenal – bettered his 11 goal involvements. If he keeps progressing, Angulo will be a very useful weapon for Régis Le Bris.

Tottenham: Lucá Williams-Barnett

Spurs seem to have exciting young talents breaking through every other season, and now it’s Williams-Barnett’s turn to see if he can make his mark. Williams-Barnett started last season playing Under-18s football but quickly broke into first-team contention. He made one senior appearance but featured on the bench semi-regularly throughout the campaign.

He was one of Spurs’ standout players in the PL2 despite only playing 10 games. Williams-Barnett recorded an astounding 1.25 combined goals and assists per 90 in the PL2, ranking him fourth among all players (500+ mins). The 17-year-old attacking midfielder also created 0.8 big chances per 90 last season, again ranking him fourth (500+ mins). He has featured heavily in pre-season, building great momentum which he can hopefully take into the season.

He was scoring and assisting goals for fun with Manchester United and was named the Player of the Season, despite an Arsenal title win.

6 Fernandes will want to follow up his Player of the Season award with another huge campaign at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

Sports.title: Argentina at pains to immortalise England victory which ‘felt like winning World Cup’
Sports.content:
Argentina at pains to immortalise England victory which ‘felt like winning World Cup’

The Argentine Football Association has voted to forever remember the nation's victory over England with a commemorative day.

July 15 will now be 'National Football Teams Day' to mark the 2-1 semi-final win at the World Cup earlier this summer.



3 Messi was instrumental as Argentina beat England in the 2026 World Cup semi-final Credit: Getty

Announcing their new special day, the AFA said: "The date was chosen to commemorate the Albiceleste's great and historic victory over England in the semi-final of the 2026 World Cup.

"The team, led by Lionel Scaloni, were trailing the English side by a single goal but, thanks to goals from Enzo Fernández and Lautaro Martínez, managed to turn the result around and send the whole country into a frenzy, with people flooding the streets in celebration."

There will, however, be no special day to mark Argentina's appearance in the subsequent final - which they lost to Spain without registering a single shot on target.



A number of players face disciplinary actions for disgracing themselves on the world stage with thuggish tantrums at full-time.

'Like winning the World Cup'

Argentina used their victory over England to promote their claim of the Falkland Islands.



Players held a sign which read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas' at full-time, which translates to 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

FIFA has already charged the South Americans with four breaches of conduct with punishment set to follow.



Leandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina and coach Roberto Ayala are facing separate assault charges after attacking Spain players after the final.

Nevertheless, the AFA continues to celebrate the World Cup as if the Albiceleste won it.

"I know that for Argentinians, we won the World Cup the moment we beat England, because that's really what everyone wanted," AFA president Claudio Tapia said during the recent AFA Sponsor Day.

3 Argentina crashed out of the World Cup in disgrace Credit: Getty



Tapia added on Wednesday: "We are proud of our national team's performance, and of the fact that they created that sense of epic invincibility - that nobody could beat us."

We really must stress, again, their subsequent defeat to Spain in the final, which was widely celebrated as a victory for football.

Meanwhile, England legend Stuart Pearce wants the book thrown at Argentina as a result of their behaviour in the latter stages of the World Cup.

Although he doubts FIFA will deliver given their track record over the summer.



"What do you think they are going to do to the Argentinian players?" Pearce asked.

"Bear in mind, they upgraded Jarell Quansah's suspension and a six-game suspension to a Qatari [Assim Madibo].

3 FIFA have launched a probe into Argentina's Falklands banner Credit: Getty

"So, a player, after the game has finished, throwing punches...

"If you set a precedent for banning a player for six games for an accidental tackle, which I think is ludicrous because he wasn't a well-known player.



"Then bans for Ronaldo were quashed..."

Sports.title: Ivan Toney transfer could transform Premier League club into title contenders
Sports.content:
Tottenham could make a serious push for the Premier League title if they signed an elite level goalscorer.

That’s the verdict of talkSPORT hosts Carlton Cole and Adam Catterall when discussing Spurs’ summer so far.



2 De Zerbi is expected to have Tottenham challenging at the other end of the table this season Credit: AFP

The north London club have been the biggest spenders so far, splashing out nearly £250m and they are not done yet.

A total of seven players have joined as the defence and midfield have been overhauled.

Serious surgery is still needed at the top end of the pitch.

Richarlison was their top scorer in all competitions with just 12 goals as they escaped relegation on the final day of the 2025/26 season.



The Brazil forward and Dominic Solanke are their main talismen - but the club have made a habit of losing their top scorers in recent seasons.

Before last season, each of their top scorers from the previous three campaigns have left the club.



These were Harry Kane, Son Heung-Min and Brennan Johnson.

Spurs’ 20 goal strikers?

Catterall and former Chelsea and West Ham striker Cole believe they are an elite marksman away from pushing higher up the table, even to a title challenge.

Catterall said: “It's going in the right direction to behave in a different way in the transfer market. I just look at the top end of the pitch and I think to myself where's the goals coming from in this side?”



Cole added: “They need a 20 goal a season striker. There's not many in the world, is there?

Tottenham signings this summer Sandro Tonali (Newcastle) - £100m

Mateus Fernandes (West Ham) - £85m

Jan Paul van Hecke (Brighton) - £52m

Martin Dubravka - Free

Andy Robertson - Free

Marcos Senesi - Free

Cole Ramsey (Aston Villa) - Undisclosed

“I think that they'd look at bringing Ivan Toney or try to get Harry Kane back. They'll be flying if they bring him back.”

Catterall responded: “If Harry Kane came back into THIS Spurs side I’d move them from top six to a top four with a serious push [for the title].

“Is Dominic Solanke or Richarlison getting you 20 goals a season?”

In reply, Cole added: “Richarlison, no. We’ve seen his body of work. But I still have hope for Solanke if he can stay fit. I like him as a player.



“He’s just never never fit, that’s the problem. If you can get a run of games and get that confidence I think you could be your man because they've got someone there that can put the ball in the back of the net. They’ve got [James] Maddison coming back as well.

“They've got players coming back from injury where they're gonna be looking up and with the recruitment as well if they’ve got it right. It’s been very very good.”

2 Kane's goals fired Bayern to a league and cup double as he scored 61 times for the club last season Credit: Getty

Toney, 30, currently plays in the Saudi Pro League for Al Ahli and has scored 72 goals in 93 games.



Meanwhile, Kane is settled at Bayern Munich where he has won back-to-back Bundesliga titles.

The 33-year-old, who has 146 goals in 147 games for the German club, has one year left on his contract, but is expected to sign an extension.

Who will Spurs sign?

A left-sided player is the main target for Roberto De Zerbi at the moment, with Savinho and Cody Gakpo both linked.

Man City’s Savinho is the most likely incoming and has been a long-term target for Spurs.



City would need a replacement and they themselves have been linked with £70m-rated Pedro Neto of Chelsea.

Links have also surfaced around Nicolas Jackson to the north London club, however they are not expected to make a move.

Sports.title: Djed Spence linked with surprise £35m Premier League transfer this summer
Sports.content:
Liverpool are reportedly interested in making a move for Djed Spence amid their right-back woes.

The Reds have Jeremie Frimpong as their only available senior option for the role, although Calvin Ramsey has featured in pre-season.



2 Spence has emerged as a shock target for Liverpool Credit: Getty

Conor Bradley remains sidelined with a significant knee injury that he suffered in January during a 0-0 draw with Arsenal.

His absence, alongside Frimpong's fitness issues, led to former head coach Arne Slot playing midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai at right-back.

Joe Gomez is also capable of playing in the position, but could miss the start of the season after picking up an injury during pre-season.



Liverpool could soon turn towards Spence, with The Sun reporting their interest in the Tottenham Hotspur man.

The 25-year-old had an impressive World Cup campaign with England as they finished third.



Spence signed a long-term contract with Spurs last summer but, as talkSPORT reported in July, they are open to offers.

A move could cost Liverpool £35million, although other clubs appear to hold stronger interest in the defender.



This includes teams from the Premier League and Italy, including the Milan duo AC and Inter.

Roberto De Zerbi's rebuild

After escaping relegation on the final day of last season, Roberto De Zerbi has been working on a new-look Spurs.

Jan Paul van Hecke has joined from Brighton in a £52m move, while fellow centre-back Marcos Senesi signed for free.

2 Spurs could sell Spence to help fund their rebuild under De Zerbi Credit: AFP



Andy Robertson also joined in a free switch after leaving Liverpool.

Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali have arrived as a new midfield pairing in deals worth £185m combined.

Luka Vuskovic departed for Brighton in a £46m move having never made a senior appearance for Spurs.

Academy graduate Will Lankshear has also left and signed for Championship promotion hopefuls Middlesbrough in a £20m deal.

Spurs look set to earn more funds as they are understood to be in line for a 20 per cent share of a fee for Troy Parrott.



Their former striker is a target for West Ham United, who are pushing hard to sign the Republic of Ireland international.

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle’s replacement confirmed after Arne Slot and Vitor Pereira links
Sports.content:
Al Ahli have announced Marino Pusic as their managerial replacement for Matthias Jaissle, who has joined Newcastle United.

Pusic joins the Saudi Pro League giants on a two-year deal after a spell at Al Jazira in Abu Dhabi.

2 Pusic has replaced Jaissle at Al Ahli Credit: Getty

The Dutch-Croatian coach also worked at Shakhtar Donetsk, where he won the Ukrainian Premier League and two Ukrainian Cups.

Al Ahli have completed a swift appointment following Jaissle's exit to Newcastle as Eddie Howe's successor.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot is understood to have been one of a number of candidates for the job.

Vitor Pereira, formerly of Wolves and Nottingham Forest, was also appreciated by Al Ahli, but it's Pusic who has been given the job.

He has some big shoes to fill as Jaissle won the 2025 Saudi Super Cup and two AFC Champions League Elite titles during his stint.

Al Ahli finished third in the Saudi Pro League last season, five points off champions Al Nassr.

What can Newcastle expect from Jaissle?

Jaissle has arrived at Newcastle during a turbulent summer in which Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have left.

Club captain Bruno Guimaraes is also set to join Premier League rivals Arsenal in a £75million move.

Newcastle have even been tipped to be relegation contenders in the new season.

However, Jaissle's former Al Ahli CEO Yazan Al-Sharif believes he has what it takes to be a success at St. James' Park.

2 Jaissle is tasked with building on Howe's success at Newcastle Credit: Getty

Appearing on talkSPORT Breakfast, he said: "He's a very high-energy coach, who enhances open and clear discussion with the players.

"Most importantly, the dressing room with Matthias Jaissle is going to take another level, for sure.

"About his philosophy and the way his football is played, he mostly plays high pressing and counter-pressing when losing the ball.

Al-Sharif added: "I think he is going to do a lot of tremendous work with Newcastle, having that foundation left by Eddie Howe."

Jaissle looks set to take charge at Newcastle for the first time on Saturday in a pre-season friendly against Valencia.

His Premier League debut follows on August 24 when the Magpies travel to Liverpool.

Sports.title: Arsenal fans are deluded, signing Vinicius Jr is like me asking Rihanna out on a date
Sports.content:
Arsenal fans are deluded, signing Vinicius Jr is like me asking Rihanna out on a date

Arsenal fans have been told they are 'deluded' for thinking they could sign Vinicius Junior - and Gabby Agbonlahor compares it to when he used to DM Rihanna.

talkSPORT understands that Real Madrid are now confident that Vinicius Junior will extend his stay with them rather than depart.



3 Arsenal were ready to make Vinicius Junior their highest paid player Credit: Getty

The Brazilian international was open to a summer departure to Arsenal but fresh talks have been held with a compromise set to be reached.

Real have upped their offer, according to The Athletic's David Ornstein, and that is likely to sway the 26-year-old.

His contract is due to expire next summer, which had given Arsenal hope they could jump in and sign him, with Real unwilling to lose Vinicius for nothing.



Now ex-Aston Villa and England forward Agbonlahor has had his say on the transfer saga.

Speaking on Breakfast with Shebahn Aherne, Agbonlahor said: "Arsenal fans are so deluded.



"The hope was there, but it's like when I was younger and I used to DM Rihanna and ask her if she wanted to come to the Bull Ring in Birmingham.

"That's on level with Arsenal thinking they've got a chance of getting Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid.



"Arsenal only sign players from Real Madrid when they are coming to the end, and they aren't at their best.

"It's Real Madrid. You don't leave Real Madrid unless you are going to get crazy, crazy money.

"I don't see Vini Junior coming to the Premier League, none of the teams are big enough."

3 Agbonlahor revealed something around his past involving Rihanna and compared it to Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius Jr Credit: Getty



Expanding more on Arsenal's attempts, he said: "It was an audacious attempt, to say the least.

"It was always going to be tough. Vinicius Junior leaving Real Madrid to come to Arsenal, it just doesn't sound right.

"Think about Neymar at Barcelona, he's not going to leave Barcelona for Arsenal.

"They were always going to come to an agreement. Real Madrid were never going to let a talent like that go.



"He's worth over £100million easily. Real Madrid are never going to let him go.

"I was just looking at the players there and thinking that if he comes in and starts earning a ridiculous package, then they'll start asking questions."

Aherne then suggested that Agbonlahor would have played for clubs where he earned less.

And he responded: "Yeah, but not to that level.

"They've just won the Premier League, and you've got Saka and Rice thinking they are world-class players themselves."



Alternative

Now that Arsenal appear to have missed out on Vinicius Jr, they will need a new left wing target.

One of the names they've been linked with, who has a lot of interest from Liverpool, is Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman is keen on a switch to Anfield, but the Gunners have been urged to swoop in.

3 Barcola might find himself in the middle of a transfer tug of war Credit: Getty



That is what former West Ham United and Newcastle United star Kevin Nolan thinks.

Speaking on talkSPORT, he said: "In that left-hand side role, or Barcola, if you like.

"They're the ones who I thought would suit more of an Arsenal-type player than Vinicius Jr."

Arsenal's transfer business

After winning the Premier League, Mikel Arteta has completed the signings of Illan Meslier and Christos Tzolis.



They are set to complete the signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United.

The Brazilian international and Toon captain has undergone a medical after a fee of £75million was agreed.

But the fans will want more before they start off against Coventry City, live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Where to watch Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund: Mikel Arteta hints at team news with timeline for player returns
Sports.content:
Where to watch Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund: Mikel Arteta hints at team news with timeline for player returns

Arsenal return to the Emirates for the first time since being crowned Premier League champions.

The Gunners continue their pre-season with the Emirates Cup, welcoming German giants Borussia Dortmund to London.

7 Arteta is preparing his squad for their return to London for pre-season action where he will welcome back his captain Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta's men are just two games into their preparations for the new campaign, taking on Spanish opposition so far.

They thrashed Girona 4-1 in their opening friendly before taking on Real Betis on Wednesday, which they lost 3-1 in Dublin.

“I'm disappointed with the result," Mikel Arteta told arsenal.com. "We are here to win football matches.

“We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I’m very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It's true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that's the learning from today.”

As for Dortmund, they've played four games already this summer, winning two and losing two of their outings.

The Bundesliga side have just returned from Japan, where they came out on top against Tokyo but lost to Cerezo Osaka.

Where to watch the match

This Emirates Cup clash will take place on Sunday, August 9.

Kick-off at the Emirates Stadium is scheduled for 2pm.

This is Arsenal's first match back at home since their 1-0 win over Burnley in May before lifting the Premier League title on the final day of last season as champions at Selhurst Park having beaten Crystal Palace.

7 Arsenal lost their first match of pre-season friendlies when Real Betis beat them 3-1 Credit: Getty

7 Former Arsenal defender Hector Bellerin was among the familiar faces in Dublin Credit: Getty

7 Arsenal fans and players got a reminder of what they were preparing to defend in the coming season at the Aviva Stadium Credit: Getty

Fans will be able to watch the action live on the Gunners' website and app, via their Pre-Season Pass.

Supporters can 

talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will also keep you up to date with all the latest news, scores and reaction during pre-season.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

What is the Emirates Cup?

The first Emirates Cup game was played 19 years ago in 2007.

It is a friendly clash that has been played yearly in various formats to celebrate the partnership with club sponsor Emirates.

When the event was first founded, four teams competed in a group stage, with each team playing two matches each.

7 The Emirates is hosting the Emirates Cup, the glamorous annual pre-season tournament involving Arsenal Credit: Getty

7 Arsenal captain Odegaard is back training after his World Cup exploits and could play against Dortmund Credit: Getty

7 Bellingham is following in brother Jude's footsteps in Germany and could play against Arsenal Credit: Getty

However, more recently, it has changed to a simple one-off tie.

Arsenal have won the Emirates Cup nine times since its creation, aiming to make it to double digits this pre-season.

Last year, the Gunners beat Athletic Bilbao 3-0 thanks to goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz.

What is the current team news?

Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli should both be back to feature for Arsenal after rejoining the squad post-World Cup after playing for Brazil.

Meanwhile, Ecuador's Piero Hincapie, who joined the club in a permanent transfer, Germany international Havertz and Sweden striker Gyokeres will continue to get minutes following their earlier return from the tournament.

A host of other big names are due back soon, too, Arteta confirmed as he attempted to offer a timeline for key names returning.

“It has been ten days away from home," he said in reference to the pre-season tour. "So we’re looking forward to coming back, seeing some players as well."

Mikel Merino, Martin Zubimendi and David Raya all won the World Cup with Spain and were given extra-time to recover, while Eberechi Eze, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka all played for England.

"Martin [Odegaard] will be back and then the English and Spanish internationals will be back soon as well. So, we're going to start to have more and more players at the moment, we still miss a lot of them.”

Jurrien Timber remains a fitness worry in pre-season.

For Dortmund, 20-year-old England U21 international Jobe Bellingham is sure to feature, along with World Cup star Felix Nmecha in midfield.

Ex-Chelsea midfielder Carney Chukwuemeka was substituted with a knock last time out, so he is a doubt.

Sports.title: National League South club suspended and unable to fulfill opening three fixtures
Sports.content:
National League South club Ebbsfleet United have been suspended from the league with their opening three fixtures postponed.

Concerns have been raised about the club’s financial position and they had recently been subject to a winding up petition by HM Revenue and Customs [HMRC].



2 Ebbsfleet play in the National League South - but their opening three games are postponed Credit: Getty

The Fleet, who are managed by former Millwall, Leyton Orient and Gillingham player Josh Wright, have until 5pm on Tuesday, August 18 to provide satisfactory evidence that they can meet their financial obligations for the upcoming season.

The National League’s Compliance and Licensing Committee will review the case on August 19.

As a result, their opening three fixtures against Slough Town, Folkestone Invicta and Chelmsford City have been postponed.



National League statement

In a statement, the league said: “The National League’s Compliance and Licensing Committee convened on 5 August 2026, following recent correspondence and information relevant to the club, to further consider ongoing issues regarding Ebbsfleet United FC and its financial position.

“The club, which competes in the National League South, has previously been found in breach of National League regulations and is under embargo.



“One significant issue is settlement of PAYE liabilities dating back to April 2026, which led to HM Revenue & Customs reportedly issuing a winding-up petition against the club.

“The Committee considered ongoing non-compliance, in particular under Appendix H of the National League Financial Reporting Initiative.



“Appendix D Clause 4.3 of the National League Financial Reporting Initiative relates to a club's ongoing obligations in relation to its financial position. The Committee determined that these obligations are not met to its satisfaction, specifically regarding the club’s ability to meet its financial obligations throughout the 2026/27 Season.

“Following careful consideration, the Committee has taken the decision under applicable regulations to suspend Ebbsfleet United FC, with a review to be undertaken by the Committee on 19 August. As a result of suspension, at this time, the club will not be able to fulfil the opening three fixtures of the coming Season.

“A detailed letter has been issued to the club today, setting out the Committee’s decision. Ebbsfleet United FC has until 5.00pm on Tuesday 18 August to provide satisfactory evidence that its obligations have been and will be met in accordance with applicable regulations.

“The club remains subject to embargo until such time as the Committee is satisfied that relevant matters have been resolved.

2 Ebbsfleet have also been under an embargo since July Credit: Getty



“Opponent clubs for the first three published fixtures have been informed of the decision. Others have also been informed, including the Independent Football Regulator.”

Ebbsfleet statement

Ebbsfleet also released a statement explaining its position in relation to the winding up petition and the suspension from the league.

The statement read: “The club were informed by The National League at 9.31am this morning that, after a committee meeting last night on August 5, they have come to the decision to suspend the club for the first 3 matches of the season.

“The first 3 league matches will be postponed and re-scheduled for a later date.



“Obviously, for our playing group, management , staff and most importantly supporters, this has come as a shock and is extremely upsetting.

“The league wrote to club owners last week in response to the HMRC winding up petition and requested assurances around the debt and other liabilities and asked for a response by midday yesterday ( August 5)

“We had been advised these debts would be satisfied in time and our statement of August 4 outlined that.

“The owner’s letter of response to the league yesterday proposed the HMRC debt would be cleared by the end of August once a full transfer of ownership had taken place and the league in their letter this morning have highlighted that inconsistency in undertakings by the ownership.



“The league’s letter today also identifies their concerns around the club’s budgeting for the coming season and debt position , although that information was presented on July 10 with the club’s budget pack to the league within compliant timelines.

“Vetting and financial checks for the new proposed ownership and takeover have taken place over the last 12 months and were approved by the league on May 1 in writing.

“However, with the recent overturning of the Northfleet Harbourside development, the league have also raised concerns around the club’s financial viability, debt that has been placed into the club and how it is treated.

“The league have provided the owners until 10am on August 19 to rectify its position and demonstrate this to the league.



“Obviously our players, staff and supporters have taken a number of blows in the last week, none of which is within their control or a result of their work or actions, and we ask for understanding and care during this time while the ownership situation is solved.

“Everyone has worked so hard and completed an excellent pre-season and we look forward to this being rectified and demonstrating the results of that hard work throughout the season.”
