Sports.title: Inside Leeds' blueprint to get into Europe: Daniel Farke's brutal pre-season regime borrowed from Jurgen Klopp, how they beat Champions League clubs to sign Harry Wilson and the two new faces they want now
Sports.content:
Leeds United are making a splash this summer – and not just because players had the pleasure of rubbing shoulders with Michael Phelps in the United States last week.

The minority investor was there to watch his team play Liverpool off the park in the second half of a 4-2 friendly win in Chicago, with two training-ground throw-in routines that would not have looked out of place in the NFL matches Soldier Field usually hosts.

Phelps, the greatest Olympian of all time with 23 gold medals, has brought his kids up as Leeds fans and he will be hoping Daniel Farke’s team are ready to progress after a season battling to stay afloat upon their return to the Premier League.

Leeds have had an encouraging summer window so far that saw them win races to sign Harry Wilson on a free transfer and England goalkeeper James Trafford in a club-record £45million deal from Manchester City.

New £34million Bosnia defender Tarik Muharemovic, fresh from having his ankle trodden on by Folarin Balogun at the World Cup, looks a solid buy from Sassuolo to replace Pascal Struijk. And, with a couple more signings – a left back and another attacker are on the list – Leeds could have a squad ready to challenge the top half of the Premier League after finishing 14th last time out.

Some are even mentioning the dreaded ‘E’ word and want to take inspiration from Sunderland and Nottingham Forest, two clubs who managed to get into Europe within three years of promotion back to the top flight, as well as Brighton and Brentford.

Leeds turned on the style in Chicago last week against Liverpool, coming from 2-0 down to win 4-2

Daniel Farke put the squad through a gruelling pre-season. Many days saw two training sessions, with double workouts to condition the body for an arduous campaign ahead

Minority investor Michael Phelps was there to watch his team play Liverpool off the park in Chicago

Farke put the squad through a gruelling pre-season. Many days saw two training sessions, with double workouts to condition the body for an arduous campaign ahead. In the morning, they would be football-focused and, in the afternoon, sessions would be strength-based.

There were two days of fitness tests to start pre-season and the footballs have been out every day but one, with players feeling a difference on the pitch after Farke’s physically demanding routines.

Farke, who asks players to call him ‘boss’ and dislikes the moniker ‘gaffer’, took inspiration from Jurgen Klopp for his workouts that involve a 1km running drill known as the lactate test, which measures how long it takes for lactic acid to build quicker than the body can clear it. The longer, the better – and it exposed who was keeping fit and who had slacked over summer.

When Leeds were promoted 12 months ago, the recruitment team were ahead of the curve in noticing a trend in the Premier League. They knew the game was switching to a more direct style and many of their transfer targets were, for want of a more diplomatic phrase, big brutes. Anton Stach is 6ft 4in, Jaka Bijol and Sebastiaan Bornauw 6ft 3in, Lukas Nmecha and Sean Longstaff 6ft 1in.

This year, they will stick by that policy and 6ft 4in Muharemovic fits into it – but Leeds are keen for a bit of flair, too. Germany winger Julian Brandt was targeted but ended up going to Ajax. Former Fulham man Wilson, then, is the star attraction.

Several clubs, including Champions League-bound Aston Villa, had made a pitch to sign Wilson when it became clear he would follow manager Marco Silva out of the door at Craven Cottage. But he chose Leeds for a number of reasons.

One was the fact Leeds made a push to sign him 12 months earlier, which proved to Wilson that they did not simply want him because he was available for nothing. With the possibility of qualifying for the World Cup with Wales, Wilson did not want the turbulence of moving at that time.

Chairman Paraag Marathe has recently stepped aside from his position at the San Francisco 49ers to focus on his football ventures, including Rangers. He sold the winger a dream on the second of many calls between player and club. Marathe made Wilson feel wanted.

New 6ft 4in, £34m signing Tarik Muharemovic (right) adds to Leeds' land of the giants

Several clubs, including Champions League-bound Aston Villa, had made a pitch to sign Harry Wilson, but he chose Leeds

Chairman Paraag Marathe has recently stepped aside from his position at the San Francisco 49ers to focus on his football ventures, and played a key role in convincing Wilson to join Leeds

He talked about the loud, proud and loyal fanbase and discussed how Leeds were in the process of redeveloping Elland Road to increase its capacity.

‘After the first call I had with Leeds, with the chairman about the direction of the club, they were my number one choice,’ Wilson told us this week. ‘I spoke to a couple of other teams and nothing changed my mind.

‘The ownership group, the plans they have for the club. They know the size of the club with the fanbase and the history and the work they're doing to the stadium already to increase the capacity, the investment they're putting into the squad. It's all just going in one direction and that's what I want to be a part of.’

Marathe and a phone call from Farke, who tried to sign Wilson at his former club Norwich City, went a long way – but nothing sweetened the deal more than the persistence of club captain Ethan Ampadu, a Wales team-mate.

‘I almost had to block Ethan!’ laughed Wilson. ‘He played a big role. I'm really close with all the Welsh boys here. DJ (Dan James), I've played with since we were 14. Joe (Rodon), similar.

Asked about his ambitions, Wilson – who had the best season of his career last term, with ten league goals and seven assists – added: ‘Clubs have shown in recent years that the first season back in the Premier League, it's all about making sure you stay up. But in the end, Leeds stayed up really comfortably last season.

‘When you look at the likes of Sunderland and Forest, who've come up in recent years and have got into Europe, that's definitely an aim that we can have.

'But I think that second season syndrome has been the case with a few teams. So this season let's try and build on what the club created last year, that strong base, making sure our home form is good, which is massive and let's see where that takes us.’

Harry Wilson (left) adds to the Welsh contingent in Leeds' squad, including Daniel James (second left), Ethan Ampadu (right) and Joe Rodon (not pictured)

Wilson believes Leeds can take inspiration from the likes of Sunderland and Nottingham Forest in qualifying for Europe soon after promotion to the Premier League

Farke is set to stick by the back-five formation that turned his fortunes around last term. The boss had been sleepwalking towards the sack as Christmas approached, with Leeds in the relegation zone with a run of six defeats in the seven games leading up to December.

But after the switch, Leeds lost only five of 25 matches and reached an FA Cup semi-final.

Farke was criticised for his negative tactics at Wembley and knows he must build on solid defensive foundations with more exciting football this time around.

Trafford is a marquee signing. Some City observers believe he should have been given the No 1 jersey ahead of Gianluigi Donnarumma and many in the England set-up expect him to be the long-term successor to Jordan Pickford.

Comfortable in possession and a strong shot-stopper, it is an excellent addition, beating Newcastle United to the punch. Business is not done yet and a versatile attacker is top of the list. Dominic Calvert-Lewin had a fine season, scoring 15 times in all competitions, but needs help in sharing the goals around, with none of his team-mates managing more than eight.

Farke believes US international Brenden Aaronson is vastly underrated but another creative outlet would be welcomed with open arms, especially after Jack Harrison departed for MLS side New England Revolution. A deputy for injured left back Gabriel Gudmundsson is also wanted.

The boss has three more friendlies to fine-tune his squad: RB Leipzig and Augsburg at home on back-to-back Saturdays, and a clash with rivals Manchester United in Dublin at Croke Park on Wednesday.

Farke fell into coaching by accident having graduated in economics and originally wanted to be a sporting director.

This is his third crack at the Premier League after two relegations with Norwich, but sources insist he is growing every week and he believes that relationships have a greater impact than tactics.

Farke believes US international Brenden Aaronson is vastly underrated but another creative outlet would be welcomed with open arms

Sources insist Farke is growing every week and he believes that relationships have a greater impact than tactics

A literature nut whose favourite author is Gabriel Garcia Marquez, he also likes 19th-century poet Walt Whitman. The American’s best-known line ‘I contain multitudes' speaks to how leaders must contradict themselves to find answers.

Farke and the hierarchy will be mulling those over in the coming weeks: how to maintain Leeds’ solid base but still take attacking strides? How to keep his trademark calm demeanour while demanding more? How to be more ambitious in the transfer market without it coming back to bite financially?

If they can get the answers right, they can be successful this season. Just maybe not quite as successful as Mr Phelps.

Sports.title: UEFA ramp up pressure on defiant Gianni Infantino and insist they WILL boycott the World Cup if he refuses to quit - after under-fire FIFA president vowed to fight on
Sports.content:
UEFA ramp up pressure on defiant Gianni Infantino and insist they WILL boycott the World Cup if he refuses to quit - after under-fire FIFA president vowed to fight on

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

UEFA have doubled down on their threat to boycott the World Cup as the organisation reiterated it has 'lost confidence' in FIFA president Gianni Infantino.

Infantino has faced a major backlash since plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup emerged, leading to European football's governing body UEFA's initial threat to boycott the tournament if the plans were enacted.

UEFA's initial statement on Saturday had branded Infantino's proposal to flog commercial and event operations as a ‘shabby, back room, opaque deal’.

While plans have been scrapped, FIFA executives on Wednesday issued a statement giving their 'full support' to Infantino while acknowledging 'mistakes' in the plan.

FIFA said they have now apologised in a letter to the various football associations and that a ‘review’ will be carried out.

UEFA have now stressed the conditions to avoid a boycott of FIFA competitions have not been met, while the organisation again took aim at Infantino, as well as those 'whose careers depend on his favour'.

UEFA repeated that it has lost confidence in FIFA president Gianni Infantino and reiterated its threat to boycott the World Cup

'UEFA’s associations were very clear about the conditions attached to their non participation in FIFA competitions,' the statement read.

'First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

'These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency. That position holds.

'Yesterday’s announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing.'

An international football insider told Daily Mail Sport: ‘This had to be done. He has to go and this is the only way to force him out.’

Infantino had called a crisis meeting in Morocco on Wednesday, which concluded with a statement that FIFA’s secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, who had criticised Infantino, and other management board members in attendance ‘reaffirmed their full support for the president’.

For good measure, it added: ‘FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation.

‘There are always lessons to be learned, and FIFA will continue to improve its processes in light of this experience. In this instance, however, it is important to stress that, although mistakes were made, everything that was done was done in full compliance with the FIFA regulatory framework.’

The statement came hours after Luis Figo became the latest high-profile name to call for Infantino’s head in a blistering attack in Daily Mail Sport.

Infantino is facing mounting pressure over his failed plan to sell off stakes in the FIFA World Cup

Football legend Luis Figo became the latest high-profile individual to call for him to resign, while Arsene Wenger distanced himself from Infantino's plans

Figo had described Infantino’s now-aborted plan to flog a stake in the World Cup to private investors as the ‘lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed’ and a ‘grubby, underhand plot’.

Figo, the former Barcelona and Real Madrid star, who initially backed Infantino in 2015, branded the Swiss a ‘relic who should have no part in football’s future’ and accused him of ‘a litany of abuses’.

Aside from the World Cup sell-off, he referenced the decision to suspend the ban for USA striker Folarin Balogun after his red card at the World Cup and the half-time show during the final which ‘broke the laws of the game’.

‘Infantino has debased the office of FIFA president he promised to elevate,’ he wrote.

‘He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve.’

Amid heavy criticism and calls for Infantino to go, Grafstrom sent an all-staff memo describing the situation as ‘sad and reproachable’ and adding ‘individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go.’

However, second-in-command Grafstrom was pictured laughing and joking with Infantino at a women’s Africa Cup of Nations game following the meeting, ahead of the release of the statement.

Should he survive, Infantino would face re-election in March, and would need 106 votes from FIFA's 211 members to win another term in charge of the global game.

Sports.title: Jordanian FA suddenly receive eight-month overdue payment from FIFA but insist they still WON'T back Gianni Infantino - days after accusing president of 'blackmail'
Sports.content:
Jordanian FA suddenly receive eight-month overdue payment from FIFA but insist they still WON'T back Gianni Infantino - days after accusing president of 'blackmail'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein has confirmed the receipt of an overdue payment from FIFA, but has insisted his organisation will not back the governing body's under-fire president Gianni Infantino.

Prince Ali, who ran against Infantino for the FIFA presidency in 2016, had issued an explosive statement earlier this week over his running of the organisation.

He accused Infantino of delaying prize money payments and refusing to address the problem unless Jordan endorsed him for a fourth term at the helm of world football.

Along with highlighting challenges of getting their fans to attend the World Cup in the United States and their prize money being taxed by the host country, Prince Ali had highlighted that their players were awaiting payment for reaching the final of the Arab Cup in Qatar last December.

‘The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time FIFA brags about how many billions they have in reserve,' Prince Ali wrote.

‘It is clear the problem really is with leadership. For months, FIFA has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters - until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

Jordan FA president Prince Ali confirmed FIFA have made an overdue payment but insisted they will not back Gianni Infantino

Earlier this week Prince Ali accused Infantino of delaying prize money payments and refusing to address the problem unless Jordan endorsed him for a fourth term

The Jordan FA chief issued a statement on Thursday, confirming FIFA have now made the payment but stressed it does not change their serious concerns about their leadership

‘We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.

‘But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.’

In an update on social media, Prince Ali confirmed FIFA have now made the overdue payment but he renewed his criticism of the governing body and Infantino.

'Thank you to the FIFA administration for suddenly this morning delivering what was owed to our players and coaching staff, for the Jordan National team’s accession to the final of the FIFA Arab Cup in Qatar last December,' Prince Ali wrote.

'This was funding that should have been received 8 months ago.

'While this is a good development for our players, it does not change the serious concerns we in the football world have regarding the FIFA leadership, nor does it change what our FAs have been subjected to in the past.

‘There are always lessons to be learned, and FIFA will continue to improve its processes in light of this experience. In this instance, however, it is important to stress that, although mistakes were made, everything that was done was done in full compliance with the FIFA regulatory framework.’

Aside from the World Cup sell-off, he referenced the decision to suspend the ban for USA striker Folarin Balogun after his red card at the World Cup and the half-time show during the final which ‘broke the laws of the game’.

‘Infantino has debased the office of FIFA president he promised to elevate,’ he wrote.

‘He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve.’

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes in London to finalise £75m move to Arsenal after leaving Newcastle training camp - as Forest move for Ousmane Diomande reaches an impasse: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes in London to finalise £75m move to Arsenal after leaving Newcastle training camp - as Forest move for Ousmane Diomande reaches an impasse: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Diomande in doubt

Ousmane Diomande's move to Nottingham Forest has hit a major snag with the deal now far from certain.

Forest had been close to agreeing a fee of about £35m with Sporting Lisbon for the centre-back but Daily Mail Sport understands talks have hit the buffers.

Oliver Glasner had made the centre-back his top target - as he did at Crystal Palace last summer, which also proved unsuccessful.

Ousmane Diomande's move to Nottingham Forest is understood to have hit a snag

It now remains to be seen if the transfer can be revived in the remaining days of the window.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Trafford closes on Leeds switch

James Trafford has completed his medical with Leeds ahead of his £40million move from Manchester City.

The England goalkeeper is set to move for a club record £40m plus £5m in add-ons.

City have been trying to bring in Geronimo Rulli from Marseille as a replacement.

Dykes snubs Charlton for Millwall

Scotland striker Lyndon Dykes has agreed a one-year deal with Millwall.

The 30-year-old has completed a medical and is finalising his move.

Dykes rejected a longer term offer from Charlton Athletic, where he spent the second half of last season, as he looks to help Millwall earn promotion.

Scotland forward Lyndon Dykes is set to join Millwall

Villa and Toon keep tabs on defender

Racing Santander defender Jorge Salinas is attracting attention from Aston Villa and Newcastle United.

The 19-year-old can play left back and centre back and has also been watched by Barcelona and Manchester United scouts.

Some of the clubs view him as a player for the future while others are considering a bid this month.

Bruno heads to the capital

Bruno Guimaraes is understood to be in London to finalise his £75million move to Arsenal.

The 28-year-old left Newcastle's pre-season camp on Wednesday after a fee of £75m was agreed with Arsenal. Newcastle are continuing to work on a replacement.

Bruno Guimaraes is in London to complete his move from Newcastle to Arsenal

Gunners keep tabs on the next Kvaratskhelia

Arsenal scouts were at Larne's Europa League qualifier against Iberia 1999 on Tuesday.

They were understood to be running the rule over the Georgian side's attacking midfielder Andria Bartishvili.

The exciting 17-year-old has been on Arsenal's radar for a number of months and has been compared in style to compatriot Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at Paris St Germain.

Indeed, the French side are also understood to be among his admirers as well as clubs in Italy.

Bartishvili is on loan at Iberia from Kolkheti 1913, however, he is expected to be sold in the coming days as interest intensifies.

Hammers confirm Veltman

West Ham have confirmed the signing of former Brighton defender Joel Veltman.

The Dutch defender has signed a one-year contract with an option for a second year.

'I'm delighted to have signed, and I can't wait to get started,' said Veltman. 'The project here really excites me.'

'I spoke to Nuno [Espírito Santo], as well as my family and my agent, and everything added up. We know that West Ham need to be in the Premier League, and for sure that is our goal for the season.

'I think I bring my experience, my winning mentality and togetherness. I bring leadership - I've been the captain at Ajax, and I enjoy talking to my teammates and using my experience to help the squad.

'I'm just so excited to give everything, to meet my new teammates and to see all the supporters too.'

West Ham have announced the signing of Brighton defender Joel Veltman

JOEL VELTMAN STATS Played 24 Premier League matches in 25-26, but only started nine and played 1050 minutes Scored once last season - against West Ham (2-2 draw at London Stadium to salvage a point for Brighton) Across the Premier League season, Veltman made a total of 99 defensive contributions Won 75 duels (67% success rate) Won 20 aerial duels (62.5% success rate) 31 tackles 18 interceptions Six shots blocked 10 fouls committed 40 recoveries 44 clearances Five yellow cards Started all four cup matches he played in (two in Carabao Cup, two in FA Cup) *By Isabelle Martin

Barca rival Real Madrid's interest in Rodri

Barcelona have finally made their interest in Manchester City midfielder Rodri official to rival Real Madrid for his signature.

Rodri wants to return to Spain but Manchester City have been waiting for other clubs to declare their interest to get the optimum price for the 30-year-old.

Barcelona have finally expressed their interest in Manchester City and Spain midfielder Rodri

They have made a new contract offer to the Spain captain who has one year left but are aware of his desire to explore a move back.

Rodri was keen on a move to Madrid but equally is understood to be open to joining Barca's project where eight of the national team are in the current squad.

Sevilla right-back Juanlu Sanchez has been having his medical checks ahead of a permanent move to Bournemouth.

Sports.title: Trabzonspor confirm Mo Salah signing: Turkish club hand Liverpool legend record-breaking two-year deal - as eye-watering new contract details are revealed
Sports.content:
Trabzonspor have formally confirmed the signing of former Liverpool star Mohamed Salah on a lucrative two-year contract.

Salah had been greeted by Trabzonspor fans after touching down in Istanbul on Wednesday ahead of the move.

While Salah had been wearing the team's kit and addressed fans, Trabzonspor had repeated throughout that the club were still in negotiations with the star.

Formalities have now been completed with Salah having undergone a medical and signed a two-year contract with the Turkish side.

'Our new signing Mohamed Salah has signed the contract binding him to our club for two years, with the participation of our President Ertugrul Dogan,' Trabzonspor stated on social media.

Trabzonspor confirmed Salah's contract details on a public disclosure platform after completing the deal.

Mohamed Salah has signed a lucrative contract with Trabzonspor worth a reported £14.5m-a-year

Salah had been given a hero's welcome after arriving at Trabzon Airport on Wednesday night

Salah has now formally completed his move to the Turkish side after leaving Liverpool

'Under the terms of the agreement, the player will receive a total guaranteed payment of €17,000,000 (£14.5m) per football season, comprising an annual salary of €10,000,000 (£8.5m) and a signing fee of €7,000,000 (£6m),' the statement read.

'Additionally, the player will receive performance-based bonuses for each football season.

'Furthermore, under the image rights agreement, the player will receive a 20 per cent share of the revenue from products sold by our retail company that are specific to "Mohamed Salah."

'A payment amounting to five per cent of the gross remuneration payable to the player will be made as an agency fee.'

Supporters of the Turkish club had been celebrating Salah's arrival on Wednesday with crowds gathering at the Ataturk Airport in Istanbul.

The crowds greeted Salah, who was pictured in a Trabzonspor shirt having flown from the Greek island of Mykonos, where he had been on holiday, to Turkey.

Salah later travelled on to Trabzon, where more fans had massed by the airport.

'I am very happy to be in this incredible atmosphere. I don't recall ever seeing anything like this before,' Salah said.

'There are 25,000 people here —it's incredible. I've never seen anything like it.

'I have achieved success everywhere I've been, and I want to achieve success at Trabzonspor as well.'

Reports in Turkey claim Salah will earn 20 per cent of the profits from shirt sales featuring his name

An official signing ceremony has also been scheduled at Trabzonspor's Papara Park stadium this evening.

Trabzonspor invited fans to 'wear their new season kit to witness history'.

Turkish giants Besiktas had previously been in talks with Salah, but negotiations with the Egyptian star stalled last week.

Salah's future has been the subject of huge interest since the surprising decision was announced back in March that he would leave Liverpool one year into his two-year contract extension.

Many anticipated that Saudi Arabia would be the most likely destination after Al-Ittihad made a £150million bid in summer 2023, but Trabzonspor have secured the signing of Salah, who fell out with former Liverpool boss Arne Slot last season.

The Turkish side finished third last season behind Fenerbahce and champions Galatasaray.

Salah, who is the third-highest goalscorer in Reds history with 255, did not engage in talks with teams before the end of the season out of respect to the Merseyside club.

His long-serving agent, Ramy Abbas, repeatedly insisted nothing had been decided and reaffirmed that stance during the World Cup.

But since returning from the competition in the US, talks have accelerated with interested parties.

An official signing ceremony will take place on Thursday evening after Salah completed the move

Fans have been invited to wear the club's new kit to attend the event with their new star

Salah is renowned for his remarkable professionalism and will back himself to remain at a high level deep into his thirties.

Salah was the star man as Slot’s side won the Premier League in Slot's first season, the Egyptian's second English title, but his level dipped last term with just ten goals compared to a staggering 34 when he spear-headed the 2024-25 title win.

Liverpool are yet to replace the player who was voted Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Players' Player of the Year three times at the club.

With the start of the season fast approaching, Bradley Barcola of PSG remains the most likely high-profile attacking signing.

But the 23-year-old, valued at £145million by his club, plays predominantly on the left and Jamie Carragher recently warned against buying him as a replacement for Salah.

Sports.title: Argentina announce new national day to celebrate World Cup semi-final win over England - after victory reignited South Americans' claim to the Falkland Islands
Sports.content:
Argentina announce new national day to celebrate World Cup semi-final win over England - after victory reignited South Americans' claim to the Falkland Islands

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has announced July 15 will be 'National Football Teams Day' to mark Argentina's semi-final victory over England during this summer's World Cup on that date.

Argentina came from behind to beat England 2-1 late on in Atlanta, with Lionel Messi recording two assists as Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez scored in the 85th and 92nd minutes to book their second consecutive World Cup final.

It was regarded as a historic moment for the country, who celebrated the triumph as a political one, too, a chance to assert their claim over the Falkland Islands (Las Malvinas), which Britain has ruled since January 1833. Players celebrated with a banner that read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates to 'The Falkland Islands are Argentinian', after the final whistle.

'The date was chosen to commemorate Argentina's historic victory over England in the World Cup semi-final,' AFA said.

'Lionel Scaloni's team was trailing the English side by a single goal, but with goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez, they turned the game around, sending the entire nation into a frenzy of celebration.

'But the tribute isn't just for that milestone achieved by the senior national team.

Argentina came from behind to beat England 2-1 late on in Atlanta, with Lionel Messi recording two assists as Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez scored in the 85th and 92nd minute

It was regarded as a historic moment for the country, who celebrated the triumph as a political one, too, a chance to assert their claim over the Falkland Islands (Las Malvinas)

'The recognition, of course, also extends to each and every one of the national teams (youth, men's and women's, futsal, beach soccer, and field football), who train daily at the Lionel Andres Messi training complex with the hope, joy and responsibility of representing Argentina.'

The lifting of the banner triggered a fierce backlash in the UK, with former Prime Minister Keir Starmer insisting that while 'the World Cup might not be ours, the Falkland Islands definitely are. Self-determination rests with the islanders and our commitment to the Falklands will never waver'.

FIFA's rules forbid the use of any political messaging at the World Cup and Starmer called for an investigation into the matter, which the governing body last week confirmed.

Argentina President Javier Milei described the players' celebration with the banner as 'perfectly valid,' and said the message 'reflects a sentiment shared by all Argentines,' although he expected FIFA to sanction the team with a fine.

'I know that for Argentinians, we won the World Cup the moment we beat England because that's really what everyone wanted,' AFA president Claudio Tapia said during the recent AFA Sponsor Day.

Tapia added: 'We are proud of our national teams' performance, and of the fact that they created that sense of epic invincibility - that nobody could beat us.'

FIFA have also opened disciplinary proceedings into two Argentina players, Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina, along with Argentina coach Roberto Ayala, over allegations of assault following their conduct in the ugly scenes that marred the World Cup final against Spain.

Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time and the post-match scenes involved violent clashes between the players, with Argentina midfielder Paredes throwing Spain's Gavi to the floor

Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time and the post-match scenes involved violent clashes between both sets of players. Spain's captain Rodri was struck by Molina as he went to celebrate with his team-mates, before Dani Olmo was punched by coach Ayala.

Argentina midfielder Paredes also attacked Eric Garcia by grabbing him by the neck and then, along with team-mate Thiago Almada's help, threw unused Spanish substitute Gavi to the floor.

Paredes faces three counts of assault, Molina faces two counts (one completed and one attempted) and Ayala is charged with one count.

The trio, as well as the winger Thiago Almada and the Spanish midfielder Gavi, have also been charged with unsporting behaviour following the post-match brawl.

The FIFA investigation covers potential breaches 'in light of discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators' during several Argentina matches at the World Cup.

Sports.title: Real Madrid confident of seeing off Arsenal interest in Vinicius Jr after offering improved £19m deal - as Brazilian adds to uncertainty by deleting entire Instagram history
Sports.content:
Real Madrid are awaiting a response from Vinicius Jr after offering the Arsenal target improved terms in excess of £19million a year.

The Brazil international’s current terms with Madrid expire at the end of next season and Arsenal have made him aware they are willing to step in if he fails to find agreement with the Spanish giants.

Talks between the player’s agents, general director Jose Angel Sanchez and chief scout Juni Calafat took place in Madrid on Wednesday. Jose Mourinho also underlined that the 26-year-old is also firmly in his plans.

Real are believed to be increasingly confident of keeping the Brazilian superstar Vinicius Jr at the Bernabeu.

Despite the increased confidence at the Bernabeu, the player added to the uncertainty on Wednesday night by deleting his entire Instagram history.

Vinicius' page, which has 63.9million followers, currently displays no images or bio and he's also removed his profile picture.

Vinicius Junior in training with Real Madrid this week as the transfer saga takes another twist

Vinicius Jr deleted all the content from his Instagram, which was mostly Real Madrid related

The dramatic move - not uncommon among footballers - could be interpreted in a number of different ways but typically can be interpreted as dissatisfaction with the current club.

All of the Real Madrid training and playing images that featured prominently on his account have now gone.

Waiting in the wings and hoping to capitalise on the situation are Arsenal.

The Gunners made initial enquiries into the player last week, with manager Mikel Arteta insisting that the Premier League winners will be 'very ambitious' during the summer's transfer window.

But reports on Wednesday suggested Madrid were bullish about their chances of seeing off interest from north London - particularly with Mourinho's backing.

One of the major sticking points in negotiations between Real and Vinicius' camp has been the re-signing fee.

But the latest increase in their offer has left Real confident that Vinicius Jr will commit his future to the Spanish giants.

Real do not want to lose the Brazilian on a free, with his contract set to expire in less than a year.

The player is thought to view any contract he signs with Los Blancos, where he has played since 2018, as the defining deal of his career - and recognition of his efforts for the club that in recent seasons have seen him become a Ballon d'Or contender in their colours.

Vinicius returned to join his team-mates at their pre-season camp on Monday to undergo the standard start-of-season medical tests and train for the first time under new manager Mourinho.

Arteta meanwhile has remained upbeat about his plans for the rest of the window, following the £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge.

‘We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously,’ Arteta said following Arsenal's pre-season friendly against Girona.

‘We want to get better like anybody else, and you can see the transfer market and our opponents... We won't sit still and we are very ambitious with what we are doing.

‘The margins are very small. Because we want to get better and the level is going to increase.

'We need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team.’

Sports.title: Scottie Scheffler defended after microphones picked up row with his caddie
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler defended after microphones picked up row with his caddie

Two-time Masters champion Scottie Scheffler has been criticised ever since his heated exchange with his caddie at the Memorial Tournament back in June

View 2 Images Scottie Scheffler and his caddie, Ted Scott (Image: Ben Jared/PGA TOUR via Getty Images)

Golf star Min Woo Lee has defended Scottie Scheffler after the two-time Masters champion was involved in a heated exchanged his caddie back in June. Scheffler finished tied-12th at Muirfield earlier in the summer, but caught plenty of attention during the opening round in Ohio.

‌



During the opening round in Dublin, Scheffler hit one of his shots on the 16th hole into the water and was visibly frustrated as he spoke to his caddie, Tedd Scott, as he walked towards the drop zone.

‌



Audio picked up from the microphone showed Scheffler having a heated exchange with Scott as he walked down the fairway, with the four-time major winner being the subject of criticism ever since.

‌



However, Lee has leapt to the defence of Scheffler, explaining why the 30-year-old may have reacted the way he did in that moment at the Memorial tournament.

"First of all, I think that was a tough moment," Lee said on the Life on Tour podcast. "I know he's not like that all the time.

Why Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler aren't playing in Wyndham Championship as stars pull out READ MORE :

Rory McIlroy shows true colours as he's spotted partying at Ibiza nightclub READ MORE :

"It was just a really tough day at Memorial, and Memorial's one of the toughest — I think it's the toughest golf course outside of the majors. So blow-ups happen, and it just looked bad."

‌



Lee added: "I don't think social media and the audience know, 'Is this how he treats his caddie?' I think a lot of players do that, and it's just unlucky that the microphone was right there taking it all in.

"As an audience, you'd like that, you'd want to listen to all that, but as a player and colleague, I wouldn't want a mic that close to me, just because stuff like that can happen. He's one of the best players in the world and he's saying, 'How can the wind be there and not there?'

"I think caddies are very, very strong-skinned, and they've gone through a lot. Sometimes we give them slack and they just have to brush it off.

‌



"Sometimes they want to yell back at us, but it's a tough situation. I'm sure a lot of my caddies have wanted to shout back at me."

View 2 Images Scottie Scheffler and caddie Ted Scott (Image: Mike Mulholland/Getty Images)

‌



Scheffler was asked about the moment on the 16th hole at Muirfield, where he alsop reflected on his opening round in Ohio.

“That’s just another really good iron shot, and the wind switched from down off the right to pretty significantly in off the right,” Scheffler said after his first round on June 4.

“If it’s down off the right, that ball’s probably where I hit my wedge shot to. So just don’t really know what I’m supposed to do there outside of trying to hit a good shot, and then it’s frustrating when it doesn’t work out, especially when it doesn’t work out in that direction.

“I would rather get gusted in off the left, not in off the right there. All you can do is just try to hit good shots.

“It can be very frustrating sometimes when you feel like you’re hitting good shots and then you’re going to the drop zone.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua 'won't be in the UK' and could be on a WEEKDAY
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua 'won't be in the UK' and could be on a WEEKDAY

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are set to finally face off in November, but there could be an unexpected outcome surrounding exactly when the fight takes place

View 2 Images Anthony Joshua sent a chilling warning to Tyson Fury after knocking out Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's blockbuster boxing clash is set to take place in the United States on a weekday. The heavyweight fight is finally set to take place this year after the Gypsy King defeated Mariusz Wach in Thailand, and Joshua survived a scare to defeat Kristian Prenga.

‌



The British boxing giants are 'almost certain' to face off in the US, per Sports Illustrated, with Madison Square Garden set to be the destination. Netflix are said to have steered the bout Stateside, and the streamer could yet pick a shock day for fight to take place.

‌



UK broadcast norms could be thrown out of the window with a rejection of the usual Saturday night schedule. Instead, a Friday night is being targeted by the streaming service.

‌



November 20 is being touted as a potential date for the fight in a bid to avoid any clash with College Football, it is claimed. Netflix have veered from its Friday slot just once, when Terence Crawford defeated Canelo Alvarez almost 12 months ago.

Speaking following his win over Wach, Fury, 37, suggested he didn't know where the fight would take place. The former world champion outlined a number of potential destinations.

British boxer rushed to hospital after suffering bleed on her brain READ MORE :

“I’ll regroup, and hopefully the next big fight is signed next week, and we head wherever we’re going to head. Who the f*** knows," he said.

‌



"Is it gonna be in Vegas? Is it gonna be in New York? Is it gonna be in Ireland? Is it gonna be in London? Who knows, Belfast maybe? It might even be here in Pattaya, Thailand!”

Meanwhile, AJ's promoter Eddie Hearn has said that the bout agreement means that the fight must take place in the United Kingdom. "It's done. We signed a legally binding contract about three months ago," Hearn said.

View 2 Images Tyson Fury beat Mariusz Wach behind closed doors over in Thailand (Image: AP Photo/Sakchai Lalit)

‌

"There's a reason that we put contracts together. There's a reason AJ employs lawyers, there's a reason that me and him sit down and have endless conversations to make sure every move is correct.

"We insisted that this fight was in the UK. I know AJ will sometimes want to be a peace-keeper, but the reality is he said to me 'I want the fight in the UK.'"

‌



Hearn has since admitted: "There was never any doubt this fight was in the UK until there were some approaches from America in terms of the revenue that could be achieved at MSG."

While both Fury and Joshua are in the twilight of their careers, the winner of their fight could receive a title shot. Murat Gassiev is willing to give the victor an opportunity, having defended his WBA belt against Peter Kadiru.

Sports.title: Newcastle's embarrassing starting XI for first match of season if Lewis Hall joins Man Utd
Sports.content:
Newcastle's embarrassing starting XI for first match of season if Lewis Hall joins Man Utd

Newcastle have seen a number of key stars depart St James' Park this summer

View 5 Images Newcastle could look wildly different this season (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Newcastle could be forced to field an extremely depleted starting XI against Liverpool should Lewis Hall transfer to Manchester United. The Magpies have announced Matthias Jaissle as their new head coach following Eddie Howe's departure last week.

‌



However, Jaissle walks into a tough situation in the north east with numerous key stars unavailable. Hall has been heavily linked with a move as the Red Devils make him their leading target for their left-back department.

‌



Bruno Guimaraes has been given permission to travel for a medical to sign for Arsenal after the clubs agreed a £75million fee. Newcastle had been keen to retain their captain for the upcoming season but the Brazil international told chiefs that he was set on a move to north London.

‌



Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon have already left Newcastle, signing for Tottenham and Barcelona respectively. Jacob Murphy has been touted with a move to Everton as he entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Newcastle finally confirm Matthias Jaissle as new manager to replace Eddie Howe READ MORE :

Inside Bruno Guimaraes' Arsenal transfer and the secret battle both clubs want to win READ MORE :

The Magpies are also dealing with several injuries this pre-season. Before his departure, Howe confirmed that Tino Livramento's calf surgery meant his issues were "the most longer term" and he could be missing at the start of the Premier League season.

Will Osula, Sven Botman, Lewis Miley and Joelinton all had minor injuries at the start of pre-season but have since returned to training. If Hall, Guimaraes and Murphy leave, then Newcastle would really be left in an embarrassing predicament to face Liverpool.

‌



5 View 5 Images Bruno Guimaraes is the next star nearing an exit (Image: Newcastle United/Newcastle United via Getty Images) 5 View 5 Images Lewis Hall could be the next to depart St James' Park (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

‌



Nick Pope would retain his starting berth, although the goalkeeper has also been linked with a possible exit. Dan Burn and Sven Botman would be relied upon in central defence, but the first problem arises in the full-back department.

With Livramento out and Hall potentially away, 34-year-old Fabian Schar would have to slot in at right-back. Alex Murphy would be thrown in at the deep end at left-back, despite making just eight appearances for the Magpies in his career.

The midfield is extremely depleted due to the absences of Tonali and Guimaraes, with Joelinton the most senior option. Joe Willock and Lewis Miley would partner the Brazilian but may struggle to replace their club captain's presence. Nick Woltemade would be leading the line as a solo striker, with Yoanne Wissa and Anthony Elanga on the wings.

While the forward line could be argued to be a dependable strike force, the lack of experience at left-back and the loss of creativity in the middle of the park could point to an embarrassing start to the 2026/27 season.

Sports.title: Man Utd forced to fork out millions as Marcus Rashford benefits from contract loophole
Sports.content:
Man Utd forced to fork out millions as Marcus Rashford benefits from contract loophole

Manchester United face losing up to £5million due to past mistakes over contracts with Marcus Rashford expected to benefit

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is set for a seven-figure bonus on top of his hefty Manchester United wages (Image: Getty)

Marcus Rashford is set to pocket an extra £4million if he stays at Manchester United due to a clause in his contract which has been activated because the club are back in the Champions League. The England international is among three players that can receive such a windfall with his current deal signed before United changed the structure of bonuses in contracts.

‌



Prior to the arrival of Sir Jim Ratcliffe, players would automatically receive a 25 per cent wage increase upon Champions League football being secured. Such terms were included in the sizeable long-term deals signed by Mason Mount and Andre Onana in the summer of 2023, which was exactly when Rashford penned a new five-year deal.

‌



United failing to play in Europe last season resulted in pay cuts but Champions League football for the new campaign has seen them go back up. For Rashford and Mount, who are still at the club, it is particularly beneficial because of the clause in their legacy contracts.

‌



Marcus Rashford primed for Ruben Amorim reunion after Man Utd transfer twist READ MORE :

The chance for a salary increase still exists in United deals for first-team players but they now have to earn it, as per The Telegraph, which is done through playing in over 60 per cent of the minutes in the proceeding campaign. That requires players to have been on the pitch for just over 2,000 minutes.

Rashford and Onana spent the campaign on loan elsewhere while Mount played just over half of the total required, but it is something that none of the trio have to worry about when it comes to receiving bonuses.

With Rashford taking in roughly £16million per-year, United's return to elite European football means he will be receiving an extra £4million on top of his weekly wage.

‌



United are also being forced to pay Mount in excess of £1m annually and while Onana's wages for the season are being covered by Trabzonspor, his salary has increased as well with this loan far less beneficial financially due to the clause.

View 2 Images Manchester United look to have managed to avoid paying Andre Onana an extra £1.5million

Both Rashford and the latter have been made available for permanent transfer but United have had problems selling either, largely due to their wages and the bonus in their contracts.

‌



Despite impressing at Barcelona, who opted against signing him permanently for financial reasons, that is likely why United were so eager to sell Rashford. A significant U-turn has since been completed on that stance, however, with it now looking more likely he will stay at Old Trafford.

Given the unnecessary outlay, United's summer plans are being impacted with deals for top targets deemed too expensive. The club were able to strike clever deals for Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos but missed out on signing Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes.

Sports.title: International footballer, 27, beaten to death in shocking street attack as thugs ambush him
Sports.content:
International footballer, 27, beaten to death in shocking street attack as thugs ambush him

Ugandan footballer David Owori was reportedly attacked with paving stones outside of his home before dying with an outpouring of grief taking place in his home nation

View 2 Images David Owori died on Wednesday after a brutal attack (Image: SC VILLA)

An international footballer has died aged 27 after being ambushed by thugs and beaten. David Owori was rushed to a medical facility after being left unconscious from a brutal attack and died on Wednesday.

‌



Police say the fatal assault saw Owori resist an attempt to steal his belongings, while witnesses reportedly saw attackers hit the Sports Club Villa captain with paving stones. An SC Villa spokesperson said that Owori was targeted just outside his home in Makindye, a Kampala suburb in Uganda.

‌



"The player was ambushed by thugs as he approached his home, leaving him with life-threatening injuries before he was rushed to the medical facility," they said.

‌



Owori's club posted a short tribute following their captain's passing. "Our hearts are broken," it read.

"SC Villa mourns the tragic passing of our beloved captain, David Owori, following a brutal attack. We have lost more than a player—we have lost a leader, brother and friend. Our deepest prayers are with his family. Rest well, Captain."

One dead and 12 injured after horrific lightning strike during football match READ MORE :

Uganda's football association also paid tribute to Owori, who wore national team colours during the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. They said he 'carried the hopes of a naiton'.

‌



"The Federation of Uganda Football Associations mourns the untimely passing of Owori David, Captain of SC Villa and Uganda Cranes player," a statement read.

"David was not just a footballer. He was both a leader and an inspiration to a generation. As Captain of SC Villa, he led with courage, humility and passion. In the Uganda Cranes jersey, he carried the hopes of a nation.

‌

"On behalf of the FUFA Executive Committee, Delegates, Members, Secretariat Staff and the entire football fraternity, we extend our deepest condolences to SC Villa, his family, teammates, coaches and all Ugandans on the loss of Owori.

"We have lost a son, a leader and a star. His light on and off the pitch will never be forgotten.

‌



"We pray that the Almighty grants Owori David eternal rest and gives his family and SC Villa the strength to bear this great loss during these trying times. Rest in peace, Captain."

Uganda's parliament held a minute of silence for Owori on Wednesday.

The midfielder helped SC VIlla to a first league title in 20 years in 2024 after joining the club for the second time in 2023. The earlier parts of his career saw spells as Proline FC, Spanish side Velez CF and Swedish team Utiskitens BK, in addition to SC Villa.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup first round TV guide: How to watch every match live this weekend
Sports.content:
Carabao Cup first round TV guide: How to watch every match live this weekend

The Carabao Cup first round kicks off this weekend, marking the return of domestic club football ahead of the EFL season getting underway

Sports.title: Godolphin superstar’s brother produces ‘wow’ moment with 21 length debut victory
Sports.content:
Godolphin superstar’s brother produces ‘wow’ moment with 21 length debut victory

Fortitudine, whose famous sibling is the recently retired Rebel’s Romance, produced a stunning performance to defeat the 5-6 favourite at Kempton

View 2 Images Fortitudine won by 21 lengths on debut (Image: https://x.com/RacingTV)

A brother of Godolphin superstar Rebel’s Romance produced a ‘wow’ moment on Wednesday night with a 21 length debut victory. Fortitudine is the three-year-old gelded full brother of the recently retired champion by supersire Dubawi.

‌



Rebel’s Romance ran his last race at Newmarket last month when he captured the Group 2 Princess Of Wales’s Stakes, the 22nd success of his career. He won nine Group 1 races including the Breeders’ Cup Turf twice, Dubai Sheema Classic and Hong Kong’s Champions & Chater Cup, finishing with career earnings of £12.2 million.

‌



Fortitudine has a long way to go to match those achievements but he began his career in impressive fashion on the all-weather at Kempton.

‌



Ffos Las race meeting moved to earlier start time to avoid effects of solar eclipse READ MORE :

The gelding went off the 7-2 second favourite for the 1m3f novice stakes behind the odds-on Dialstone, who had finished second on his only previous start.

Jockey James Doyle had him out of the stalls smartly and took him straight to the front. He kept pouring on the power, pushing right away from his rivals in the straight.

‌



The Racing Post analysis said the winner “produced a genuine wow moment on his debut, jumping from a wide draw at speed and keeping the gallop up right to the line to pull right away from the whole field. Post-race comments by the rider plus his starting price suggest this sort of performance wasn't expected at all, so he rates a most exciting prospect for the Charlie Appleby stable”.

View 2 Images Out on his own: Fortitudine at Kempton (Image: https://x.com/RacingTV)

Doyle was aboard Rebel's Romance when he triumphed in the 2022 Breeders' Cup Turf.

‌



He said: “He was quite professional. I gave him one tap, then he balanced up and away he went. He’s learning on the job nicely.

“He feels like he lengthens away. He doesn’t do anything too quickly, so I was keen to keep the revs up, keep him in a nice high gear and keep him galloping. The trip is right and he might even get a bit further.”

He added: “I was a bit surprised myself when I had a little look around. It bodes well; hopefully he's in for a good career.”

Sports.title: Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola

Andoni Iraola is desperate for a signing in central defence, where Liverpool are "very thin", and the club could beat Arsenal to Aston Villa and England star Ezri Konsa

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is desperate for defensive reinforcements (Image: Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool could rival Arsenal for the signing of Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa as Andoni Iraola desperately seeks a solution to his injury crisis. Pre-season has shown just how short Liverpool are in central defence, providing some urgency to their search for a new centre-back.

‌



An injury to Joe Gomez in a friendly against Sunderland has highlighted the lack of depth in the position, with £55million signing Jeremy Jacquet yet to feature in pre-season as he's eased back from a shoulder injury and Giovanni Leoni still recovering from his ACL injury.

‌



With Virgil van Dijk given time off after the World Cup, Iraola has been forced to turn to youth, starting Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, and Luke Chambers, 22, in the 4-2 defeat by Leeds on Sunday, while Mor Talla Ndiaye, 18, has also featured in pre-season.

‌



The departure of Ibrahima Konate means Liverpool need an experienced player to partner Van Dijk and the Guardian reports that Konsa has emerged as a target. The England international is also on Arsenal's radar after William Saliba suffered a back injury at the World Cup, but Villa's £60m valuation is thought to be beyond the Gunners' means.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jamie Carragher criticises Mohamed Salah's Turkey move after Liverpool exit READ MORE :

Konsa has two years left on his contract at Villa, where he has played since 2019, making 286 appearances in all competitions. The 28-year-old has a wealth of Premier League experience and could fit the bill for Iraola, who has voiced frustrations at the lack of depth in the squad he inherited this summer.

‌



Jacquet, who signed in January from Rennes, and Victor Munoz (£35m from Osasuna) are the only two major deals done so far and the issue is shown by the fact Iraola's assistant, Tommy Elphick, had to fill in at centre-back in a recent training drill.

Iraola admitted recently: "With the centre-back, with the right-back situation, in terms of defensive depth, we are, I think, very thin right now so I think it's a solution that we are trying to find, yes."

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa is a target for Liverpool and Arsenal (Image: Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

‌



Gomez will miss the Premier League opener against Newcastle on August 23, leaving Van Dijk as the only fit senior centre-back in the squad. The Dutchman did not join his team-mates on the United States leg of their pre-season, leaving Iraola will less time to work with him before the campaign kicks off.

"When the market is open, you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad," Iraola said last month. "There are obvious situations where we need to sign players."

Liverpool are undergoing a summer of transition, with Iraola arriving to replace Arne Slot after a disappointing campaign, which saw Konate, Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson leave. To complicate matters further, Fenway Sports Group chief Michael Edwards has also left, piling more pressure and responsibility onto sporting director Richard Hughes to get deals done.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead
