“Everybody has got this trade-off between when you're bringing upgrades – chassis and PU – and also where you spend your money,” McNish continued. “Because you can't spend everything at one time, because then you don't have anything to fight with later. So it's got to be a managed expectation, and not just over one season, but multiple seasons as well.

“And so certainly from our point of view with the ADUO [Additional Upgrades and Opportunities for weaker powertrains], we brought something in Barcelona straight away, which was some small adaption, and that worked well, that helped us on our way. And then I would say the bigger parts are for 2027. So we will not see anything big on the power unit until then.”

Allan McNish, Racing Director of Audi F1 Team Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

When Autosport followed up with how big a step he would expect from the 2027-spec power unit, McNish chuckled: “That’s ‘27. Give us a break. We’re only halfway through ‘26, I need my cup of tea first.

“You've got where you're going, but it's also relative to the competition. And so therefore we're always benchmarking against the competition, and how quickly they move, and how quickly we can evolve.

“You could see that we've evolved in our performance this year so far, which has been definitely power-unit-related as well, making sure that we try to maximise some of the systems on that, but also definitely on the chassis with the upgrades that we spoke about there. And so I think we've definitely done that.

“We will do again in the second half of the year, but for the power unit that’s the ‘27 topic. It’s more hardware than anything, and that’s not a quick thing to change.”

Expanding on the Barcelona update’s “driveability” focus, Hulkenberg had detailed at Spa-Francorchamps: “It is about what you request on the pedal, but how the PU responds, how the torque delivery is. Does it surge, is it consistent, is it smooth? It is very fine stuff.

“We can talk about it, but you need to have experience to feel it. It happens in a blink of an eye, less than a tenth on a corner exit. But with a car on the limit, over the limit, all these things matter a lot.

Nico Hulkenberg, Audi F1 Team Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

“If you then have driveability issues on top of that, it is like trying to hit a curveball. The same on the gearbox side with shifting, shift quality.

“As you are all aware and heard of, there can be big differences in terms of shift quality, upshifts and downshifts. And they have an impact on car balance and car behaviour too. So it all goes together.”

Sports.title: Hamilton vs Leclerc: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Does Lewis Hamilton have an eighth world championship in him? Has he not recovered from the blow of 2021 or did he simply never gel with the ‘ground effect’ cars of 2022-25?

Those hoping to see the seven-times world champion fight for another title will have drawn great encouragement from what they have seen so far in 2026. Last year, in his first season at Ferrari, he came off badly in comparison to Charles Leclerc , taking a 19-5 pasting in qualifying and making zero podium appearances to his team mate’s seven.

Hamilton has given full credit to team principal Frederic Vasseur for implementing the changes he needed to make a success of his transition to Ferrari, whether that has involved different brake material or swerving the simulator. On the face of it, it has paid off, and Ferrari now have two A-list drivers performing at their peak.

Leclerc is still shading Hamilton on average in qualifying, but the fight between the two has been much closer. Hamilton has delivered more consistently on race day, including that breakthrough victory in Spain.

Both drivers have misfired at times. Leclerc had a spate of errors including costly crashes in qualifying at the Circuit de Catalunya and during his home race.

Hamilton, meanwhile, has picked up a bad habit of incurring the stewards’ wrath, collecting a series of needless penalties in recent races. Though some may not have been his fault or were debatable calls, many others were straightforward, and he was fortunate to avoid a worse penalty for his yellow flag slip in Silverstone.

For all that, Hamilton is Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s closest rival in the championship at the summer break. “Has the time finally come for Hamilton to hang up his helmet?” we asked in May, in what already looks like one of the most poorly-timed polls ever featured on RaceFans.

Sports.title: Antonelli vs Russell: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Early in the season it seemed certain that whichever of the Mercedes drivers came out ahead would be crowned world champion. That remains likely, but the threat posed by rival teams has grown in recent races.

Little about Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s form in his rookie season indicated that 12 months later he would be beating his team mate quite as emphatically as he is. But heading into the summer break, Antonelli holds a valuable 59-point lead over the other Mercedes driver.

It’s a far cry from the situation around 12 months ago. At the end of the ‘European season’, Antonelli was 15-1 down against George Russell in qualifying. He ended the season still with less than half his team mate’s points tally.

But after a difficult mid-season, following a Mercedes upgrade which did not go as intended, Antonelli rebounded impressively with the end of the year in sight. He reached the podium twice over the final four rounds.

So while Russell’s season-opening victory in Australia looked like the shape of things to come, Antonelli shattered those illusions by winning the next five rounds in a row. He got the rub of the green at times – technical trouble hit Russell in qualifying at Shanghai and took him out while he led in Montreal – but he has also seemed fundamentally more at ease with Mercedes’ W17 than his team mate.

The unusually high rate of problems on Mercedes’ cars, and Russell’s particular problems with poor straight-line speed at Silverstone and Spa, have further complicated the picture. Antonelli’s car has not been immune, breaking down in Spain and breaking an aerodynamic component at Silverstone. Overall, Russell has probably had slightly worse luck, but not 59 points’ worth. Antonelli is leading this championship on merit, and Russell will have to dig deep in the second half of the season if he is going to avoid a painful defeat.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: How far is modern F1 like the ‘turbo era’? | Formula 1
Asian Le Mans Series to take place entirely in Europe following war in Middle East | Brief
Sports.content:
The Asian Le Mans Series has announced its 2026-27 season will take place entirely at European circuits.

Since 2021 the series has only raced at the Dubai Autodrome, Yas Marina in the United Arab Emirates and Malaysia’s Sepang International Circuit. Its upcoming championship will take place at Jerez in Spain, Paul Ricard in France and Autodromo do Algarve in Portugal. The championship will be renamed the ‘Winter Le Mans Series’ as a result.

The change is the latest in a series of alterations to the motorsport calendar which have arisen following the war in the Middle East.

“While moving the Asian Le Mans Series to Europe is not ideal, the situation in the Middle East dictated that we worked to find the best solution,” said series promoter Stephane Ratel. “Between SRO, LMEM and the ACO we have a huge pool of experience to draw on, and the consensus was a Winter Le Mans Series in southern Europe was the most sensible option given the mounting external constraints.”

Formula 1 cancelled its races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia earlier this year. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has indicated the series will race in Europe if its final two rounds in the Middle East cannot go ahead.

Sports.title: FIA failed to listen to warnings over its 2026 F1 rules change – Coulthard | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Former Formula 1 driver David Coulthard blames the FIA for the poor state of the series’ 2026 regulations.

The championship revised its rules just four races into the new season after discovering significant shortcomings which left the cars seriously starved of energy on some tracks. This was evident from the first race of the season in Melbourne where cars slowed down significantly approaching fast corners because they could not recover enough energy to keep their batteries sufficiently charged.

Some figures in F1 had warned about this problem years before the new rules were introduced. Coulthard said the FIA should take responsibility for failing to listen to them.

“The new regs came at us with drivers and engineers going, ‘this is not going to be good’, and pretty much silence from everyone else,” Coulthard told Up to Speed. “We get to Melbourne and we go, ‘ah, they have deceleration as they go towards certain corners’.”

Coulthard believes the FIA should have anticipated the shortcomings in the new rules.

“I feel that we saw this coming and nobody really was listening,” he said. “And the fact they had to react to the reality in a sport that simulates the hell out of the future was a bit disappointing and that has to fall really with FIA.

“I know they’ll get sensitive and go ‘well we are a small group of people and the Formula 1 teams have hundreds of people’ but all of the evidence was there that having 50-50 on electrical and battery was going to be challenging.”

He said the series reacted well to the problem by introducing changes after the Miami Grand Prix. F1 will also make further changes to its regulations over the next two seasons in an attempt to improve the cars’ performance.

“What are we doing going forward? We’re going to have more internal combustion next year and it’s suggested even more the year after. So to see the obvious, and then react, is a bit disappointing.”

He likened the new rules to “the halftime show at the [football] World Cup – it was a bit of a disappointment.”

Sports.title: Why Sugar Ray Leonard Remains Boxing’s Gold Standard
Sports.content:
Leonard’s rise reached another level in November 1979 when he stopped Wilfred Benitez to capture the WBC welterweight championship. He never spent his prime protecting a title against limited opposition. Instead, he pursued the defining names of his era, including Roberto Duran, Thomas Hearns, Marvin Hagler and later Donny Lalonde. Few champions have matched that level of opposition while continuing to win on boxing’s biggest stages.

Leonard’s greatest strength may have been his ability to adjust. After losing to Duran in their first meeting by choosing to trade at close range, he completely changed his approach in the rematch. Using movement, sharp combinations and psychological pressure, Leonard frustrated Duran until the Panamanian famously quit in the eighth round. That performance remains one of boxing’s finest examples of tactical adjustment between fights.

Another defining victory came against Hearns in September 1981. Trailing on the scorecards late in the fight, Leonard produced a dramatic rally before stopping the unbeaten champion in the 14th round. After returning from retirement following a detached retina, Leonard outpointed Marvin Hagler in one of boxing’s most debated championship fights. That victory reinforced his reputation for delivering on the sport’s biggest stages.

Leonard retired with a 36-3-1 record, 25 knockouts and world titles in five weight classes. His career was built on victories over Hall of Fame opponents at a time when boxing’s biggest names routinely fought one another. That willingness to chase the toughest available challenges became one of the defining traits of his career.

Leonard’s accomplishments continue to resonate because they were earned against an extraordinary generation that included Roberto Duran, Thomas Hearns and Marvin Hagler. Few champions have defeated that caliber of opposition during a single era, which is why Sugar Ray Leonard remains boxing’s gold standard.

Sports.title: Hamzah Sheeraz’s Pressure Fighter Problem Casts Doubt On Undisputed Hopes
Sports.content:
Adames and Zachenhuber approached Sheeraz in different ways, yet both achieved success by applying constant pressure. Neither man spent much time backing away. Both absorbed punches to close the distance, forcing exchanges while keeping Sheeraz from settling behind his long jab. Instead of controlling the pace with his size and reach, Sheeraz spent long stretches reacting.

That presents a major concern at 168 pounds because the division contains numerous fighters who thrive under those exact conditions.

Christian Mbilli relentlessly marches forward. Kevin Lele Sadjo brings constant pressure. Jaime Munguia keeps throwing punches until opponents break. Lester Martinez keeps pressing forward and makes opponents fight at close range. Osleys Iglesias possesses enough power to make every exchange dangerous. Diego Pacheco controls distance behind his jab and steadily applies pressure. Even Saul Canelo Alvarez, despite being late in his career, excels at cutting off the ring and forcing opponents to fight his fight.

Becoming undisputed is never about defeating a single champion. It requires beating a series of elite fighters across contrasting styles. Pressure fighters, punchers, technicians and counterpunchers all present different challenges. The deeper the division, the harder that task becomes.

The Berlanga knockout looks more like a favorable stylistic matchup than proof that every weakness vanished. Berlanga gave Sheeraz room to establish his rhythm and capitalize on defensive mistakes. Adames and Zachenhuber denied him that comfort, forcing rounds that were far more competitive than many expected.

A single tough fight does not define a career. Sheeraz still possesses the size, skill and punching power to win a world title. His performances against Adames and Zachenhuber, however, show that aggressive opponents who refuse to surrender ground present a difficult style for him to solve.

Until Sheeraz answers that question against top opposition, talk of cleaning out the super middleweight division appears premature. Winning one championship is difficult enough. Sweeping through one of boxing’s deepest divisions is an entirely different challenge.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Leans Toward Conor Benn Upset Over Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
“I think we’re going to get an example of what it is. You always hear the saying where they say it’s easier to get the belt, but then it’s harder to keep it, right? Maybe Ryan right now might find out that. Ideally, in the business aspect, everyone wants to see Ryan win,” said Teofimo to Sean Zittel. “But Conor Benn is hungry. He’s in there. He’s in the gym every day. He’s speaking Spanish to the man, and he’s not even Hispanic. I think those things show the determination and what it means to Conor Benn. When he didn’t look so great against Eubank the first time, he came back with vengeance the second time. Conor Benn is no pushover, man. Look, I said it before, I think Conor Benn might pull the upset. We just have to wait and see.”

Garcia’s dominant performance against Mario Barrios also factored into his thinking. Teofimo said that version of Ryan would be extremely difficult to beat, but he is not convinced the same fighter will appear on September 12.

His support for Benn also comes with a personal incentive. Teofimo said he is rooting for the British contender because a victory would improve the chances of landing a future fight in the United Kingdom. He added that either Benn or Garcia would be an attractive opponent after his August 22 WBA welterweight title fight against Rolando Romero.

Sports.title: Canelo Refuses To Give Crawford Full Credit For Defeat
Sports.content:
“You cannot control the results,” Alvarez said. “Even when you do everything good, things don’t go your way. I learned that. Sometimes we forget the bases, and I forgot the bases in that fight,” said Canelo to CBS Mornings about his loss to Crawford. “Mentally, I was not there. I did everything correct in the training camp, but mentally I was not there. I learned that. If I’m going to still fighting, I need to be there mentally and physically.”

Alvarez’s explanation puts the spotlight on his own performance rather than Crawford’s. He did not point to injuries, problems in training camp or controversial judging. Instead, he argued that his mindset kept him from performing at the standard he expected of himself.

Not everyone will accept that explanation. Crawford spent months crafting a game plan, executed it with discipline and repeatedly beat Alvarez to the punch. His speed, timing and ring IQ played a major role in one of the biggest victories of his career. Because of that, some fans will view Alvarez’s comments as an honest assessment of his own shortcomings, while others will see them as an attempt to soften the impact of a clear defeat.

One thing is certain: Canelo does not believe the fight reflected his best version. Combined with his recent comments about wanting a lucrative rematch, it is clear he still believes he can produce a different result if the two ever meet again.

Canelo still has to get past WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli on October 31 for a Crawford rematch to remain a realistic possibility. Even if he defeats Mbilli, it’s far from certain Turki Alalshikh will want to finance a second fight after last September’s disappointing first meeting. Crawford spent much of the night boxing cautiously, tying Canelo up whenever he closed the distance, while Alvarez faded after the sixth round. Given the lukewarm reaction to the bout, Turki may decide his money is better spent on fresher matchups rather than revisiting a fight that failed to meet expectations.

Sports.title: Remembering Boxing’s Most Unusual Heavyweights
Sports.content:
Dallas Cowboys defensive end Ed “Too Tall” Jones brought NFL fame into the boxing ring during the late 1970s. He finished 6-0 after stepping away from football, although many questioned the quality of his opposition. Jones was knocked down in his professional debut before escaping with a heavily booed majority decision over Abraham Meneses. Only one of his six opponents owned a winning record. Following a first-round knockout of Ricky Gonzalez in his final bout, Jones returned to the Cowboys.

Eric “Butterbean” Esch became one of boxing’s biggest attractions during the 1990s thanks to his enormous size and knockout power. Known as “The King of the Four Rounders,” Butterbean finished with a 77-10-4 record and 58 knockouts. His most memorable performance came in 2002 against former heavyweight champion Larry Holmes. Fighting ten rounds for the only time in his career, Butterbean scored a knockdown in the final round before losing a unanimous decision in the 53-year-old Holmes’ farewell fight.

Chicago’s Craig Bodzianowski won his first 17 professional fights before a motorcycle accident resulted in the amputation of his right leg below the knee. Refusing to walk away from boxing, he returned with a prosthetic limb and eventually challenged WBA cruiserweight champion Robert Daniels. Bodzianowski lost the decision after suffering severe facial damage, yet simply reaching a world title fight under those circumstances remains one of boxing’s most remarkable comeback stories.

None of these men became heavyweight champions remembered for championship reigns. Instead, each earned a lasting place in boxing history because their careers unfolded in ways few other fighters could match.

Sports.title: Cassius Clay vs Doug Jones 1963 The Night A Future Champion Was Pushed To His Limit
Sports.content:
Despite his unbeaten streak, skepticism remained. His speed and reflexes had overwhelmed previous opponents, yet critics remained unconvinced those strengths would survive against a seasoned contender who refused to be intimidated. His habit of pulling straight back with his hands low also invited scrutiny. If Jones timed those defensive lapses, many believed the young contender’s shortcomings would finally cost him.

Clay intensified the spotlight. He first predicted a sixth-round stoppage before changing it to the fourth after spotting a newspaper photograph of Jones reading a book titled The Rise and Fall of Cassius Clay. He mocked Jones throughout the promotion. Jones responded calmly, saying Clay’s boasting increased both purses while maintaining he would win.

Jones immediately justified the pre-fight concerns. He landed clean right hands early, repeatedly timing Clay as he leaned straight back, and absorbed the favorite’s attacks without flinching. When the fourth round passed without the promised knockout, the Madison Square Garden crowd greeted Clay with loud boos. The final rounds remained competitive before Clay finished with a stronger burst of activity to secure a unanimous decision.

The verdict settled little. Two officials scored the fight five rounds to four with one even for Clay, while the referee had him comfortably ahead. Many ringside writers disagreed, with one media poll producing more scorecards for Jones than Clay. The disputed result, combined with Jones’ performance throughout the contest, left many wondering whether Clay was truly ready for Sonny Liston.

History answered those questions quickly. Clay stopped Henry Cooper three months later before defeating Liston in one of boxing’s greatest upsets. Jones never received his own title opportunity despite pushing the future champion harder than almost anyone during his rise. For one night inside Madison Square Garden, Doug Jones forced the boxing world to question whether the sport’s loudest prospect was truly destined to become heavyweight champion.

Sports.title: Robert Garcia Accuses Jaron Ennis Of Targeting Injured Josh Kelly To Avoid Vergil Ortiz Jr.
Sports.content:
“If Boots decides to fight Kelly and take advantage of Kelly being cut and everything, then that’s kind of showing me that you really don’t want to fight Virgil,” Robert said to Sean Zittel. “The fighter will probably do it because he’s a fighter. He’s a warrior, and he’ll probably get the biggest payday in his career, and he could lose to anybody else because, let’s be real, Kelly might not be the best in the division. So, they’re going after him to take advantage of that opportunity to get another belt under his belt.”

The veteran trainer dismissed any suggestion that his fighter needs an interim bout before pursuing the division’s biggest name. Ortiz is already back in camp. He said the former interim champion wants Ennis next.

“We don’t need a tuneup. We want to go straight into Boots,” Garcia said. “If Boots decides to go after him and take advantage of that big old cut, then that’s the way they’re going to do it. I can’t force them either.”

Ennis has repeatedly spoken about adding more world titles, with Kelly and WBC champion Sebastian Fundora mentioned as possible opponents. Garcia rejected that explanation, insisting the larger fight sits across the ring.

“No, that’s a lie. He doesn’t want to fight Virgil,” Garcia said. “The fight against Virgil is three times bigger when it comes to his payday, to a meaningful fight. Nobody’s going to care because you beat Kelly or you beat Virgil. A win over somebody like Virgil means a lot more than Josh Kelly.”

Asked why he believes Ortiz wins the matchup, Garcia offered a brief reply.

“Because I know he beats him,” Garcia said. “I know he beat him.”

Sports.title: Jose Valenzuela Calls For William Zepeda Title Fight
Sports.content:
“Felicidades por la victoria. Sin duda, es otra gran pelea que me encantaría hacer. Ojalá algún día podamos compartir el ring,” Valenzuela wrote on X. Translated, Valenzuela said: “Congratulations on the victory. Without a doubt, it’s another great fight that I’d love to make. Hopefully one day we can share the ring.”

Fresh off his second-round knockout of a ring-rusty Edwin De Los Santos on June 28, Valenzuela (16-3, 10 KOs) is trying to turn that performance into another title opportunity. Before calling for Zepeda, he repeatedly called out fellow Zuffa fighter and WBO light welterweight champion Shakur Stevenson, but those public challenges gained little attention.

Matching Valenzuela with Zepeda presents a different challenge.

Zepeda is promoted by Golden Boy Promotions and competes on DAZN, while Valenzuela is now aligned with Zuffa Boxing and fights on Paramount+. Crossing promotional lines and television platforms is possible, but it usually requires a matchup with significant commercial value.

Unless one side is willing to bridge that promotional divide, Valenzuela may have to keep looking in-house for his next opportunity while Zepeda pursues bigger names at lightweight. Neither promotion has shown interest in working together yet.

Ghana News.title: Nearly half of Africans consider emigrating as jobs, poverty drive migration — Afrobarometer
Ghana News.content:
Nearly one out of every two Africans has considered leaving their country in search of better opportunities, with unemployment and poverty emerging as the biggest factors driving migration across the continent, according to the latest Afrobarometer African Insights 2026 report.

The report, titled ‘Beyond Borders: Citizen Perspectives on a Shifting Global Order,’ indicates that 45 per cent of Africans have at some point contemplated emigrating, while 25 per cent say they have thought about relocating abroad "a lot."

The findings represent a 40 per cent increase in migration aspirations compared with surveys conducted between 2016 and 2018, highlighting growing economic pressures confronting many households across Africa.

The report is based on Round 10 Afrobarometer surveys conducted in 38 African countries during 2024 and 2025, providing one of the continent's most comprehensive assessments of citizens' views on migration, governance, trade and international relations.

Economic pressures

According to the report, economic considerations overwhelmingly dominate migration decisions.

Half (50 per cent) of prospective migrants cited the search for employment as their principal reason for wanting to relocate, while 29 per cent said they would leave to escape poverty and improve their standard of living.

The study found that migration aspirations are strongest among young people and those with higher levels of education, reflecting concerns over limited employment opportunities despite increasing educational attainment across many African countries.

Changing migration destinations

The report also points to a significant shift in where Africans hope to migrate.

Whereas previous surveys showed many Africans preferred moving within the continent, that trend appears to be changing.

The proportion of potential migrants who would rather relocate to another African country has declined sharply from 36 per cent in 2016-2018 to 26 per cent in the latest survey, suggesting that increasing numbers are now looking beyond Africa for economic opportunities.

The report says the changing pattern reflects evolving perceptions about where better employment prospects and improved living conditions can be found.

Support for free movement

Despite the growing desire to emigrate, Africans generally remain supportive of regional integration and the free movement of people.

A modest majority (56 per cent) support freer cross-border movement across the continent, underscoring continued backing for initiatives aimed at strengthening regional mobility and integration.

However, many respondents believe that crossing African borders remains difficult in practice.

Nearly two-thirds (63 per cent) said travelling between African countries is challenging because of administrative, legal and logistical barriers.

The findings suggest that while many citizens embrace the principle of continental mobility, they believe implementation remains far from seamless.

Mixed attitudes toward immigration

The survey also reveals nuanced public attitudes toward immigration.

On the social and cultural front, Africans generally display openness toward foreigners, with 77 per cent saying they would either welcome immigrants as neighbours or would not mind living next to them.

However, attitudes become more cautious when immigration is viewed through an economic lens.

Respondents were evenly divided over whether immigrants benefit or harm national economies.

In addition, 64 per cent said they would prefer their countries to admit fewer—or no—foreign job seekers, while 70 per cent expressed similar preferences regarding refugees.

Policy implications

The report suggests that Africa's growing migration ambitions reflect persistent concerns about youth unemployment, limited economic opportunities and poverty, even as governments pursue deeper regional integration through initiatives such as the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

It notes that although Africans broadly endorse freedom of movement across borders, policymakers must simultaneously address the economic conditions pushing citizens to seek opportunities abroad while managing public concerns over immigration, labour markets and refugee inflows.

The findings underscore the importance of creating jobs, expanding economic opportunities and strengthening regional cooperation if African countries are to retain skilled young people and harness their potential for long-term development.

Ghana News.title: Nations FC drawn against FC Diarra in CAF Confederation Cup debut
Ghana News.content:
MTN FA Cup champions Nations FC have been drawn against Malian side FC Diarra in the first preliminary round of the 2026/27 CAF Confederation Cup.

The first leg is scheduled to be played between September 4 and 6, with the return leg taking place from September 11 to 13.

Nations FC, should they progress, will face the winner of the tie between Niger's AS Zam and Burkina Faso's ASKO de Kara in the second preliminary round.

The upcoming campaign marks a historic milestone for Nations FC, as it will be the club's first-ever appearance in a CAF-sanctioned competition. The Abrankese-based side secured qualification after lifting the 2025/26 MTN FA Cup, earning the right to represent Ghana on the continental stage.

Ghana News.title: Osei-Asare urges Mahama to review Cocoa Board Bill, warns against misuse of parliamentary majority
Ghana News.content:
Former Deputy Finance Minister and Member of Parliament for Atiwa East, Abena Osei Asare, has urged President John Dramani Mahama to use the government’s two-thirds majority in Parliament responsibly, calling for a review of the Cocoa Board Amendment Bill, which he says could affect the rights and livelihoods of cocoa farmers.

Abena Osei-Asare has appealed to President Mahama to reconsider aspects of the Cocoa Board Amendment Bill, warning that the government’s two-thirds majority in Parliament must be used to serve the interests of Ghanaians and not to impose decisions that could negatively affect citizens.

Speaking at the "Democracy Under Attack" demonstration on August 6, Osei-Asare acknowledged that the current parliamentary situation, where one party holds a two-thirds majority, is unprecedented and was not anticipated by the framers of Ghana’s Constitution.

"It is true that the people of Ghana have given one party two-thirds. It is something the Constitution never ever envisaged would happen. But yes, it has happened," she said.

She, however, stressed that such power comes with responsibility and must be exercised carefully for the benefit of the wider population.

"So, we expect them to use this and use it properly to the benefit of the larger nation and not abuse this. That's all we are asking," she added.

Osei-Asare raised concerns about the recently passed Cocoa Board Amendment Bill, particularly provisions he says require cocoa farmers to seek approval from the Ghana Cocoa Board before changing the use of their cocoa farms.

She questioned whether citizens should be restricted from making decisions about their own properties without government permission.

"Mr President, come again. We can amend this law," she appealed.

The former minister urged President Mahama to follow the example of the recent amendment of the tribunal bill, which he said was revised after concerns were raised.

"Remember, recently, the tribunal bill was amended again, even though it had been passed not long ago. So come back, look at this again, and come back and let's amend this," she said.

According to Osei-Asare, the current provision could amount to government taking control over private properties and livelihoods without adequate consideration for citizens’ rights.

She argued that a cocoa farmer should not be considered to have committed an offence simply because they decide to change the use of their land.

"If today I want to change the use of my land from, say, a cocoa farm to something else, and I don't come and seek permission from you, it is illegal and I have committed a wrong?" she questioned.

Osei-Asare directly appealed to the President to listen to concerns surrounding the legislation, reminding him that the two-thirds majority in Parliament was given by Ghanaians for a specific purpose.

"Mr President, listen to us because remember you have the two-thirds majority in Parliament, and I'm sure the people of Ghana gave it to you for a purpose," she said.

He urged the government to use its parliamentary strength to promote national development, protect citizens’ interests and strengthen democracy.

"Let's not abuse this. Use this right for the building of the nation. That's all we are asking for," Osei-Asare concluded.

Ghana News.title: Government’s galamsey fight would make fallen helicopter crash victims proud  – Paa Kwesi Schandorf
Ghana News.content:
The eight state officials who lost their lives in last year's helicopter crash would be proud of the government's efforts to combat illegal mining if they were alive today, the spokesperson for the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, Paa Kwesi Schandorf, has said.

Speaking on JoyPrime as the nation marked one year since the August 6, 2025, tragedy, Mr Schandorf said the government's initiatives against galamsey represent the most meaningful way to honour the memory of the deceased.

"Absolutely yes. If the fallen heroes were alive today, they would be proud of government's effort in the galamsey fight," he said.

Mr Schandorf maintained that the best tribute to the victims was not only to remember them through commemorative events but to sustain a determined and effective campaign against illegal mining.

"The best tribute we can pay to their memories is to mount a competent fight and that's precisely what we've done so far," he added.

The eight officials, including Defence Minister Dr Edward Kofi Omane-Boamah and Agriculture Minister Dr Ibrahim Murtala Mohammed, died when a Ghana Air Force Z9 helicopter crashed at Adansi Sikaman in the Ashanti Region on August 6, 2025, while travelling to Obuasi in connection with the government's anti-galamsey operations.

The anniversary has been marked by a national inter-faith memorial service and renewed reflections on the country's progress in tackling illegal mining.

Ghana News.title: DR Congo begins Ebola and cholera screening for 255 passengers after Congo River boat incident
Ghana News.content:
Congolese authorities are carrying out Ebola and cholera screening for all 255 passengers aboard a boat intercepted on the Congo River.

The Yingfeng 2 - operated by a Chinese company - was halted near Bende Bende port, some 65km (40 miles) upstream from the capital, Kinshasa.

Health Minister Roger Kamba said screening was being carried out as a precautionary measure after a passenger with fever and diarrhoea, who had got off at an earlier stop, had died in hospital. A further two adults, a three-year-old child and a newborn have also died.

Teams from the health ministry and the World Health Organization (WHO) have boarded the boat and set up a mobile lab to conduct tests.

"For now, no-one has tested positive, and it is likely no one will be positive after 21 days of incubation has elapsed," Kamba told reporters.

The vessel departed Kisangani, DR Congo's third largest city, about two weeks ago, the BBC understands.

Ebola cases have recently been reported there, with at least four deaths.

Kamba added there had been no Ebola cases in Mongala Province - where the passenger who died disembarked - contrary to earlier reports.

The boat travelled more than 1,700km downstream towards Kinshasa before being intercepted.

Security services have been instructed to quarantine the Yingfeng 2 offshore in line with WHO standards to prevent potential spread of the virus into the capital. Public health teams remain on standby to act once the boat is secured.

The country has been grappling with its 17th Ebola outbreak since May 15. It has been caused by the rare Bundibugyo species of the virus, which had not been seen for more than a decade.

There are no drug treatments that specifically target Bundibugyo, nor does it have a vaccine, although the first human trials for one are currently under way in the UK.

Three months since the outbreak was declared, infections and deaths continue to rise.

Official figures show that there have been 3,973 confirmed cases and 1,801 deaths - the second deadliest Ebola outbreak.

There are currently more than 17,000 people under monitoring after coming into contact with Ebola cases, 674 patients in isolation or treatment across five provinces, and 776 recoveries, according to authorities.

In Kinshasa, preparations for a possible Bundibugyo response are intensifying, with surveillance and rapid-response capacity being reinforced at Maluku, the city's main entry point.

Officials have reiterated that the measures are precautionary, but they underline the gravity of the situation.

Ghana News.title: NPP presents petition to Supreme Court, Jubilee House over alleged arbitrary arrests, selective justice
Ghana News.content:
The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has presented a petition to the Supreme Court and the presidency, accusing the Mahama administration of undermining Ghana's democracy through what it describes as arbitrary arrests, intimidation of political opponents and selective justice.

The party first marched to the Supreme Court, where it presented a petition expressing concerns about what it described as growing threats to judicial independence and the rule of law.

It subsequently proceeded to the Jubilee House to deliver a second petition to the presidency.

The petition was presented at Jubilee House by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin at the end of the party's 'Democracy Under Attack' demonstration.

The presentation was initially delayed after the NPP objected to the level of government representation at the ceremony. Party leaders argued that it was disrespectful for the presidency to nominate only Presidential Staffer, Nana Yaa Jantuah, to receive the petition, despite the presence of senior NPP officials, including the Minority Leader, the party's General Secretary and the Chief of Staff to the party's flagbearer.

"We have selected our democracy. Without prejudice to your person, to nominate only you to come amounts to disrespecting us as a political party," Afenyo-Markin told Nana Yaa Jantuah.

He, however, said the party would proceed with the presentation in the interest of democracy, with the NPP's Deputy National Youth Organiser presenting the petition on behalf of the party.

In his remarks, Mr Afenyo-Markin urged the government to remember that no political party remains in power indefinitely and warned against using state institutions to target political opponents.

He accused the government of abandoning its campaign promises on job creation, the 24-hour economy, electricity tariffs and cocoa prices while focusing instead on intimidating critics.

He questioned the imprisonment of NPP Ashanti Regional Chairman Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, arguing that the circumstances of his conviction raise concerns.

The Minority Leader also criticised the removal of the former Chief Justice, alleging that it formed part of an attempt to influence the judiciary. He further accused the government of directing judicial processes during the courts' vacation period to hear cases involving NPP members.

Mr Afenyo-Markin also criticised the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO), alleging that the agency imposes excessive bail conditions on opposition figures by demanding properties worth millions of cedis before granting bail.

He cautioned the government against assuming it would remain in power permanently, saying the NPP could return to office after the 2028 general election.

Referring to what he said was an IMF report indicating losses of GH¢9.6 billion in GoldBod transactions, he argued that allegations of financial impropriety against public institutions should remind the government that it could also face scrutiny in the future.

"We are saying democracy is under attack, and let us all take steps as players in the governance structure to correct it and make Ghana a better place," he said.

Nana Yaa Jantuah received the petition on behalf of the government.

Ghana News.title: US Senate committee votes to hold Fauci in contempt over Covid hearing
Ghana News.content:
A US Senate committee has voted to hold former top health official Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress after he refused to answer questions during a hearing focused on his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.

The vote - which fell along party lines - means that the committee will refer the case to the justice department for potential prosecution for failing to comply with a congressional subpoena.

It is unclear if the department will do so.

Fauci invoked his constitutional right against self-incrimination more than 100 times during his testimony last week, drawing the ire of Republican lawmakers.

Former President Joe Biden gave Fauci a pre-emptive pardon on his last day in office in 2025, protecting him from federal prosecution for his actions between 2014 and 2025.

Fauci could, however, still face charges for anything after that date, including contempt of Congress.

Additionally, he could still be subject to state or local charges that are not covered by the pardon.

"The chair directed Anthony Fauci to answer. He refused," Kentucky Republican Rand Paul said ahead of the vote. "That is what we are voting on today — not his opinions, not his policies, not anything he said from the podium six years ago. "

"We are voting on whether a witness who has received the benefit of a federal pardon can be ordered by this committee to answer questions and then defy that order without consequence," he added.

Ghana News.title: Empowering grassroots women for clean energy and Ghana’s sustainable future
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s transition to clean energy is often discussed in terms of renewable electricity, solar power, energy infrastructure, electric mobility and national energy policy. However, one of the most important aspects of the transition happens at the household and community level, where women make daily decisions about cooking, energy use, livelihoods, waste, agriculture and community well-being.

Clean cooking is arguably the most immediate intersection between gender and energy in Ghana. Women traditionally carry a significant share of household cooking responsibilities. Where households depend on firewood or charcoal, women and girls can spend considerable time sourcing fuel whilst also bearing disproportionate exposure to household air pollution. The impacts extend beyond health to time poverty, education, income generation and participation in community life.

Ghana’s 2026 National Energy Compact acknowledges persistent gender disparities in clean cooking. It reports that female-headed households are more likely to use charcoal for cooking than male-headed households, and that women occupy only about 25% of jobs in public energy utilities.

For Ghana’s clean energy transition to be genuinely just and inclusive, grassroots women must be recognised not only as beneficiaries, but also as entrepreneurs, innovators, educators, community leaders and agents of change.

Empowering grassroots women is not only about creating livelihoods, but it is also about advancing Ghana's development priorities, strengthening communities, building local capacity, fostering inclusion, and accelerating progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Grassroots Women are Key Participants in the Clean Energy Value Chain in Ghana

It is evident that a major opportunity exists for women to shift from simple energy consumers to become key participants in the clean energy value chain. At Wusuta in the North Dayi District of the Volta Region, a remarkable transformation is taking place. Women are turning what was once considered waste (coconut husks) into clean, affordable briquettes, creating a sustainable energy alternative while opening new pathways for economic empowerment.

Powered by the Africa Just Transition Network (AJTN) and the Renewable Energy for Communities Coalition (RE4CC), of which EcoClub 360 is a proud member, this initiative demonstrates the power of placing grassroots women at the heart of Ghana's just energy transition. EcoClub 360 was represented by its Founder and Executive Director, Ms Patience Ahiabor, who joined partners in supporting this community-driven effort.

Globally, development organisations and energy bodies such as Sustainable Energy for All (SEforALL) and the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) recognise women’s crucial contribution to energy transitions.

In Ghana, the opportunity for Wusuta women is not only to simply produce briquettes. It is also a demonstration of how women are contributing to climate and environmental protection by connecting energy transition with climate adaptation, forest conservation, circular economy, biodiversity protection and women’s economic empowerment, which Ghana’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), under the Paris Agreement, explicitly integrate as core components of climate action. Additionally, the women’s traditional knowledge can help researchers, government agencies, development partners, NGOs and private companies design technologies that will contribute to sustainable energy, while creating opportunities to earn sustainable incomes, reducing dependence on conventional fuels, and strengthening the resilience of their families and communities.

Conclusion

Ghana’s clean energy transition will only be truly transformative when the women at the heart of our communities are empowered to actively participate, lead, and benefit. From transforming agricultural waste into clean energy briquettes to championing sustainable livelihoods and protecting local ecosystems, grassroots women’s contributions demonstrate that climate action can begin with solutions rooted in communities.

Our collective responsibility is to ensure that these women have access to skills, finance, technology, markets and decision-making spaces to scale their solutions. The future for Ghana’s clean energy transition should not be built for communities without communities. It must be built with the women who are creating change from the ground up. A just transition must therefore be inclusive, gender-responsive and community-driven. Let us accelerate Ghana’s sustainable energy future by empowering more grassroots women as core leaders in the clean energy sector.

Our Planet Our Future!

Patience Ahiabor

Founder & Executive Director

EcoClub 360

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
