World.title: I’ll quit APC if Tinubu disrespects Catholic bishops, says Orji Kalu
World.content:
Former Abia State Governor and Senator representing Abia North, Orji Kalu, has said he would resign from the All Progressives Congress (APC) if President Bola Tinubu ever disrespects Catholic bishops or the Catholic Church.

Mr Kalu made the declaration on Wednesday during an appearance on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme, where he defended the president against allegations that he had insulted the Catholic Church following recent exchanges between the Presidency and Catholic leaders over the state of the nation.

The senator dismissed claims that President Tinubu was hostile to the Catholic Church, insisting that the president had maintained a cordial relationship with the church and respected its role in national discourse.

According to him, the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) has historically served as the conscience of the nation by speaking on issues affecting Nigerians, regardless of the government in power.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“President Tinubu did not insult the Catholic Church. This is not the first time the Catholic Church will visit the president. In every country—from the Democratic Republic of Congo to Angola, South Africa and elsewhere—the Catholic Church and other churches are the conscience of the country,” Mr Kalu said.

He noted that the CBCN had consistently issued statements on the state of the nation, including during military rule, stressing that such interventions should not be interpreted as hostility towards any administration.

“I do not see what Cardinal Onaiyekan said that was wrong. During the military era, the Catholic Bishops’ Conference met every year and expressed its opinion about the state of the nation,” he said.

Mr Kalu added that President Tinubu was not a threat to the Catholic community, arguing that the president had always maintained a constructive relationship with church leaders.

“To me, Tinubu is not a threat to the Catholic community. The president has a good relationship with the Catholic Church. Any time they ask for his opinion, he gives it. What politicians cannot tell a president, a Catholic bishop can say,” he said.

The senator also rejected suggestions that Mr Tinubu intended to undermine Nigeria’s democratic process, saying the president remained committed to conducting credible elections.

“If you heard him well, he said there would be a free and fair election and that he would not intimidate anyone. Any day the president disrespects Catholic bishops, I will resign from the APC,” he said.

His comments come amid controversy sparked by recent remarks by Archbishop Emeritus of Abuja, John Onaiyekan, a cardinal, who raised concerns about worsening economic hardship and insecurity during an engagement with President Tinubu. The response by some presidential media aides drew criticism from sections of the public, with some describing their remarks as disrespectful to both the cardinal and the Catholic Church.

2027 election

Speaking on the 2027 general election, Mr Kalu expressed confidence that President Tinubu would secure a second term in office, arguing that the administration’s achievements had not been adequately communicated to Nigerians.

According to him, the APC had failed to effectively publicise the government’s performance in infrastructure, security and economic reforms.

“A lot has been done by this government. We simply have not marketed this government well enough,” he said.

Assessing the administration’s performance, Mr Kalu said President Tinubu had achieved about 65 per cent of his objectives since assuming office and predicted that the rating would improve in the coming months.

“By September or October, that performance will be close to 70 per cent,” he said.

“That restriction order does not mean that all the accounts of Osun State have been frozen. It is just a targeted restriction on one account of the Osun State Government,” he said.

The EFCC spokesperson said investigators observed multiple transfers from the account to several corporate entities within a short period, prompting the intervention.

He argued that failing to act would have amounted to neglect of the commission’s statutory responsibility to safeguard public funds.

“If we don’t take that step and funds are eventually looted, Nigerians will ask where the EFCC was when those funds were being moved,” he said.

World.title: Temitope Osoba’s family denies reports on circumstances of her death
World.content:
The family of Temitope Osoba has dismissed reports circulating on social media and some online platforms concerning the circumstances surrounding her death, describing them as false, speculative and unauthorised.

In an official statement posted on her Instagram page, the family expressed sadness over what it described as the spread of unverified information at a difficult period for her loved ones.

The family urged members of the public to disregard the reports and refrain from sharing content that could further deepen their grief.

“On behalf of the family and loved ones of Temitope Osoba, we are deeply saddened by the spread of false and unverified reports concerning the passing of our beloved,” the statement read.

The family stated that the various claims circulating about her death were “false, speculative, and entirely unauthorized,” stressing that no official information had been released on the matter.

“We respectfully urge the public to refrain from sharing or promoting misinformation that only adds to the pain our family is already enduring,” it added.

The family appealed for privacy and understanding, saying they needed time to mourn without the added burden of rumours and sensational reports.

It assured the public and the media that any information the family chooses to release would be communicated through official channels and authorised representatives.

“We ask the public and members of the media to rely solely on those official statements and to disregard all unverified reports,” the statement added.

The family of Awonuga/Osoba thanked members of the public for their prayers, love and support, while appealing for respect for Temitope Osoba’s memory and the family’s privacy during the mourning period.

World.title: TVET Probe: Reps give Education minister Sept 17 deadline, demand records
World.content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives Committee on Polytechnic and Higher Technical Education has directed the Federal Ministry of Education to submit all records relating to the implementation of the Federal Government’s Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programme by August 18, 2026.

The committee also issued a final invitation to the Minister of Education, directing him to personally appear before lawmakers on September 17, 2026, to explain the implementation of the programme and address concerns raised during the ongoing investigation.

The resolutions were reached on Thursday during an investigative hearing at the National Assembly, where lawmakers expressed displeasure over the minister’s repeated failure to honour invitations or send a representative to appear before the committee.

Chairman of the committee, Hon. Fuad Kayode Laguda, said the panel had been requesting relevant information on the TVET programme since January 30, 2025, but the ministry had yet to provide the requested documents.

According to him, the latest invitation to the ministry was issued on July 30, 2026, but neither the minister nor any representative appeared before the committee.

“We have written several correspondences starting from January 30, 2025, seeking information on the activities of Technical Vocational Education Training being implemented by the government. The last invitation was on July 30, but the minister is not here and no representative was sent to the committee,” Laguda said.

He said the committee had maintained a cordial relationship with the ministry in the past, describing the minister’s absence as unexpected and contrary to the principles of legislative oversight.

Laguda reminded the ministry that Sections 88 and 89 of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) empower the National Assembly to investigate the activities of ministries, departments and agencies in the discharge of their responsibilities.

The minister’s absence attracted criticism from members of the committee, with Hon. Rabiu Yusuf accusing him of showing “a high level of disrespect” to the legislature.

“This communication was neither acknowledged nor responded to. Information requested by the committee was not provided. We can rightly assume that there is a high level of disrespect to the institution of the legislative body by the executive, particularly the Minister of Education.

“I think it is high time for us to pass a vote of no confidence on the minister,” Yusuf said.

Another member of the committee, Hon. Bayo Adepoju, described the development as “a direct affront to Parliament,” insisting that Nigerians deserved transparency on the implementation of the programme.

“This is rude, unacceptable, and something that should not happen in a democracy. We are constitutionally empowered to conduct oversight on ministries, departments and agencies.

“Nobody is above Parliament. After six letters to the ministry, the minister has still failed to appear. Nigerians deserve to know how this programme is being implemented,” he said.

Although some lawmakers called for a vote of no confidence against the minister, the committee resolved to give him another opportunity to appear before considering any further action.

Hon. Paul Kalejaiye and other members appealed for restraint, urging the committee to issue a final invitation and allow the minister to respond.

“This is the first time we are making a public pronouncement on him. We should give the honourable minister another chance by issuing him an ultimatum and fixing a date to appear before this committee before we pass a vote of no confidence,” Kalejaiye said.

Laguda also expressed belief that the minister’s absence might have been due to unforeseen circumstances.

“I’ve had engagements with the minister in the past. I don’t see him as someone who would deliberately do this. Maybe there are reasons for it, but whatever is responsible, this definitely should not happen again,” he said.

The committee subsequently directed the Ministry of Education to submit all documents and information relating to the TVET programme, from inception to date, to its secretariat on or before August 18, 2026.

“We are using this platform to request from the ministry to supply the committee with the necessary information that has been requested from inception to date. The submission of this information should be made available to the secretariat by the 18th of August,” Laguda said.

He added that the committee would reconvene with the minister and officials of the ministry on September 17, 2026, expressing hope that the minister would appear in person.

The committee said the requested documents would enable lawmakers to properly assess the implementation of the TVET programme and ensure accountability in the management of public funds allocated to technical and vocational education.

World.title: State Police: IGP Disu tasks officers on objective national debate, public enlightenment
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has urged officers and men of the Nigeria Police Force to take an active role in shaping the national conversation on the proposed establishment of State Police through informed engagement, objective analysis and public enlightenment.

Disu gave the charge on Thursday at a one-day workshop on State Police organised by the Nigeria Police Institute at the Nigeria Police Resource Centre, Abuja.

The IGP described the workshop as a timely platform for critical reflection on one of Nigeria’s most significant security policy debates, stressing the need for police personnel to be well-informed as discussions on the proposed reform continue across the country.

He said, “As discussions on the creation of State Police continue to gain momentum across the country, members of the Nigeria Police Force must remain well-informed and contribute constructively to the ongoing discourse.

“The workshop provides an opportunity for participants to examine the implications of State Police, raise pertinent questions, address legitimate concerns and make meaningful contributions that would enrich national policy discussions on policing and internal security.”

Disu urged participants to engage actively and objectively during the deliberations, stressing that the knowledge acquired should extend beyond the workshop.

He charged the officers to return to their respective commands and formations to share the knowledge gained with colleagues, noting that such engagement would promote better understanding of State Police, dispel misconceptions and reduce concerns often associated with major institutional reforms.

The IGP emphasised that informed dialogue and continuous professional engagement were essential to preparing officers for possible changes in Nigeria’s policing architecture.

He commended the Nigeria Police Institute for organising the workshop, expressing confidence that the discussions would contribute meaningfully to the ongoing national conversation on policing reforms.

Disu reaffirmed his commitment to building a professional, informed and forward-looking police force capable of enhancing national security and public safety.

In his remarks, the Director-General of the Nigeria Police Institute, Prof. Olu Ogunshakin, commended the IGP for constituting the Nigeria Police Force Steering Committee on State Police.

Ogunshakin noted that several recommendations of the committee had been reflected in the proposed State Police framework, describing its work as a significant contribution to the ongoing policing reform process.

He said the workshop was part of broader efforts by the Nigeria Police Force to prepare personnel for emerging policing reforms while sustaining professionalism, operational effectiveness and public confidence in law enforcement.

World.title: Christian elders urge FG to see bishops’ comments as sincere counsel, not opposition
World.content:
By Chimaobi Nwaiwu

NNEWI — The Christian Elders and Professionals Consultative Council of Nigeria (CEPCCN) has urged the Federal Government to view the observations made by the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) during their recent visit to President Bola Tinubu as sincere counsel aimed at strengthening leadership rather than partisan opposition.

The council also called for constructive engagement between the government and faith-based institutions, describing such interaction as essential for promoting national peace, justice, good governance and sustainable development.

In a statement signed by its National Chairman, His Lordship Bishop Justice Alpha Ikpeama, CEPCCN said the call had become necessary following the public debate that trailed the bishops’ meeting with the President and subsequent reactions from government officials.

The statement titled, “A Respectful Appeal for Constructive Engagement Between Government and the Church,” emphasised the need for mutual respect and open dialogue between the government and religious institutions.

CEPCCN said: “The Christian Elders and Professionals Consultative Council of Nigeria (CEPCCN) has followed with keen interest the recent public discourse arising from observations made by Christian leaders concerning the state of the nation and the responses from government representatives.

“As a non-partisan Christian consultative, advisory and policy institution, CEPCCN believes that constructive engagement between government and faith-based institutions is essential for promoting national peace, justice, good governance and sustainable development.”

The council noted that the Church has over the years played a significant role in nation-building through education, healthcare delivery, humanitarian interventions, moral instruction, peace-building and community development.

It added that Christian leaders have the responsibility to raise concerns on issues affecting Nigerians, stressing that such interventions should be regarded as constructive civic engagement rather than political opposition.

“Such contributions are consistent with the constitutional freedoms of expression, association and religion and should be viewed as constructive civic engagement, rather than partisan opposition,” the statement added.

The group recalled that sincere advice strengthens leadership, citing the biblical admonition that “faithful are the wounds of a friend,” and urged leaders to embrace honest counsel when offered in good faith.

CEPCCN encouraged the Federal Government to continue engaging religious institutions, professional bodies, civil society organisations and other stakeholders with openness and willingness to listen.

“Constructive criticism should not automatically be interpreted as hostility but appreciated as an opportunity to strengthen public policy, improve governance and deepen public confidence,” it said.

The council, however, urged religious leaders to ensure that their interventions remain responsible, objective and guided by the principles of truth, justice, compassion, national unity and the common good.

It also called for renewed efforts by government to address critical national challenges, including insecurity, economic hardship, unemployment, inflation, food insecurity, healthcare and education.

Ahead of the 2027 general elections, CEPCCN appealed to political leaders, government institutions, traditional rulers, professional bodies, civil society organisations, the media and citizens to place national interest above partisan considerations.

The council stressed that democracy thrives where there is accountability, institutional independence and responsible citizen participation.

“Dialogue should prevail over confrontation, consultation over suspicion, and statesmanship over division,” it said.

CEPCCN reaffirmed that mutual respect between government and faith-based institutions would promote national stability, public trust and social cohesion, urging all stakeholders to work together towards building a peaceful, just and prosperous Nigeria.

World.title: Don’t let green energy become new colonialism, ITUC-Africa warns
World.content:
…Says energy revolution must create jobs, not just profits

By Victor Ahiuma-Young

Nairobi : Organised Labour through the International Trade Union Confederation, ITUC-Africa has warned that Africa risks replacing one form of colonial exploitation with another unless it takes control of its energy transition.



According ITUC-Africa, the continent’s vast renewable energy resources and critical minerals must drive industrialisation, job creation and economic transformation instead of enriching foreign interests.



Speaking at the New Energy for Africa 11 Convening:? African Workers’ Contributions to Energy Sovereignty, Green Industrialization, and a Common African for COP31, in Nairobi, Kenya, ITUC-Africa Deputy President Rose Omamo urged African governments, climate negotiators and development partners to ensure that the shift to clean energy delivers decent jobs, strengthens public energy systems and gives African countries greater control over their natural resources.



Omamo said the continent should approach the global green transition with a united position ahead of the COP31 climate summit, warning that expanding electricity access alone would not solve Africa’s development challenges unless investments also created industries, added value to local minerals and improved the livelihoods of ordinary citizens.



According to her, “We welcome efforts to address the energy crisis on our continent. More than 600 million Africans still live without electricity, and this situation cannot be allowed to continue.



“However, expanding electricity access is not enough on its own. We must ask who will own the new energy infrastructure, who will finance it and who will benefit from it. We must ask whether these investments will strengthen public energy systems, support African industries and create decent jobs.



“Africa’s success cannot be measured only by the number of new electricity connections or the amount of energy generated. It must also be measured by the jobs created, the industries developed, the communities connected and the improvements made in the lives of ordinary people.



Turning to the growing international demand for Africa’s critical minerals, Omamo warned against repeating the continent’s historical pattern of exporting raw materials while importing expensive finished products.



She said: “There is also growing global competition for Africa’s critical minerals, including cobalt, lithium, copper, graphite and rare earths. These resources are important for renewable energy technologies, electric vehicles and battery storage.



“Africa must not repeat the experience of exporting raw materials and later importing expensive finished products. Our minerals must support local processing, manufacturing, skills development and decent employment. They must contribute to peace and development instead of exploitation, displacement, conflict and violations of workers’ rights.”



Omamo said workers must play a central role in shaping Africa’s transition to clean energy instead of being consulted only after major investment decisions had already been made.



“For ITUC-Africa, workers must be at the centre of the energy transition. They cannot be treated as observers or invited only after policies and investment decisions have been finalised.”



She noted that “the transition must protect workers while creating opportunities for young people, women and those in the informal economy.



“A just transition is ultimately about people. It is about workers having secure jobs, fair wages, social protection and a voice in decisions that affect their lives. It is about ensuring that communities dependent on existing industries are supported through change. It is also about creating new opportunities without weakening labour rights or increasing insecure work.”



Calling for stronger engagement with governments, the African Union and climate negotiators, Omamo urged delegates to develop a common African trade union position ahead of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey.

“Our task is to ensure that Africa’s energy transition does not reproduce the inequalities of the past under a green name.



“It must help Africa develop its own industries. It must create decent jobs. It must improve access to affordable energy. It must protect workers and communities. It must strengthen public services. It must give African countries greater control over their resources and their development choices”, ITUC-Africa Deputy President, noted.



She added by urging “African leaders to seize the opportunity presented by the global energy transition. The energy transition is already happening. The important question is whether Africa will simply provide raw materials for the transition of other regions, or whether we will use this opportunity to transform our own economies and improve the lives of our people.”

World.title: Barcelona close in on Rodri after midfielder rejects Real Madrid
World.content:
Spain’s midfielder #16 Rodri kisses the Golden Ball Award during the award ceremony of the 2026 World Cup football tournament final match between Spain and Argentina at the New York/New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford on July 19, 2026. (Photo by Odd ANDERSEN / AFP)

Manchester City and Spain midfielder Rodri has reportedly given the green light to a move to Barcelona this summer, in a major development in the transfer race for the 30-year-old.

According to journalist Gerard Romero of Jijantes FC, Rodri has said ‘yes’ to joining the Catalan giants, paving the way for Barcelona to begin negotiations to complete the transfer.

Rodri had been strongly linked with a move to Real Madrid, with the Spanish giants reportedly having agreed personal terms with the midfielder and holding discussions with Manchester City over a potential deal.

However, delays in reaching an agreement are understood to have opened the door for Barcelona, who have moved quickly and now appear to have secured a verbal affirmation from the 2026 FIFA World Cup winner.

Barcelona can now turn their attention towards negotiating the finer details of a potential transfer for the former Ballon d’Or winner.

World.title: Diomande joins Real Madrid as club’s most expensive player [Top 5]
World.content:
Real Madrid have reached an agreement with RB Leipzig for Ivorian winger Yan Diomande, with the player set to move to the Santiago Bernabéu this summer.

According to Marca, both clubs finalised the agreement on Thursday morning, with Diomande already travelling to Madrid to undergo his medical examination.

Real Madrid could officially announce the signing on Thursday, with the transfer set to become the most expensive in the club’s history.

The Spanish giants are expected to pay €125 million for the 19-year-old, with a further €10m to €15m potentially payable in add-ons.

The deal would take Real Madrid’s spending on new arrivals this summer to more than €300 million, with the club also reportedly spending €55 million on Marc Cucurella, €25 million on Carlos Espai and €20 million on Denzel Dumfries.

Ibrahima Konaté and Bernardo Silva, meanwhile, joined the club on free transfers.

Real Madrid have also generated substantial revenue from player sales, particularly from academy graduates, with total income from such departures reportedly reaching €184.5 million.

Diomande’s arrival is not expected to affect Real Madrid’s ongoing negotiations with Brazilian forward Vinicius Junior, according to Marca.

Vinicius has entered the final stages of his current contract, which expires at the end of next season, while Arsenal have reportedly shown strong interest in the forward.

Yan Diomande – €135m (2026) Jude Bellingham – €127m (2023) Eden Hazard – €121m (2019) Gareth Bale – €101m (2013) Cristiano Ronaldo – €94m (2009)

World.title: Davido-Uzodimma : Imo aide says comment was personal, not Governor’s position
World.content:
Gov Hope Uzodimma of Imo State

The Senior Special Assistant to the Imo State Governor on Electronic and Creative Media, Ambrose Nwaogwugwu, has clarified that a statement circulating online regarding Afrobeats star, David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, was his personal opinion and not that of Governor Hope Uzodimma.

Nwaogwugwu, in a statement issued on Thursday, said the statement was authored by him in his capacity as a private citizen commenting on a topical national issue, and should not have been attributed to the Imo State governor.

He said the attribution had created a wrong impression, urging media platforms and bloggers to correct what he described as a misrepresentation.

“The comments being credited to the Governor by some bloggers are a clear misrepresentation of the facts.

“It is unfortunate that some bloggers chose to attribute the statement to the Governor when it was, in fact, a personal opinion I expressed in my capacity as a private citizen commenting on a topical national issue,” Nwaogwugwu stated.

He explained that official statements on behalf of Governor Uzodimma are issued by the Chief Press Secretary, while the Imo State Commissioner for Information speaks for the state government, except where other officials are expressly authorised.

The clarification followed reports linking the governor to comments on Davido’s recent call for a free and fair governorship election in Osun State.

Davido had, during a press conference on Wednesday, appealed to an unnamed politician from Imo State to allow the people of Osun to freely choose their preferred candidate in the August 15 governorship election.

The singer, while alleging concerns over possible interference in the poll, urged political actors to promote peace and respect the will of voters.

Reacting to the development, Nwaogwugwu said his response was made in his personal capacity and did not represent the position of Governor Uzodimma or the Imo State Government.

He urged media practitioners to exercise caution in attributing comments to public officials, stressing the need for accuracy, fairness and responsible journalism.

“It is therefore inappropriate to attribute a harmless personal opinion that I authored in my personal capacity to the Governor, particularly when the statement did not indicate that I was speaking on his behalf,” he added.

Nwaogwugwu subsequently called on media platforms that published the report to make corrections in order to properly reflect the source and context of the statement.

World.title: Shettima Begins Two-Week Leave Thursday
World.content:
* Pledges renewed commitment to national service

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

Vice-President Kashim Shettima on Thursday commenced a two-week leave — his first since assuming office over three years ago.

According to a statement issued by the media aide to the vice-president, Stanley Nkwocha, during the leave, the vice-president will devote time to study, reflect and do intellectual renewal as part of efforts to strengthen his capacity for continued service to the nation.

The leave offers Shettima an opportunity to review the administration’s ongoing programmes, deepen his understanding of emerging national and global policy issues, and prepare for the responsibilities ahead as the Federal Government intensifies the implementation of the Renewed Hope Agenda.

Since assuming office on May 29, 2023, the vice-president, the release stated, has remained actively engaged in the coordination and supervision of several strategic government initiatives, particularly in economic development, food security, humanitarian affairs, digital transformation, job creation and regional cooperation.

He has consistently chaired the monthly National Economic Council (NEC) meeting, which brings together the governors of the 36 states, the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria and other relevant public officials to deliberate on policies affecting the economy and the welfare of Nigerians.

Beyond his responsibilities within the country, Shettima has represented President Bola Tinubu at major international and regional engagements, advancing Nigeria’s position on economic integration, peace and security, climate action, investment and sustainable development.

He remains deeply committed to the ideals of loyalty, duty and service that have defined his role in the administration, as well as to supporting President Tinubu’s efforts to build a more secure, productive and prosperous Nigeria.

The vice-president will return to office at the end of the two-week leave period and resume his official responsibilities with renewed energy and dedication to the service of the nation.

World.title: Tinubu to EFCC: Vacate Court Order Freezing Osun Govt Account
World.content:
.Says he’s deeply embarassed by timing of the anti-graft agency’s action

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu on Thursday directed the Economic and Financial Crimes Commossion (EFCC) to vacate recent court order freezing the bank account of Osun state government.

EFCC had on Wednesday ordered the freezing of Osun state government’s salary account domiciled in First Bank (FBN).

The President, in a seven-paragraph strongly worded release stated that he had to intervene to disabuse the public mind that any government agency was being used to interfere in the August 15, 2026 gubernatorial poll in Osun state, which is some few days away.

According to Tinubu: “Osun State is only a few days away from its gubernatorial election. Therefore, nothing ought to be done to give an impression that the EFCC or indeed any other agency of the federal government is being used to interfere with the election.

“Based on the foregoing premise, I am duty-bound to issue a directive on this issue in consonance with the overriding public interest in preserving public confidence and the integrity, credibility, and fairness of our democratic process.

“Accordingly, I have directed the EFCC to immediately proceed to the court to vacate the order and discontinue whatever action it has instituted against the Osun State Government in this regard.”

The President, who claimed he has not been briefed about the issue, said he’s deeply embarassed by the timing of the action of the anti-graft agency on Osun state.

His words: “I must state that I feel deeply embarrassed not by the EFCC’s exercise of its mandate backed by a court order, but by the timing of the agency’s action. This is so because every action taken by an institution of State, especially at the Federal level, is always credited to me, as the President, even when I may not have had any prior knowledge of the action.”

Tinubu in the release stated, inter alia: “It has come to my notice that the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) obtained a court order on August 5, 2026, freezing the accounts of the Osun State Government. I must state that I feel deeply embarrassed not by the EFCC’s exercise of its mandate backed by a court order, but by the timing of the agency’s action. This is so because every action taken by an institution of State, especially at the Federal level, is always credited to me, as the President, even when I may not have had any prior knowledge of the action.

“Since assuming office, I have consistently maintained that anti-corruption and law enforcement agencies must be allowed to discharge their statutory responsibilities independently, professionally, without fear or favour, or political interference. I have therefore deliberately refrained from directing or interfering in the operational activities of the EFCC or any other investigative or prosecutorial agency because I firmly believe that strong democratic institutions, operating within the confines of the law, are indispensable to democratic good governance and the rule of law.

“As President, I am committed to allowing institutions of State to function and take any action they consider necessary in the interest of proper governance without the need for any prior approval. Indeed, that is why institutions are set up by law with clearly defined powers. While I am yet to be fully apprised of the facts which informed the action of EFCC in approaching the court to obtain the said order freezing the Osun State Government account, I am not in the slightest doubt that the timing of the action of EFCC is inauspicious, and therefore I feel compelled to intervene.

“Osun State is only a few days away from its gubernatorial election. Therefore, nothing ought to be done to give an impression that the EFCC or indeed any other agency of the federal government is being used to interfere with the election.

“Based on the foregoing premise, I am duty-bound to issue a directive on this issue in consonance with the overriding public interest in preserving public confidence and the integrity, credibility, and fairness of our democratic process.

“Accordingly, I have directed the EFCC to immediately proceed to the court to vacate the order and discontinue whatever action it has instituted against the Osun State Government in this regard.

“Long live the Federal Republic of Nigeria.”

World.title: FG Approves Financing Framework to Accelerate Electrification of Health Facilities
World.content:
Yinka Olatunbosun

The Federal Government has approved an institutional reform and financing framework to accelerate the electrification of health facilities nationwide, in a move officials say will bring reliable, 24-hour power to hospitals long hampered by erratic electricity supply.

The decisions were reached at the third meeting of the Inter-Ministerial Steering Committee (IMSC) of the Nigeria Power for Health Initiative (NPHI), a presidential programme jointly coordinated by the Federal Ministries of Power and Health and Social Welfare, which is targeting reliable electricity for at least 30 percent of Nigeria’s health facilities by the end of 2027.

The meeting, chaired by the Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Isiaq Salako and co-chaired by the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, drew top government officials, development partners and members of the Inter-Agency Technical Committee (IATC), which presented the recommendations under consideration.

Speaking at the meeting, Tegbe declared that the initiative must now move from announcements to actual project delivery. Describing the NPHI as one of the Tinubu administration’s flagship programmes, he said the emphasis should shift toward commissioning completed projects that Nigerians can see for themselves, rather than further groundbreaking ceremonies and public messaging.

He emphasized the need for teaching hospitals, state hospitals and primary healthcare centres fully energized, noting that the Rural Electrification Agency has already energized 5 Federal Teaching Hospitals and several other health facilities nationwide. He also tied the initiative directly to patient outcomes, arguing that dependable power would end hospitals’reliance on emergency generators, and pledged that the Ministry would continue to prioritize the initiative’s funding needs while ensuring value for money.

Salako, who disclosed the outcomes of the meeting, said the Steering Committee approved a financing framework to mobilize investment for healthcare electrification, alongside a facility energy management framework requiring participating hospitals to build sustainable systems for managing their energy infrastructure.

He said the committee also cleared eight (8) private sector proposals for further engagement, drawn from about 70 submissions received during the National Healthcare Electrification Investor Matchmaking Week in Lagos. He added that Energy Management Teams are already in place at federal tertiary hospitals, with state governments being encouraged to set up similar structures, and that the initiative will now be institutionalized through dedicated budgetary provisions and a full-time Project Coordination Unit to oversee implementation going forward.

The Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Power, Mahmud Mamman, underscored the stakes for the health sector, noting that uninterrupted electricity is essential for powering critical medical equipment, preserving vaccines, supporting laboratories and strengthening emergency response systems. He described the NPHI as a landmark collaboration bringing together government, development partners and the private sector to tackle one of the health sector’s most pressing infrastructure gaps.

The Nigeria Power for Health Initiative signals the Federal Government’s intent to treat reliable electricity as a pillar of healthcare delivery. As the NPHI moves from framework to delivering projects, it expresses the importance of healthcare reforms in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, where functional healthcare is defined not only by the personnel and equipment within it, but also by the power that keeps them running.

World.title: APCI Urges Schools to Prioritise Student Safety, Launches National Anti-Bullying Week
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

The African Principals Conference Initiative (APCI) has urged schools and education stakeholders to prioritise student safety, well-being and a positive school culture as they prepare for the 2026/2027 academic session.

The call came as the initiative launched a nationwide registration for the 2026 national anti-bullying week and school debates, scheduled to hold in November 9 to 13.

The programme forms part of a broader national strategy under APCI’s Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Federal Ministry of Education to strengthen safeguarding measures and promote safer learning environments across schools nationwide.

The Director-General, Joseph Ayodele, in a statement, explained that the quality of education should no longer be measured solely by examination results or university admission rates, but also by how safe and protected students feel in school.

“The future of education will not be measured only by examination results or university admission rates. It will increasingly be measured by how safe our schools are, how protected our children feel, and how intentionally we build learning environments where every child can flourish emotionally, socially and academically,” he stated.

Ayodele noted that schools with positive cultures consistently record better academic outcomes, higher student engagement, improved teacher morale, lower absenteeism and healthier relationships among students, staff and parents.

Describing school safety as a leadership responsibility, he stressed the need for evidence-based policies, effective safeguarding systems, emotionally intelligent leadership and stronger collaboration among government, educators, parents and communities.

As part of its renewed drive, the initiative also unveiled a three-pronged national school safety framework to be implemented during the 2026/2027 academic session in partnership with the Federal Ministry of Education and state ministries of education.

The framework comprises the national anti-bullying week and school debates, a national school climate baseline assessment scheduled for March 2027 to measure bullying prevalence, emotional well-being and school safety indicators, as well as a school leadership administrative evaluation to assess institutional leadership in areas such as safeguarding compliance, conflict management and student welfare.

The director general commended the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC), led by its Executive Secretary, Dr. Aisha Garba, for supporting the implementation of the Federal Ministry of Education’s national anti-bullying policy.

Ayodele cited UBEC’s participation in the national sensitisation workshop on anti-bullying for Federal Unity Colleges held on July 20, 2026, and its support for school engagement activities during the 2025 national anti-bullying week in Lagos as evidence of its commitment to safe and inclusive learning environments.

According to him, “Findings from its 2023 student well-being and bullying tracking study, conducted jointly with Africa Brands Review, revealed that students exposed to bullying and interpersonal violence are more likely to experience lower academic achievement, increased anxiety, poorer mental health, higher absenteeism and weaker attachment to school.”

The findings, he stated, underscore the growing recognition that school safety is a key determinant of educational performance rather than merely a welfare issue.

He therefore advocated restorative disciplinary practices, social-emotional learning, teacher professional development, counselling services, peer mentoring and early intervention systems as more effective responses to bullying than punitive measures.

Ayodele appealed to public, private, faith-based, military, mission and community-owned schools across the country to register for the event, saying participating schools would gain access to advocacy materials, programme resources and a network of institutions committed to child protection and student well-being.

He maintained that every Nigerian child deserves to learn in an environment free from fear and intimidation, urging government, school leaders, teachers, parents, civil society organisations and development partners to work together to ensure that school safety becomes a defining priority of the new academic session.

World.title: Dangote Hails Ugochinyere at 44, Describes Him as Courageous Champion of Democracy
World.content:
Africa’s richest man and President of Dangote Group, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, has congratulated the Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Petroleum Resources (Downstream), Hon. Ikenga Ugochinyere, on the occasion of his 44th birthday, describing him as a courageous champion of democracy.

In a congratulatory message issued on behalf of the Board, Management and Staff of Dangote Industries Limited, Dangote described Ugochinyere as a distinguished lawyer, civil advocate and legislator whose accomplishments and contributions to national development belie his age.

He joined the lawmaker’s family, friends and well-wishers in thanking Almighty God for a life marked by remarkable accomplishments and meaningful service to the nation.

According to Dangote, Ugochinyere’s contributions to legislative governance have helped enrich democratic discourse, strengthen institutional accountability, shape conversations around energy policy and advance the broader interests of Nigeria.

The Dangote Group President particularly commended the lawmaker’s courage, describing him as a public servant who has consistently demonstrated the willingness to stand for truth and principle, even in the face of pressure and opposition.

“Mr. Chairman, you have demonstrated enormous courage in the face of undue pressure, without being concerned about how many others shared your position, but rather standing firmly with clarity, conviction, and an unwavering commitment to the interest of our dear fatherland,” Dangote said.

He added that history would remember Ugochinyere among those who defied the odds and made sacrifices in pursuit of the greater good rather than personal interest.

Quoting the Bible in Mark 10:42–45, Dangote noted that true greatness is rooted in service, saying the lawmaker had demonstrated a commitment to this principle through his public service.

He further commended Ugochinyere’s contributions to Nigeria’s political landscape, particularly his advocacy for youth empowerment, good governance and legislative independence.

“Your steadfast advocacy for youth empowerment, good governance, and legislative independence remains highly commendable,” he stated.

Dangote prayed that Almighty God would continue to grant Ugochinyere good health, greater wisdom, strength and the grace to excel in his endeavours.

He also wished the lawmaker many more years of impactful service to Nigeria and congratulated him once again on the milestone.

World.title: Former Finance Minister Kemi Adeosun Loses Husband
World.content:
Former Minister of Finance, Mrs. Kemi Adeosun’s husband, Mr. Anthony Adeniyi (Niyi) Adeosun, is dead.

He died on Wednesday, August 5, in Lagos. He was 62 years old.

The announcement of his death was made by the Adeosun family in a statement signed by Reverend C. A. Adeosun on behalf of the family.

The family said it was announcing the passing of its “beloved husband, father, and brother… with profound sorrow, yet in total submission to the will of Almighty God.”

Describing the late Adeosun, the statement said he was “a distinguished businessman and a devoted Christian whose integrity, generosity and steadfast faith touched the lives of all who knew him.”

According to the family, “He lived a life defined by hard work, service to God and an unwavering commitment to his family and community.”

The statement said he is survived by his wife, former Minister of Finance, Mrs. Kemi Adeosun; his cherished children and his siblings, including Mr. Adewale Adeosun, Founder of Kuramo Capital, along with a host of other family members, friends, and associates.

While expressing grief over the loss, the family said it took comfort in the assurance of God’s Word in Revelation 14:13: “Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord… that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them”.

The family requested privacy during the mourning period, adding that details of the funeral and Christian burial arrangements would be communicated in due course.

It also thanked all who had reached out with prayers, condolences and support, praying that the deceased’s “gentle soul rest in perfect peace in the bosom of the Lord.”

World.title: Air Peace Chairman Cautions Unions against Paralysing Aviation Industry
World.content:
Chinedu Eze

The Chairman and CEO Air Peace Limited, Dr Allen Onyema, has cautioned aviation unions not to embark on action that will lead to prolonged disruption of the aviation industry.

Reacting to the threat of aviation unions to picket the operations of the airlines over debts owed NCAA, Onyema warned that mounting fiscal pressures, high borrowing rates, and illegal union interference are threatening the survival of domestic carriers, declaring that operators will not succumb to intimidation.

He wondered why after NCAA and the airlines had agreed on payment arrangement to liquidate the debts, which accumulated during the US-Iran war; when the cost of aviation soared from N900 per litre to N3, 500, the unions came up with the threat to picket the operations of the airlines.

Speaking during the book launch of Muneer Bankole, Chairman of Med-View Airline, in Lagos yesterday, Onyema stated that domestic airlines operate under the harshest conditions globally and deal strictly with the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), not labour unions.

He disclosed that Air Peace in one year had recorded 56 bird strikes which had severe damage on the airline’s fleet and cost huge amount of money in dollars to repair them, some of them involving engine replacements.

Onyema described the moves by trade unions to picket airlines or enforce debt recovery on behalf of government agencies as an “aberration” without global precedent, warning that any attempt to disrupt airline operations poses a direct threat to aviation safety.

“We don’t have any problem with the unions, neither do we have business with them. We have business with the NCAA, and we have been complying with what the NCAA directs us to do. If anybody thinks they can use unions to intimidate airlines in this country, they are wasting their time,” Onyema said.

Highlighting the severe economic headwinds facing the sector, the Air Peace chairman noted that Nigerian airlines borrow capital at exorbitant commercial rates of 30 to 33 percent, leaving operators with minimal breathing room to maintain fleet operations and service overheads.

He called for deep national introspection regarding why over 50 domestic airlines have collapsed over the past few decades, despite being founded by successful business proprietors who thrived in other sectors of the economy.

He recalled that the International Air Transport Association (IATA) has noted in international fora that Nigeria is one of the most difficult and expensive places in the world to operate an airline due to high operational costs, including excessive taxes, multiple charges and statutory levies; high insurance premium which is six times higher than global average: and high interest rate on loans, which is from 25%.

IATA also remarked that aside from Afghanistan which is facing extreme security and political turmoil, Nigeria remains one of the toughest environments to establish and sustain a viable airline business.

“Why don’t we do self-introspection to find out and tell ourselves the truth? Why are these airlines failing? The owners of these airlines succeeded in other businesses, but failed in the airline business. We don’t need IATA or any foreigner to remind us what we are suffering from,” he said, adding that international aviation bodies have repeatedly acknowledged the gruelling conditions under which Nigerian carriers operate.

Onyema also pointed to severe infrastructure deficits at domestic airports, disclosing that Air Peace alone recorded 56 bird strikes within a single year.

He argued that while airlines pay statutory fees for airport infrastructure and services, facilities often fall short, causing extensive downtime, physical damage, and revenue losses.

“Part of the money we pay is for certain infrastructure to be provided. Now, if the infrastructure is not provided and the airlines keep losing revenue as a result, how do they pay vendors? Then union members will go and picket airlines, saying it is because airlines could not pay. I have never heard of such a thing anywhere in the world,” Onyema stated.

Addressing allegations that labour unions are being used by third parties to demean operators, Onyema asserted that airline proprietors are already pushed to the brink and will not hesitate to ground operations if unions attempt to enforce a shutdown.

“He who is on the ground fears no fall. The airlines are already on the ground. If they want to come and destroy the airlines, let them come and do it, and we all go home. We will unleash hundreds of thousands of staff to the public, and let all of them become jobless if that is the best way to solve the problem,” he added.

Onyema maintained that domestic operators remain patriotic and committed to safety, calling on regulatory authorities and international observers to monitor developments as airlines continue to engage directly with the Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the NCAA.

World.title: NAICOM Revokes Nigeria Reinsurance’s Licence, Freezes Operations Over Capital Shortfall
World.content:
Wale Igbintade

The National Insurance Commission (NAICOM) has revoked the operating licence of Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation for failing to meet the statutory Minimum Capital Requirement (MCR) and appointed Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Dr. Muiz Banire, SAN, as Receiver/Provisional Liquidator to wind up the company’s affairs.

The appointment took effect on August 3, 2026, following the cancellation of the company’s certificate of registration by the insurance regulator.

In a public notice dated August 4, 2026, Banire said NAICOM appointed him, in exercise of its statutory powers, to oversee the receivership and liquidation of Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation (RR-002).

According to the notice, the company’s licence was revoked after it failed to comply with the prescribed Minimum Capital Requirement applicable to its category of licence within the stipulated compliance period, in accordance with the Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act (NIIRA) 2025 and other extant laws, regulations and guidelines.

Banire said his appointment authorises him to immediately trace, recover, secure and take possession of the company’s assets, collate and settle its liabilities in line with the NIIRA 2025, liaise with NAICOM on matters relating to the liquidation, and submit periodic reports to the Commission.

He directed banks, financial institutions, policyholders and members of the public not to honour any instruction relating to the company except those issued by him or persons expressly authorised by him.

He further announced that all bank accounts belonging to Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation had been frozen with immediate effect pending further directives from his office.

Banire warned that any transaction carried out without his authorisation would be invalid and undertaken at the risk of those involved.

“Members of the general public, banks and financial institutions in Nigeria are hereby informed that no financial transactions should be conducted pursuant to any instruction from anyone except those that I issue as the Receiver/Provisional Liquidator,” the notice stated.

He added that only instructions bearing his official seal and stamp, or those issued by persons duly authorised by him, would be recognised throughout the liquidation process.

The Commission’s action underscores its commitment to enforcing capital adequacy requirements in the insurance industry and ensuring that only financially sound insurers and reinsurers operate in Nigeria.

The liquidation process is expected to include the recovery and realisation of the company’s assets, verification and settlement of valid liabilities, and the orderly winding up of its affairs in accordance with the law.

World.title: Long weekend travel warning: what snow could mean for your road trip
World.content:
SAWS warns of snow over mountain passes in three provinces this long weekend, with drivers urged to plan ahead: Image ChatGPT

A long weekend snow warning is now in place for South Africa, just as Monday’s public holiday has a lot of South Africans planning road trips.

Unfortunately, the weather has other plans, and drivers heading through the country’s higher-lying regions may want to build in some flexibility.

What SAWS is forecasting for this long weekend snow event

SAWS expects a cold front, accompanied by a steep upper-air trough, to make landfall over the Western Cape and Northern Cape on Sunday, 9 August, bringing cold to very cold, wet and windy conditions, rough seas, and snowfall over mountainous areas.



According to the South African Weather Service (SAWS), the system will spread eastwards into the Eastern Cape as it moves across the country.

By Monday, 10 August, SAWS expects the upper-air trough to deepen further over the central and eastern parts of the country.

Scattered to widespread rain is forecast over the southern regions, while snow is expected specifically over the mountainous parts of the Free State, KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga.



There is a low probability of light snowfall in some higher-lying areas outside those three provinces, but forecasters say confidence remains highest for those mountain ranges.

What this could mean if you’re driving

This long weekend snow risk means mountain passes in the Free State, KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga are usually the first routes affected. They can close with little warning once conditions turn.

If your long weekend plans take you anywhere near the Drakensberg, the Free State’s high-lying roads, or Mpumalanga’s escarpment routes, check road conditions again closer to the time. Don’t rely on today’s forecast alone.



Pack for genuine cold if you’re heading that way: warm layers, a full tank, and a backup route in mind.

Even drivers not heading into the mountains themselves should expect a sharp, countrywide drop in temperature.

The cold will reach right across the country over the long weekend.



I always tell people the same thing before a long weekend snow system like this arrives.

Plan for the forecast to shift, not to hold.

World.title: Major new visa system coming to OR Tambo International Airport
World.content:
South Africa's new ETA system is coming to Johannesburg's OR Tambo Airport. Image: wikimedia commons / canva

South Africa is set to take a major step towards modernising its immigration system with the official launch of its new Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) platform at OR Tambo International Airport this August.

The system, which will be launched by President Cyril Ramaphosa and Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber on 12 August, is expected to make travelling to South Africa faster, simpler and more secure for eligible international visitors.

What is the new ETA?

An Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) is a digital travel permit that allows eligible travellers to obtain permission to travel without using the traditional visa application process.



Through the new platform, travellers will be able to complete their application and biometric verification online before departure, allowing for faster processing when they arrive in South Africa.

Similar digital travel authorisation systems are already used in countries including the United Kingdom and Canada.

The launch at OR Tambo follows the successful pilot of the ETA during South Africa’s G20 Presidency and forms a key part of the Department of Home Affairs’ digital transformation programme.

According to Presidency, the ETA is the flagship reform of a broader modernisation project that also includes advanced biometric technology and an upgraded Electronic Movement Control System (eMCS 2.0).

The new digital ecosystem is intended to improve border security while making entry and exit procedures quicker and more efficient for legitimate travellers.

Boost for tourism and business

Government also believes the new system will strengthen South Africa’s competitiveness as a destination for tourism, business and investment by reducing delays and modernising immigration services.



The launch comes shortly after the Department of Home Affairs gazetted proposed regulations that would introduce a R500 ETA processing fee once the system’s integrated online payment capability is rolled out.

Under the proposal, the fee would apply differently depending on a traveller’s visa status.

Travellers from visa-required countries would use the ETA as part of the visa application process, while travellers from visa-exempt countries would initially be able to use the system voluntarily for a faster, more streamlined travel experience.

The proposed fee structure is still subject to the public consultation process before it can be implemented.

World.title: ‘I lost my kids’: Sbu Nkosi shares personal tragedy [video]
World.content:
Sbu Nkosi has shared the reason behind his club rugby career demise. Images via Instagram

Sbu Nkosi has shared the heartbreaking reason behind his decision to step away from his successful club rugby career in a tell-all interview. The former Springbok, who helped win the 2019 Rugby World Cup trophy in Japan, was believed to have battled mental health issues.

SBU NKOSI SHARES HEARTBREAKING PERSONAL TRAGEDY

Speaking in an interview with the Off The Pitch podcast, Sbu Nkosi shared new details about allegations that he absconded from his club at both the Bulls and the Sharks.

The 30-year-old shared that his mental health had drastically declined after a personal tragedy.



He said, “I went through a period where I lost my kids, I had beautiful twins. After birth, they both passed away and I had to be back on the bandwagon and playing rugby on the same weekend.

“I never got a chance to process it the way that I needed to. I carried it with me, I was grieving, I couldnt understand, and it’s hard for anyone to understand until they’ve held their own cold baby in their arms.

“That, for me, was the beginning of a rollercoaster in my mind, because as a father, you naturally would like to protect your children, and things just happened in such a way that made me feel that I had no control or protection over my children.

Sbu Nkosi shared that the dark period made him physically ill, too. The World Cup champion used the opportunity to publicly apologise for his behaviour, particularly to his clubs.

He continued: “I have to be honest and say that I could’ve reacted better, I could’ve tried to be stronger. In some situations, I felt that I was being hard done by; I could’ve handled it better.

Sbu revealed that he had received psychological support while out of the public eye.



He added, “It wasn’t a good decision for the rugby player, for the person to remain alive and living. It’s a decision I had to make

“I’m sorry to everyone that it has affected. I was in a lot of pain and I needed to fix it so that i could move on.

Sbu thanked Bulls coach Jake White for his patience and support.

DOWNWARD SPIRAL

Sbu Nkosi has made headlines for all the wrong reasons during his professional rugby career.

In 2024, he was slapped with a three-year ban after testing positive for an anabolic steroid commonly used by bodybuilders. At the time, he was signed to the Cheetahs, who reportedly offered him a “lifeline”.

Just months before signing with the Gauteng club, Sbu Nkosi’s contract with the Bulls was terminated with immediate effect.

During his tenure at the club, Sbu went AWOL in 2022 and used his Instagram account to throw shade at his club.

According to TimesLive, Sbu – who cited mental health struggles for his absence – did the same at the Sharks, too.

Speaking in a press conference in 2023, Bulls boss Jake White expressed his concern about the player’s decline.

He said of Sbu: “He’s not playing well enough, he’s not training hard enough, I don’t see him enough for him to warrant selection above guys who have been training in the group anyway….I think he battles with whatever [that’s bothering him].

“My gut feeling is that I don’t think he battles with anything other than that he needs to get his life sorted”.

RUGBY CAREER BACK ON TRACK?

Due to a doping ban, Sbu Nkosi will only be eligible to play professional rugby again in 2027.

While he hasn’t given any details about a possible return to the pitch, Sbu has shared an update on his mental health.

He shared, “I am doing well, I can say I’m out of the cave. I feel the light on my skin and the wind in my hair. And I can feel my spirit being revived again.

Sbu added: “I felt like I was almost a shadow of the man I was supposed to be, and I needed to take a step back and fix the problem before it became a problem.”

World.title: WATCH | Rugby player Sbu Nkosi opens up about his darkest mental health battles
World.content:
Rugby player Sbu Nkosi is finally opening up about his pain and personal battle, mourning the loss of his infant twins, in an interview with Darian Ducci on the podcast Off The Pitch Rugby.

Sinking under the pressure of having to go straight onto the pitch after his children died in 2022, Nkosi chose to take care of himself as a man before taking care of the rugby player.

Without telling anyone his whereabouts, Nkosi disappeared, and most feared the worst when weeks passed with no trace.



“What actually happened?” asked Ducci.

“I had been going through a very, very tough time mentally, which had started pretty much back in Durban. I went through a period where I had lost my kids,” Nkosi responded.

“You know, I had two beautiful twins birthed, and you know, a little after birth, they both passed away, and I just had to be back on the bandwagon and playing rugby on the same weekend, so I never really got a chance to process it the way that I needed to process it,” said Nkosi.

“You know, I think it’s something that’s very hard for someone to understand until they’ve held their own cold baby in their arms, you know. It sent me on a spiral, you know, to a point where I actually became physically sick,” he explained.

“Most of it started with that moment, very, very heavy moments that I still feel with the same intensity today. It wasn’t a very good decision for the rugby player, you know, but for the person to remain alive and living, I think it’s a decision that I had to make. I’m very, very sorry. I was just in a lot of pain, and I wanted to finally find a way to fix it so that I could move on.”
