World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Iraqi Drilling Company completes well rehabilitation at West Qurna 1 oil field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC) has successfully completed the rehabilitation of oil well WQ1-132 at the West Qurna 1 oil field, marking another step in Iraq’s efforts to enhance oil production efficiency and support the long-term development of its energy sector.

The project was carried out as part of the company’s operational program to improve well performance and maintain sustainable crude oil production.

According to a statement issued by the Iraqi Drilling Company, the rehabilitation work was completed in line with directives from Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi and under the supervision of the company’s Director General, Mohammed Hantoosh Asad Al-Azirjawi.

Technical and engineering teams carried out the operation using the company’s specialized expertise and equipment.

The company said the rehabilitation project forms part of its broader strategy to improve the efficiency of existing oil wells while supporting sustainable production across Iraq’s major oil fields.

Restoration work on producing wells helps maximize output, extend operational life, and improve field performance without the need for entirely new drilling operations.

The Iraqi Drilling Company emphasized that the successful completion of the project reflects the capabilities of its engineering and technical staff, who continue to execute specialized rehabilitation operations according to approved operational plans.

The company noted that relying on local expertise strengthens operational efficiency while supporting the continued development of Iraq’s oil infrastructure.

West Qurna 1 is one of Iraq’s largest producing oil fields and plays a significant role in the country’s crude oil output.

Ongoing rehabilitation and maintenance projects are designed to ensure production stability, improve operational reliability, and meet the technical requirements of field development programs.

The completion of well WQ1-132 is expected to contribute to maintaining efficient production operations within the field as Iraq continues investing in the modernization of its energy sector.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Kurdistan president discuss Erbil-Baghdad cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and the president of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Nechirvan Barzani, discussed on Wednesday the country’s political, economic, and security situation.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the two leaders indicated that it is important to boost cooperation between the federal government and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) to enhance stability, address challenges, and serve the interests of the Iraqi people, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi affirmed the government’s commitment to resolving outstanding issues in line with the constitution, preserving Iraq’s unity, and strengthening national partnership.

Barzani stated that it is important to continue dialogue between national parties. He added that the KRG supports the federal government’s efforts to enhance stability and promote national development.

The discussions focused on approaches to secure the success of the government’s national agenda.

This high-level meeting comes after al-Zaidi’s trips to Turkey and Iran, where he met top officials, and Barzani’s visit to Damascus, where he met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

World.title: Iraq wins legal case in Jordan for Samarra Pharmaceutical Company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice has announced a legal victory before the Jordanian judiciary after securing a final court ruling in favor of the State Company for Drug Industries and Medical Appliances in Samarra, a subsidiary of the Ministry of Industry and Minerals.

The ruling requires a Jordanian company to pay financial compensation following a dispute over the supply of medical materials that failed to meet agreed specifications.

According to a statement from the Ministry of Justice, the ministry’s Legal Department successfully represented the Iraqi pharmaceutical company throughout all stages of the legal proceedings before Jordanian courts.

The case involved a supply contract under which the Jordanian company was expected to provide metal covers for medical supplies. However, the supplier allegedly delivered products that did not comply with the contractual specifications.

Director of the Legal Department, Haitham Mohi Radi, said the final judgment issued by the Jordanian Court of Cassation, and upheld by both the Court of Appeal and the Court of First Instance, ordered the Jordanian company to pay financial amounts to the Samarra-based pharmaceutical company.

The ruling concludes a lengthy legal process aimed at protecting the contractual rights of the Iraqi state-owned enterprise.

The Ministry of Justice described the outcome as an important achievement in safeguarding Iraq’s financial interests abroad.

Officials said the successful litigation reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to defend state institutions before international courts and judicial authorities while protecting public funds from contractual violations.

The ministry added that the case demonstrates the expertise and professionalism of Iraq’s legal teams in handling international commercial disputes.

By successfully pursuing the claim through multiple judicial levels in Jordan, the Legal Department reinforced Iraq’s commitment to enforcing contractual rights and ensuring accountability in cross-border commercial agreements.

The decision is expected to strengthen confidence in the government’s ability to defend the interests of Iraqi public institutions through legal channels.

World.title: Ammar Al-Hakim and Iranian Science Minister discuss academic cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The head of Iraq’s National State Forces Alliance, Ammar Al-Hakim, met with Iranian Minister of Science, Research and Technology Hossein Simaei Sarraf in Baghdad to discuss expanding academic cooperation between Iraq and Iran through university partnerships, knowledge exchange, and joint educational initiatives.

The meeting focused on strengthening higher education ties while emphasizing the role of universities in addressing labor market needs and societal challenges.

According to a statement released by Al-Hakim’s office, the two sides reviewed opportunities to deepen cooperation between Iraqi and Iranian universities by promoting twinning agreements, expanding academic collaboration, and exchanging expertise.

The discussions highlighted the importance of strengthening institutional relationships to support scientific research and educational development in both countries.

During the meeting, Al-Hakim stressed that university graduates should possess skills that match the demands of today’s job market.

He also urged academic institutions to prioritize scientific research that offers practical solutions to national challenges and contributes to sustainable development.

Al-Hakim emphasized the importance of equipping university students with strong scientific knowledge to prepare them for future professional opportunities.

The Iraqi political leader underscored the role of research institutions in supporting innovation and policymaking.

He noted that universities should focus on producing research capable of addressing economic, social, and developmental issues while enhancing academic excellence.

The discussion reflected a shared interest in strengthening educational cooperation as part of broader bilateral relations.

The meeting also touched on the annual Arbaeen pilgrimage, with Al-Hakim praising the hospitality shown by Iraqis toward visitors traveling to commemorate Imam Hussein.

He said the event demonstrates positive values of solidarity and cooperation, while calling for stronger ties between societies based on shared humanitarian and religious principles.

The visit concluded with discussions on enhancing educational cooperation alongside broader people-to-people engagement between Iraq and Iran.

World.title: Iraq’s State Administration Coalition warns armed groups after September 30
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Administration Coalition has reaffirmed its support for restricting all weapons to state control, warning that any armed activity outside the authority of the government after September 30, 2026, will be treated under the country’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

The position was announced following the coalition’s 37th regular meeting, hosted by Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi, with the participation of Iraq’s senior political and constitutional leaders.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the meeting brought together the President of the Republic, the Speaker of Parliament, the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the Kurdistan Region, and leaders of the State Administration Coalition.

Participants reviewed Iraq’s political, security, economic, and public service developments, as well as regional events and their impact on the country.

The coalition reiterated its backing for the government’s efforts to ensure that all weapons remain under state authority, in line with the government program approved by the Iraqi Parliament.

The coalition stressed that Iraqi territory must not be used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries or for actions that could draw Iraq into regional conflicts.

It warned that individuals or groups engaging in such activities would be committing crimes that threaten national security.

According to the statement, after September 30, 2026, any armed activity conducted outside the state’s legal framework will be dealt with under Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

Officials also cited constitutional provisions prohibiting the formation of armed organizations outside the official security forces.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi briefed coalition members on government efforts to strengthen security, improve public services, implement the ministerial program, and address Iraq’s financial and economic challenges.

The coalition emphasized the need to:

Maintain national security and stability.

Protect essential public services.

Diversify Iraq’s oil export routes.

Increase non-oil revenues.

Combat corruption, smuggling, and financial waste.

The meeting highlighted the government’s commitment to protecting citizens’ interests while strengthening economic resilience.

On regional affairs, coalition leaders expressed support for diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions across the Middle East.

The meeting reaffirmed Iraq’s rejection of resolving disputes through military force and emphasized Baghdad’s willingness to play a constructive role in promoting dialogue between regional parties.

Participants also discussed border security, counterterrorism cooperation, combating drug trafficking and organized crime, and strengthening relations with neighboring and international partners based on mutual respect and national sovereignty.

At the conclusion of the meeting, the State Administration Coalition called for accelerating the completion of the government formation process and submitting the government’s official program to the Council of Representatives for discussion and approval.

The coalition said completing these constitutional steps remains essential for advancing Iraq’s political stability and governance agenda.

World.title: Iraq’s electricity shortage surpasses 35,000 megawatts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s electricity shortage, particularly during the summer months, has reached 35,000 megawatts, forcing Baghdad to seek immediate measures that ensure a consistent supply and prevent power outages.

Turkey has emerged as a potential long-term solution to Iraq’s issue, with Ankara’s plans to boost energy exports and gas supplies while developing Iraq’s transmission infrastructure, according to Attaqa News.

Baghdad’s attempts to diversify its electrical supply sources and secure fuel for power plants, particularly those that run on gas, are taking place amid expanding regional electricity interconnection projects to bridge the gap between rising demand and available production capacity.

Iraq relies on electricity imports from neighboring nations and Iraqi Kurdistan to cover some of its demands, in addition to importing Iranian gas to run multiple power plants.

Iraq and Turkey are relying on joint energy projects to offer short- and medium-term solutions while collaborating on major initiatives to improve Iraq’s long-term energy security.

Electricity Ministry spokesperson Ahmed Turki Jiyad announced that electricity production has surpassed 24,600 megawatts. However, total demand remains between 55,000 and 60,000 megawatts, indicating a persistent shortfall of over 35,000 megawatts.

Jiyad noted that although the current electricity output has increased daily supply hours to between 10 and 12, it still falls significantly short of meeting consumers’ actual needs, especially with the high demand during the summer months.

The Iraqi government has developed a plan to raise output capacity to 35,000 megawatts by 2030. However, the initiative’s success depends on providing sufficient fuel for power plants, as well as securing funds for new projects.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports slightly rise during July
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Data from shipping firm Kpler showed that crude oil and condensate exports from the Gulf countries steadied in July at roughly 10.7 million barrels per day, a two percent rise compared to June but still approximately 40 percent below pre-war levels.

Iraq boosted regional exports by increasing oil output compared to June, aided by growing tanker shipments that largely offset the drop in Saudi and UAE exports.

Oil shipments slowed in the second half of July due to rising security tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, as well as an increase in vessel assaults, causing some oil tankers to change their routes or turn off their tracking systems while at sea.

The consistent flow of oil shipments has eased concerns about global supply shortages. However, oil tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab remains below pre-war levels, which raises geopolitical risks in energy markets.

Iraq’s seaborne crude oil shipments increased in July by more than 153 percent, or 757,000 barrels per day, compared to the previous month.

According to Attaqa News, Iraqi oil shipments by sea rose to over 1.25 million barrels per day in July compared to 493,000 barrels per day in June.

The partial restart of commercial activity in the Strait of Hormuz prior to increased tensions and the development of the situation fueled this spike.

World.title: Govt tightens rules on AI-generated content, cuts removal deadline to 3 hours from 36 & mandates labels
World.content:
The Centre has enacted or strengthened rules including IT Rules to curb AIâgenerated deepfakes

The government has tightened rules for social media platforms to tackle AI-generated deepfakes and other synthetically generated content, including fake audio, video and text.Under amendments to the IT Rules made in February, platforms must clearly label permissible AI-generated content and ensure it carries traceable metadata so users can identify âsynthetically generated materialâ.The amended rules require platforms to take measures against unlawful AI-generated content, including deepfakes, child sexual abuse material, non-consensual intimate images and AI-based impersonation. Platforms must also inform users about the âlegal consequencesâ of creating or sharing unlawful AI-generated content.The government has cut the deadline for platforms to remove unlawful content from 36 hours to 3 hours which shall start after receiving a valid notice from the government or a court. The rules also require intermediaries to deploy âreasonable and appropriate technical measuresâ to prevent users from creating or disseminating unlawful synthetic content.Significant social media intermediaries must use automated tools or other technical measures to proactively detect certain unlawful content, including material depicting rape or child sexual abuse. They must also make âreasonable effortsâ to identify content that is identical to material previously removed.The government has also tightened grievance redressal timelines. Complaints involving sensitive issues such as nudity and impersonation must be addressed within 2 hours, compared with the earlier 24-hour timeline.Failure to comply with the IT Rules can result in platforms losing their safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the IT Act, which protects intermediaries from liability for third-party content subject to certain conditions.The government said the measures are part of its efforts to ensure an âopen, safe, trusted and accountable cyberspaceâ while promoting the âresponsible development, deployment and adoption of AIâ in India.

World.title: Netanyahu calls PM Modi to discuss West Asia situation, India-Israel relations
World.content:
PM Modi and Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu discussed bilateral ties and the evolving situation in West Asia during a phone call

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday received a telephone call from his Israeli counterpart, Benjamin Netanyahu, during which the two leaders reviewed the progress of the India-Israel special strategic partnership and discussed the evolving situation in West Asia.According to a PIB statement, PM Modi and Netanyahu reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation across a range of sectors for the mutual benefit of both countries."Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi received a telephone call from Prime Minister of Israel, HE Mr Benjamin Netanyahu today. The two leaders reviewed sustained progress in India-Israel Special Strategic Partnership and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the bilateral cooperation across various sectors for the mutual benefit of the two countries," the statement read."PM Netanyahu and PM Modi exchanged views on the recent developments in West Asia. The two leaders agreed to remain in touch," it said.The conflict in West Asia has entered its sixth month with no lasting resolution in sight.Iran said it is in the final stages of drafting an agreement with Oman on the Strait of Hormuz, a strategically vital waterway for global shipping and energy supplies.The Strait of Hormuz, through which nearly one-fifth of the world's oil and natural gas flowed before the war began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February, remains a critical artery for global energy trade.

World.title: Evening news wrap: Ex-Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal convicted in rape case; Atiq Ahmed's son killed in road accident
World.content:
Tejpal convicted: Bombay HC overturned Tarun Tejpal's acquittal, convicted him in the 2013 rape case and sentenced him to 10 years in prison.

Bombay HC overturned Tarun Tejpal's acquittal, convicted him in the 2013 rape case and sentenced him to 10 years in prison. Fatal crash: Atiq Ahmed's son Abaan and his friend Sonu were killed after their SUV crashed into a divider in Jhansi.

Atiq Ahmed's son Abaan and his friend Sonu were killed after their SUV crashed into a divider in Jhansi. No poll plunge: CJP said it will stay out of electoral politics for now and continue functioning as a public pressure group.

CJP said it will stay out of electoral politics for now and continue functioning as a public pressure group. Soren under fire: Jharkhand job aspirants demanded CM Hemant Soren's resignation and announced an Assembly gherao on August 10.

Jharkhand job aspirants demanded CM Hemant Soren's resignation and announced an Assembly gherao on August 10. Tax Bill passed: Lok Sabha cleared the Taxation Amendment Bill without debate amid Opposition protests and disruptions.

Here are top 5 news of the day:

HC convicts ex-Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal in rape case, sentences him to 10 years imprisonment

The Bombay high court convicted former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal in a rape case and sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment, overturning a trial court's 2021 acquittal.

The case relates to the alleged rape of a colleague in the elevator of a starred hotel in Goa in 2013. The high court was hearing the Goa government's appeal against the acquittal and granted Tejpal two weeks to surrender.

Atiq Ahmed's son Abaan killed in Jhansi road accident

Abaan, the son of deceased gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmed, was killed in a road accident in Uttar Pradesh's Jhansi after the SUV he was travelling in crashed into a divider. His friend Sonu also died in the accident, while three others sustained injuries and were admitted to a medical college for treatment.

According to police, the Hyundai Creta was travelling from Prayagraj to Jhansi when the driver allegedly lost control of the vehicle, causing it to hit the divider.

CJP rules out electoral politics, to continue as pressure group

The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) said it will continue to function as a public pressure group instead of entering electoral politics for now. The announcement came after a two-day meeting of the party's core team in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.





Founder Abijeet Dipke said the organisation will focus on building a nationwide citizens' movement on issues such as unemployment, education, transparency, accountability and institutional reforms, while also launching a campaign titled "Kya Bolti Public.

"

Jharkhand job aspirants demand Hemant Soren's resignation amid recruitment protests

Students protesting alleged irregularities in Jharkhand's government recruitment process intensified their agitation, demanding chief minister Hemant Soren's resignation over the government's failure to address their concerns.

A hunger-striking protester called Soren "unfit" to hold office, accusing him of ignoring the demonstrations despite returning from Bengaluru. The protesters also announced plans to gherao the state Assembly on August 10, saying they would continue their agitation until their demands are met.

Lok Sabha clears Taxation Amendment Bill amid opposition protests

The Lok Sabha passed the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill without any discussion as persistent sloganeering by Opposition members disrupted proceedings. The legislation, which also amends the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, aims to attract greater foreign investment, boost domestic electronics manufacturing and simplify the use of India-based data centres by overseas cloud service providers.

Following its passage, the House was adjourned for the day.

World.title: 'We are not enemies': Rijiju meets Rahul to break Parliament logjam over Delimitation, FCRA
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister

on Thursday said he had a "good" discussion with Lok Sabha leader of opposition

, adding that the government made a request on a specific issue and also discussed other matters.

"I had a good discussion with Rahul Gandhi ji...we made a request regarding an issue and also discussed other matters.We desire continuous communication and coordinated action with the Congress and other opposition parties. We may be political opponents, but we are not enemies; therefore, we should work together in the national interest," Rijiju told reporters.

"However, they (opposition) create an impression outside is that they won't let Parliament function at all, but who ultimately suffers from that?" the parliamentary affairs minister asked.

Rijiju also responded to reporters' questions about the opposition's demand for a statement from Union home minister Amit Shah on the Delhi Police action against student protesters during their march to Parliament on July 20, the opening day of the Monsoon Session.

"The home minister has introduced bills in Parliament and has been present in the House from morning till evening. Naturally, the minister whose bill is under consideration is the one who remains present in the House," he added.





Rijiju's remarks came a day after he reportedly met Rahul Gandhi to seek his cooperation in ensuring the smooth functioning of Parliament during the remainder of the Monsoon Session. The two also discussed the possible reintroduction of the Delimitation and Women's Reservation Bills, though the Congress leader reportedly made no commitment.

During the nearly 50-minute meeting on Wednesday, Rahul Gandhi is learnt to have told Rijiju that a statement by Amit Shah on the Delhi Police action against students protesting over the NEET paper leak issue, along with a discussion on the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, were "non-negotiables" for the House to function.

The Monsoon Session is scheduled to conclude on August 13. On Thursday, the government dismissed media reports claiming that a three-day special session would be convened from August 16 to 18 to take up the Women's Reservation and Delimitation Bills, two key items on its legislative agenda.

World.title: IIT-G develops low-cost device to detect toxic metals, bacteria in water
World.content:
IIT Guwahati researchers develop portable device that quickly detects toxic metals in water

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Researchers at IIT Guwahati have developed a portable optical sensing device that can quickly detect toxic metals, fluoride and bacteria in water samples, offering a low-cost tool for on-site water-quality checks in rural areas and places without easy access to laboratories.Named E-Eye, the device has detected arsenic, lead, iron, chromium, fluoride and Escherichia coli bacteria during laboratory tests, the institute said on Thursday. The estimated cost of the device is about Rs 3,500, with each sample test costing around Rs 2.The device uses a chemical reaction that produces a coloured compound. The intensity of the colour changes according to the concentration of the contaminant. E-Eye analyses the colour through optical sensing, converts the reading into digital data and displays the concentration of the toxicant.According to the researchers, the portable system can be deployed directly at water sources, unlike conventional testing equipment that generally requires samples to be taken to laboratories. It can also wirelessly transmit test results to water-treatment facilities.The team said E-Eyeâs results were comparable with those obtained through standard UV-Visible and Atomic Absorption spectrophotometers.More than 2,700 samples have been tested using the device, it added.âThe device operates on the Beer-Lambert law and combines optical sensing with digital electronics to generate accurate quantitative measurements. Our device has been able to successfully detect toxicants such as arsenic, lead, iron, chromium, fluoride, and Escherichia coli bacteria,â said Tapas K Mandal, professor in IIT Guwahatiâs department of chemical engineering.The researchers said the device could support water-quality monitoring under the Centreâs Jal Jeevan Mission, which seeks to provide tap water to rural households while ensuring that the water supplied is safe.Apart from drinking water, E-Eye can be used to test environmental and biological samples, vegetables, food products, tea, herbal products, soil and milk, the institute said. It may also help industries monitor liquid effluents containing heavy metals, bacteria and odour-causing compounds.The research, supported by a grant from the ministry of electronics and information technology, has been published in the IEEE Sensors Journal. The team includes IIT Guwahati professors Mandal and Harshal B Nemade, along with researchers from the institute, KIIT Bhubaneswar and Ramakrishna Mission Residential College, Kolkata.The researchers have set up ENVIONIX Labs Pvt Ltd to commercialise the technology and are exploring an industry partnership for its transfer. They are also working to integrate solar panels and cloud connectivity into the device for remote monitoring and data management.

World.title: Govt backs 20 indigenous AI models, clears 58 centres of excellence
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has selected 20 indigenous foundation-model proposals for support and sanctioned over 93 lakh hours of subsidised computing capacity as part of its effort to reduce Indiaâs dependence on foreign artificial intelligence infrastructure and technologies.

In a written reply in Lok Sabha on Wednesday, minister of state for electronics and information technology

said the proposals were selected from 506 applications received under the IndiaAI Mission. They include 12 large multimodal models and eight small language models, with the intellectual property remaining with the developers.

Among the models already launched are Sarvam AIâs 30-billion and 105-billion parameter models and Indus, Gnani.AIâs speech-to-speech model, BharatGenâs multilingual models and Avataar AIâs video-generation model.

The IndiaAI Mission, approved in March 2024 with an outlay of Rs 10,371.92 crore over five years, is aimed at creating domestic capabilities in computing, foundation models, applications, research and responsible AI.

The government has empanelled 15 computing service providers and approved subsidised computing support for 237 projects, involving 93.18 lakh GPU hours. It has also issued a purchase order for a high-performance AI computing system of around 1.1 exaflops at the National Informatics Centreâs data centre in Shastri Park, Delhi.





Eleven national-level hackathons and innovation challenges have so far resulted in 62 AI prototypes, of which 20 have been deployed in public-sector institutions. The government has also approved 58 AI centres of excellence across states and Union territories. Of these, work has begun on 22 centres in 13 states and UTs.

Another 13 projects have been selected to work on AI safety issues such as bias, privacy, algorithm audits, explainability and machine unlearning.

Prasada said India was also strengthening the wider technology ecosystem through the National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems, which has an outlay of Rs 3,660 crore. Twenty-five technology innovation hubs have been established at academic institutions in areas including AI, robotics, cybersecurity, quantum technology and fintech.

On semiconductors, the minister said 12 manufacturing projects involving committed investments of Rs 1.64 lakh crore had been approved under the Semicon India programme, with three having started commercial production.

The Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0 on July 15 with an outlay of Rs 1.27 lakh crore. The programme will support Indian-designed chips, semiconductor fabrication and packaging units, and the production of materials, gases and equipment required by the industry.

The government acknowledged that Indiaâs AI computing ecosystem currently depends on imported graphics processing units procured through approved service providers. It said the IndiaAI and semiconductor missions were intended to progressively build domestic capabilities across the AI supply chain.

Citing Stanfordâs Global AI Vibrancy Report of November 2025, the reply said India ranked third globally in AI competitiveness and was the second-largest contributor to AI projects on GitHub.

World.title: Meta admits to 'serious issues' in talks with govt over CSAM, deepfakes & bots
World.content:
The Meta row continued on Thursday as the companyâs global team held further discussions with the government over compliance with Indian laws, a day after the company apologised for briefly removing a video posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Metaâs global team is expected to remain in India for another three to four days, with more meetings planned with government officials, with the discussions also expected to cover WhatsApp issues. Meanwhile, the talks with IT ministry officials continued for a 2nd day during which the IT giant admitted to 'serious issues' and assured that they are "working hard" over CSAM, deepfakes & bots issues, as per PTI sources.

The government is seeking details on Metaâs algorithms, content moderation, compliance mechanisms, checks and balances and safeguards, including the systems used to tackle child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and deepfake content.

âPlatforms can't be run in India as per US law. These are technical matters; every aspect is to be understood,â government sources told ANI, adding âAll platforms have a responsibility towards society and the law, like all institutions.â





IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw is also scheduled to meet Metaâs global team on Thursday, while ministry officials will continue discussions with the companyâs technical teams.

âMeta has already given a public statement; technical details to be discussed today, along with logs,â sources said, adding that the government is in regular talks with other major platforms, including X and Telegram.

The fresh discussions come a day after Meta officials apologised to the government over the brief removal of PM Modiâs video from Facebook.

Joel Kaplan, Metaâs chief global affairs officer, said he had apologised to Vaishnaw âon behalf of Meta for the error restricting PM Modiâs postâ. The government had also raised concerns over CSAM, deepfake content and Metaâs content moderation systems.

The government has further questioned Metaâs compliance with Indian laws and its eligibility for safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, which provides intermediaries protection from liability for third-party content subject to certain conditions.

World.title: On the frontlines: How Indian sailors are paying the price in Middle East war
World.content:
10 Indian sailors have been killed in the Middle East while hundreds are still sailing the dangerous waters

Numbers tell the story

An officer died as he got sick on vessel off Oman Coast

The silent toll on India

The cost of war that India has paid

âSeafarers are not warriorsâ

Life on board

While world powers engage in military blockades and political posturing, the people suffering the real humanitarian crisis are the innocent seafarers trapped onboard. Deepak Kumar, third officer in merchant navy

Every seafarer should have the right to decline sailing through a high risk area without fear of damaging their career. Amit Khareta, MD at Barrow & Trent Shipping India

Protecting sailors

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Cost of trade

For thousands of Indian merchant seafarers, the Middle East war has transformed the sea from a workplace into a battlefield.They are not soldiers. They are civilians who keep global trade moving, transporting oil, fuel and essential cargo through some of the world's busiest shipping lanes, including the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman and the Red Sea. But since the US-Israel war with Iran erupted on February 28, many have found themselves navigating through missile strikes, drone attacks and naval hostilities.Some never made it home. Indian sailors have been killed in attacks on commercial vessels. Others have been injured or stranded at sea for weeks, unable to escape the conflict. Back home, anxious families spend their days glued to news bulletins, fearing every report of another ship being struck and praying for a phone call confirming their loved ones are still alive.The scale of the crisis is stark.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) recently said 166 Indian seafarers remained in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz region, with 125 aboard six Indian-flagged vessels and another 41 serving on foreign ships. In an update on August 4, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways said 3,972 Indian seafarers had been repatriated from the Gulf region, underscoring the massive effort to bring them out of one of the world's most dangerous conflict zones.India is the world's second-largest supplier of seafarers after the Philippines, with 311,936 personnel accounting for 12.16 per cent of the global maritime workforce, according to the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026.Indian officers make up 13.41 per cent of the world's officer workforce, while the country also supplies 171,218 ratings, representing 11.29 per cent of the global ratings workforce.That vast presence at sea has come at a heavy cost since the Iran war erupted.Last month, the MEA said Indian seafarers had suffered the highest number of fatalities of any nationality in attacks on commercial shipping. Later, the government informed Parliament that 10 Indian seafarers were among the 16 Indian nationals killed in the Middle East conflict.However, the human cost extends far beyond those killed in missile and drone attacks.Hundreds of Indian sailors stranded in conflict-hit waters have faced prolonged deployments, delayed crew changes, disrupted medical evacuations, supply shortages and worsening onboard conditions, exposing them to mounting physical and mental risks.One such tragedy unfolded in June when 35-year-old Second Officer Nishanth Uirthanathan died from medical complications aboard the MT Celestial near Oman after falling seriously ill.The Indian Embassy coordinated the repatriation of his remains, while the Federation of Seafarers' Unions of India (FSUI) alleged that critical medical assistance was delayed because the vessel was operating in a conflict zone. Following his death, crew members reportedly had to preserve his body using bottles of cold water as the ship lacked adequate refrigeration facilities.The human cost for India was almost immediate.Within 24 hours of the Iran war erupting, Indian seafarers had begun paying the price.On March 1. Captain Ashish Kumar and crew member Dalip (Daleep) Singh were killed when the Palau-flagged tanker Skylight was attacked near Oman's Musandam Peninsula. Hours later, another Indian seafarer lost his life after the Marshall Islands-flagged gasoline tanker MKD Vyom was struck off the Omani coast.The attacks continued over the following months.On March 11, 54-year-old Deonandan Prasad Singh was killed when the Marshall Islands-flagged Safesea Vishnu came under fire near Basra, Iraq.On May 8, Indian seafarer Altaf Talab Ker died and four others were injured after the Indian-flagged dhow Al Faize Noor Suleimani was caught in crossfire in the Strait of Hormuz.The single deadliest attack came on June 10, when the Palau-flagged Settebello was struck by US forces in the Gulf of Oman, killing Chief Engineer Patnala Suresh, Deck Cadet Aditya Sharma and Fitter Shivanand Chaurashiya.The toll continued to climb in July.Marine engineer Herambh Karmarkar was killed on July 12 after the Cyprus-flagged GFS Galaxy was hit shortly after transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Ten of the vessel's 11 Indian crew members were rescued.Two days later, Indian seafarer Rohan Kumar was killed when the Liberia-flagged Mombasa B was struck by Iranian missiles alongside Al Bahyah in Omani waters.Together, the two vessels carried 30 Indian seafarers.Other India-linked vessels also came under attack but avoided fatalities. The cargo ship Haji Ali was hit on May 13, while Marivex and Jalveer were attacked in June, with all Indian crew members rescued.The violence has shown little sign of easing.On August 4, the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya was hit near Yemen and sank. All 13 Indian crew members survived, narrowly escaping what could have been another deadly addition to India's mounting toll.For merchant seafarers, the risks are fundamentally different: commercial vessels can become targets, crews can be stranded for days and even routine medical emergencies can become life-threatening when ports and evacuation routes are disrupted.That has put a new question at the centre: who protects the people onboard?Recently, the sinking of the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya on 4 August has intensified calls for stronger protection of merchant crews. The Federation of Seafarers' Unions of India (FSUI), one of the key seafarer bodies advocating for their safety, has asked PM Modi to deploy Navy assets to protect Indian-flagged ships and Indian crews across the Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Black Sea.The Navy already operates Urja Suraksha, an escort mission for energy shipments through the Strait. FSUI wants such protection extended to commercial vessels and says it had warned the government about the risks in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait roughly a month before the Faize Noore Oliya attack.Raising concerns on safety, FSUI general secretary Manoj Yadav told TOI. âTodayâs escalation of war, which has reached the sea from land, targets commercial vessels from either side â the US and Iran,â adding that crews, including large numbers of Indians, are being caught in a conflict they had no role in.Yadav argued that military or naval forces can stop a commercial vessel without harming its crew; by boarding or detaining it, for instance instead of targeting sensitive areas such as engine rooms and accommodation blocks.âSeafarers are not warriors. They work to serve the nation and the global supply chain,â Yadav reiterated.FSUI's concerns extend beyond attacks. It says thousands of seafarers remain at risk in the Persian Gulf and Black Sea, while war-risk insurance gaps can leave families without compensation. The union has called for a government-backed insurance mechanism, $5 million for each deceased seafarer's family and employment support for next of kin.FSUI has also urged the government to seek a UN-backed independent inquiry into the deaths of seafarers in conflict zones and establish accountability.âSeafarers are the heartbeat of the ocean,â Yadav said. FSUI has called on seafarers both aboard ships and ashore to observe September 25 as a Day of Global Maritime Mourning.For the people actually on ships, the war is not a headline, it's a watch schedule.Deepak Kumar, a Third Officer in the Merchant Navy, said shipping companies now run detailed risk assessments and add security measures before entering high-risk waters, and depending on the threat level, some deploy armed guards while naval forces patrol the surrounding sea.But no amount of planning removes the strain."No seafarer wants to sail through a high-risk maritime zone," as every transit means disturbed sleep, patchy contact with home, and having to "put your emotions aside" and keep the ship running regardless.Kumar added that the hardest part often isn't the danger itself but the silence around it: families hearing of an attack near their loved one's trading route and waiting for a message confirming they're safe.Ritik Raina, another Third Officer, explained why the Hormuz transit is uniquely brutal.There is a distinction between a High Risk Area, where seafarers face threats such as piracy and armed attacks, and a Warlike Operations Area, where they are exposed directly to an ongoing military conflict. The latter carries far greater implications for crews, including enhanced compensation and, under international maritime labour agreements, the right to refuse to enter the area, he explained.The Strait of Hormuz was initially designated a High Risk Area on March 2, before being upgraded to a Warlike Operations Area three days later.For crews already inside the Gulf, however, the geography makes that distinction consequential.The Gulf is enclosed on three sides, with the Strait of Hormuz as its only maritime exit.âOnce a ship is inside the Gulf, it simply cannot leave until the blockade lifts, leaving crews to ration food, watch fresh water systems run down, and lose internet access as onboard connectivity, decided by shipowners, thins out or disappears,â said Raina.Contracts do carry war-zone bonuses, he further explained, and sailors can refuse to sail into a designated danger area before a vessel enters it.Meanwhile, former chief engineer and managing director at Barrow & Trent Shipping India Amit Khareta said geopolitical risk is increasingly becoming a reality the shipping industry has to plan around. Larger companies can sometimes divert via the Cape of Good Hope, but the added cost is not always practical for smaller owners, who may continue using high-risk routes after risk assessments and taking additional war-risk insurance.For seafarers, the choice is complicated.Khareta said many crews he has spoken to are willing to sail.Higher war-risk bonuses and additional compensation also influence that decision, with some owners offering several times the normal salary for such voyages.While Khareta himself has chosen not to sail through the current danger zone because of family obligations, he said he understands why experienced seafarers do it. But the decision, he stressed, must remain voluntary; âevery seafarer should have the right to decline sailing through a high-risk area without fear of damaging their career.âThe bigger burden, he said, is often psychological. Families worry constantly, seafarers face enormous pressure themselves while longer routes, disrupted schedules and fatigue add to the strain, but the uncertainty of not knowing what may happen once a ship enters a conflict zone weighs most heavily. âMerchant seafarers are civilians,â Khareta said. âThey are not part of the conflict, yet they are exposed to its consequences simply because global trade depends on them. âBeyond the decisions made by individual seafarers and shipping companies, the crisis has also put the spotlight on the systems meant to protect shipping in conflict zones.International maritime law already provides several layers of protection.The Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 sets minimum standards for seafarers' working and living conditions, including wages, medical care, repatriation and welfare. SOLAS lays down safety requirements for ships, while the ISPS Code deals specifically with ship and port security, requiring vessels to assess security risks and maintain plans and procedures to respond to them. But these rules were not designed to make merchant ships immune to an active war.In this context, Vidhu Shekhar, associate professor at SPJIMR, brought an economic lens to the problem, particularly on how maritime risk is distributed between shipowners, insurers and crews.âRouting decisions are made principally by owners and charterers, while the physical risk is borne by crews who have little influence over those decisions,â Shekhar said. He said sharper protections such as hazard pay and refusal rights have therefore often come through collective agreements, leaving some seafarers facing the same danger without equivalent protection. âRisk is therefore priced by contractual coverage rather than consistently by the hazard itself,â he added.For Indian sailors, Shekhar said the exposure is particularly unusual because most Indians serving internationally work aboard foreign-flagged vessels, making protection dependent on coordination between India, flag states, shipowners and insurers.India has meanwhile strengthened its own safety net. The government's âSeafarer-Firstâ framework includes real-time tracking of vessels and Indian crews, a 24-hour control room, coordination with the Indian Navy and voyage-specific risk assessments.Government advisories have also directed shipping companies and licensed Recruitment and Placement Services (RPSL) agencies to avoid deploying Indian seafarers on voyages through the Strait of Hormuz during periods of heightened risk.Meanwhile, for Upasha Kumari, a researcher on India's SAGAR doctrine, the bigger problem is that the human cost remains secondary to discussions around shipping.âWe often discuss oil prices and shipping routes, but rarely the people operating those ships,â she said. âIndian seafarers are on the frontlines of these crises.â As commercial routes increasingly overlap with conflict zones, she argued that protecting civilian crews must become a central part of maritime security and not an afterthought.For India, the challenge is not only keeping its seafarers out of danger, but ensuring that those who keep global trade moving are not left to bear the cost of conflicts they did not choose.They are civilians, working far from home, often on vessels whose routes and risks they do not control.As the war pushes commercial shipping deeper into contested waters, the question is no longer simply how to keep the cargo moving. It is how to make sure the people carrying it can make it home.

World.title: TRS chief vows nationwide stir for 50% BC quota in legislatures
World.content:
Telangana Rashtra Sena (TRS) president Kalvakuntla Kavitha on Thursday announced a nationwide movement to secure 50% reservation for Backward Classes (BCs) in legislative bodies, and unveiled a 11-point charter aimed at the empowerment of marginalised communities.

Addressing the Samajika Nyaya Telangana Sankalpa Sabha at Saroornagar, Ms. Kavitha called on the Centre to pass the BC Reservation Bill providing 50% representation to BCs in legislatures before the forthcoming Budget Session of the Parliament.

Warning of intensified agitation if the Bill is not enacted, she said the party would organise a massive ‘Chalo Delhi’ programme with thousands of activists.

Ms. Kavitha said her political decisions were guided by conviction and conscience and expressed confidence that the movement would bring about structural changes in society. She argued that had BCs received reservations in proportion to their population soon after Independence, India would have progressed further and emerged among the world’s leading powers.

Criticising both the ruling dispensation and the Opposition, she accused political leaders of pursuing contradictory positions at the State and national levels. She demanded immediate approval of the State government’s proposal for 42% reservation for BCs, which is pending with the Centre.

Recalling the teachings of late Professor K. Jayashankar on his birth anniversary, a key ideologue of the Telangana movement, Ms. Kavitha said he had maintained that while the struggle for separate statehood and social justice could not be pursued simultaneously, the fight for a socially just Telangana should continue with the same commitment once statehood was achieved.

She reiterated her resolve to carry forward that vision through the movement for greater social justice and political representation for BCs.

World.title: Three booked for assault in Chikkamagaluru
World.content:
Chikkamagaluru Rural Police, on Wednesday, registered a case against three people on charges of assaulting a person belonging to the Scheduled Caste for visiting a temple.

Kumar, 56, a daily wage worker in Hoskote village, in his complaint stated that he visited Anjaneya Temple in the village for prayers as part of customs observed in the month of Ashadha, on Tuesday. While returning from the temple, four people scolded him in foul language, referring to his caste. They questioned him for visiting the temple and chased him with sticks.

The police registered the complaint against Ganesh, Vijay and Mallikarjun. Chikkamagaluru Police are investigating the case.

World.title: Tamil Nadu Budget session to end on September 8; entire proceedings to be telecast live: Speaker
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Speaker J.C.D. Prabhakar on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) said the Budget session of the Assembly would continue till September 8. The entire proceedings of the Assembly would be telecast live, he added.

Addressing journalists after the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) meeting, he said the Revised Agriculture Budget for 2026-27 would be presented in the Assembly on Thursday (August 6). The following day, obituary references for former MLAs and condolence resolutions for filmmaker and actor K. Bhagyaraj, poet Puviyarasu, playback singer S. Janaki, and writer Poomani would be taken up.

Also read: Tamil Nadu Budget 2026 LIVE updates

The general discussion on the Revised Budget Estimates and the Revised Agriculture Budget Estimates for 2026-27 would begin on the same day and continue on August 10, 11, and 12. The discussion and voting on the department-wise Demands for Grants would be taken up from August 17 to September 8.

Mr. Prabhakar said the BAC had decided to hold the sittings from 9.30 a.m. to 1.30 p.m. The committee had also discussed holding the sittings from 4.30 p.m. to 6.30 p.m., if required. A separate announcement would be made if such an extension was required.

On the allocation of seats in the Assembly, Mr. Prabhakar said seats were allotted based on the symbol on which members had contested and won the election, and arranged in alphabetical order.

World.title: Tamil Nadu Budget 2026: Delta region farmers welcome move to expedite river linking project, studies on building barrages
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government’s Budgetary announcement on expediting river interlinking project, especially the Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar river link project, and the proposals for carrying out feasibility studies for building barrages across the River Cauvery and ecological restoration of the Cauvery Delta have largely found favour with farmers’ organisations in the central region.

“Though the allocation of just ₹150 crore for the Cauvery-Gundar project is meagre, we welcome it, as the government has taken the project into consideration after it was in cold storage for the past five years,” said G.S. Dhanapathy, State General Secretary, Farmer’s Forum of India, commenting on the State Budget proposals. He suggested that the government could seek funds for the project from the Centre or even raise a loan from the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development for executing the project.

The project seeks to divert flood discharges in the Cauvery to the water-scarce southern parts of the State by building a 262-km link canal from the Mayanur barrage on the Cauvery to the Vaigai and the Gundar. Construction of the canal by the Water Resources Department at two small stretches for about 10 km under Phase I of the project has been completed so far, but the project has not made any further progress.

Proposals on taking up feasibility studies for building barrages across the Cauvery, to store flood discharges, and the ecological restoration of the Cauvery Delta, with an allocation ₹10 crore each, have also been welcomed by farmers’ organisations.

“It is commendable that the TVK government has taken efforts towards developing irrigation and water management in its very first Budget,” said P.R. Pandian, president, Coordination Committee of All Farmers’ Associations of Tamil Nadu.

However, some of farmers’ leaders, such as Cauvery Dhanapalan, president of Tamil Nadu Vivasaya Sangankalin Kootamaippu, and Swamimalai Vimalnathan, secretary, Tamil Nadu Cauvery Farmers’ Protection Association, pointed out that detailed project reports for the construction of a few barrages across Cauvery and Kollidam rivers had already been prepared and were awaiting execution.

The allocation of ₹9,264 crore for the Water Resources Department should be effectively utilised for the renovation of irrigation tanks and other waterbodies, which have been lying in neglect for years, observed Mr.Dhanapathy.

Veteran farmers’ leader Mahadhanapuram V.Rajaram, however, felt that announcements on implementation of river interlinking projects have become routine in every Budget and emphasised the need for taking steps to store the flood discharges by constructing barrages and renovating the 25,000 lakes in the State.

Disappointment over the absence of an announcement on complete waiver of crop loans and hiking the procurement price of paddy and sugarcane, and calls for a substantial increase for the agriculture sector were also aired by the farmers’ organisations. “Unless you increase the allocation to the sector to at least 10% of the Budget, you cannot expect overall growth or bring about any change,” observed Mr. Dhanapalan.

“We are waiting with hope that announcements on full waiver of crop loans for small and marginal farmers and 50% waiver for big farmers and increasing the procurement prices will be made in the Agriculture Budget to be tabled on Thursday,” said Mr. Pandian.

World.title: Tamil Nadu Budget 2026: ‘Efforts are on to get Centre’s approval for three Chennai Metro Rail extension projects’
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, on Wednesday (August 5, 2026), said the State government is taking efforts to secure the Centre’s approval for the three Chennai Metro Rail extension projects.

In the Budget, he said, three stretches — Chennai airport to Kilambakkam (₹9,335 crore), Koyambedu to Pattabiram via Avadi (₹9,744 crore) and Poonamallee to Sunguvarchathiram via Sriperumbudur (₹8,779 crore)— have been recommended by the State government. It is now under the active consideration of the Government of India, he added.

The detailed project reports (DPR) for these extension projects were forwarded last year to the Centre and was recently reviewed by the Network Planning Group (NPG). Sources said these projects need to receive the nod from the NITI Aayog, Public Investment Board, and finally from the Union Cabinet.

Mr. Wilson also said, the ongoing 118.9 km phase II project, coming up at an estimated completion cost of ₹63,246 crore, was progressing in full swing and that the first stretch from Poonamallee Bypass to Porur Junction connecting the Vadapalani station (14.64 km) was ‘scheduled to be commissioned for public use shortly’.

Hosur-Bommasandra Metro Rail

The Tamil Nadu government has been pursuing the proposal to create a Metro Rail connectivity from Hosur in Krishnagiri district till Bommasandra in Karnataka with the Centre and the Karnataka government.

World.title: Plea to operate weekly, tri-weekly express trains daily from Kanniyakumari to Chennai
World.content:
Member of Parliament C. Robert Bruce has appealed to Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw to increase the frequency of two express trains connecting Kanniyakumari and Chennai from weekly and tri-weekly services into daily service considering the huge demand for tickets on any given day.

In a memorandum submitted to the Minister recently, Mr. Robert Bruce said the Chennai – Kanniyakumar section via Madurai and Tirunelveli generates huge revenue for Southern Railway even though very few trains are being operated in this section and no overnight train had been introduced in this section during the past few decades. Hence, the Southern Railway should give priority for introducing new trains in this section.

In this connection, the Kanniyakumari – Tambaram tri-weekly express train and the Chennai Central – Kanniyakumari weekly express train should be upgraded into daily service to serve the hundreds of wait-listed commuters, who have to now rely on government and private buses to reach their destinations.

“Even though these appeals were discussed and approved earlier, it was yet to be implemented,” Mr. Robert Bruce pointed out.

Similarly, the recently introduced Thiruvananthapuram Central – Tambaram Amrit Bharat Weekly Express is also enjoying high occupancy and hence it should be operated daily.

The MP also said in the memorandum that the Kollam – Kanniyakumari MEMU should be extended up to Tirunelveli.

World.title: Tamil Nadu Budget: Western districts to gain from textile, tourism, and energy initiatives
World.content:
The western districts of Tamil Nadu, from Coimbatore to Krishnagiri, are expected to benefit from the State Budget 2026-27 announcements on textiles, electricity, and tourism.

Presenting the maiden Budget of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government, the State’s Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson said infrastructure facilities in Tiruppur, a garment-exporting hub, will be upgraded in multiple phases to promote environmentally sustainable textile production. A Tiruppur Textiles Technology Centre (TTTC) will be established with a financial outlay of ₹10 crore for this purpose.

Regarding the energy sector, the Finance Minister said the Coimbatore-Ariyalur 765 kV Transmission Line Project will be implemented through the public-private partnership mode at a cost of ₹4,000 crore. The Phase-II Green Energy Corridor Project, valued at ₹1,187 crore and crucial for evacuating renewable energy from the State’s southern districts, will be expedited alongside the Virudhunagar-Coimbatore 765 kV Transmission Project, valued at ₹1,640 crore, the Minister added.

Further, the State government is pursuing a proposal for a Metro rail line from Hosur in Krishnagiri district to Bommasandra in Karnataka with both the Karnataka government and the Union government.

Addressing the long-pending demand of farmers, he said the government will pursue the implementation of the Anaimalaiyar and Nallar dam projects. Further, the Cauvery river, from Hogenakkal to Srirangam, will be included in a ₹53-crore proposal to promote river tourism across Tamil Nadu.

Announcements for western districts Textile Technology Centre for Tiruppur Comprehensive scheme to mitigate human-wildlife conflict Nambikkai Illam in Salem, among other districts, for people with intellectual disabilities River tourism from Hogenakkal to Srirangam

Tourism promotion

On the tourism front, the State government will launch the Tamil Nadu Eco-Tourism Mission to develop and expand nature-based tourism circuits and destinations, including trekking routes, wildlife safaris, birding and boating trails, eco-friendly stays, and interpretation and visitor centres. The Mission will be implemented across the State’s diverse landscapes, including forests and wildlife areas, through active community participation. This is expected to benefit the western districts.

Mr. Wilson promised a comprehensive human-wildlife conflict mitigation scheme incorporating scientific measures such as hanging solar fences and steel wire rope fencing, community-based forest protection, the appointment of forest protection staff, and GPS-enabled vehicles for conflict management, night patrolling, security, and monitoring across 100 conflict-prone villages in Coimbatore, Dharmapuri, Dindigul, Erode, Krishnagiri, the Nilgiris, Salem, Theni, Tirunelveli, Tenkasi, and Tiruppur districts, with an allocation of ₹20 crore for this fiscal.

For the textile sector, the government is looking at a design institute that will be set up with the participation of industry and academia at a cost of ₹60 crore. Technical textiles, an emerging sector, is yet to pick up in the State. The Technical Textiles Transformation Scheme for Entrepreneurs will be implemented in collaboration with international educational and research institutions, with financial assistance from the Tamil Nadu Technical Textiles Mission. This will provide MSMEs and textile manufacturers with international exposure, technical training, technology transfer, market intelligence, innovation support, and business mentorship.

Further, Salem is among the five districts where the Tamil Nadu government will establish an institution for persons with intellectual disabilities under the name ‘Nambikkai Illam’, with a total outlay of ₹4 crore for all five districts. These institutions will provide special education, early intervention services, rehabilitation, and vocational training to children aged three years and above. In the initial stage, each institution will function as a day school with 50 students and will later be upgraded to include residential facilities.

World.title: Tamil Nadu Budget 2026: One-sovereign gold coin, silk saree announced for brides
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government will present an eight-gram (one-sovereign) gold coin and a silk saree as ‘Annan Seer’ (Elder Brother’s Gift) to eligible women on the day of their wedding, Finance Minister Marie Wilson announced in the Assembly on Wednesday (August 5, 2026). An allocation of ₹812 crore has been made in the Revised Budget Estimates for the scheme, which was part of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s (TVK) election promise.

Also read: Tamil Nadu Budget 2026 LIVE updates

Reiterating the State government’s commitment to transforming Tamil Nadu into an elder-friendly State by ensuring a life of dignity, graceful ageing, and comprehensive social security for senior citizens, the Minister told the Legislative Assembly that an integrated home for senior citizens, equipped with essential amenities including qualified caregivers, medical personnel, and recreational facilities, will be established across all districts.

In the first year, 12 such homes will be set up in 12 districts, each accommodating 40 beneficiaries, with an allocation of ₹6.6 crore. Additionally, senior citizens’ recreation centres featuring libraries, yoga and meditation facilities, and indoor sports amenities will be established in five districts in the initial phase, selected on the basis of the population of senior citizens.

Anganwadi centres

The Minister said the government will construct 500 Anganwadi centres during the current financial year, ensuring the provision of essential basic amenities such as safe drinking water, toilets, and electricity. The initiative aims to ensure that the Anganwadi centres attended by children every day provide quality early childhood care and a safe and healthy environment.

Shelter homes for trans people

To support the transgender community in achieving socio-economic empowerment, the Minister said skill training will be provided in various income-generating trades through the Tamil Nadu Skill Development Corporation.

“Along with this, subsidy-linked bank credit facilities will be extended to enable them to establish enterprises and secure sustainable livelihoods. They will also be assisted in availing themselves of bank loans for self-employment, with a subsidy of up to ₹50,000,” he said.

Mr. Wilson announced the government will establish ‘Aran’ shelter homes in five districts to provide safe accommodation, food, counselling, and rehabilitation support to transgender persons facing social and family-related challenges. In addition, short-stay homes will be established in 15 districts to meet the needs of transgender persons travelling to other cities for education, employment, medical treatment, examinations, and training programmes.

An allocation of ₹9,818 crore has been made for the Social Welfare and Women’s Empowerment Department.

World.title: Security forces kill 12 terrorists in Balochistan's Mastung, Washuk IBOs: ISPR
World.content:
Security forces conducted two intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan’s Washuk and Mastung districts, killing 12 terrorists in total, the military’s media wing said on Thursday.

In a statement, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said the “high-tempo” operations were carried out as part of the ‘Radul Fitna’ counterterrorism campaign against Fitna-al-Hindustan in Balochistan.

Balochistan-based terrorist groups have been designated as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

The ISPR said that on August 5, “[The] movement of six terrorists was picked up by the security forces in Washuk District of Balochistan. Own troops effectively engaged these terrorists. As a result of precise and skilful engagement, all six terrorists belonging to Indian proxy, Fitna-al-Hindustan were sent to hell.”

The military’s media wing further said that during an operation in the Mastung district earlier today, six terrorists were “sent to hell after the intense fire exchange between armed forces and the terrorists”, while a terrorist hideout was also destroyed.

“Under vision ‘Azm-i-Istehkam’ (as approved by [the] Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan), security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out [the] menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” the statement concludes.

Last Wednesday, eight terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan were killed after an “intense engagement” in Balochistan’s Nushki district during multiple intelligence-based operations, the ISPR said.

“Weapons, ammunition and improvised explosive devices used by terrorists were also recovered and destroyed during the operations,” it added.

In July, security forces and law enforcement personnel jointly launched Operation Shaban in Balochistan in retaliation for a deadly attack on a police post at the Mangi Dam pumping station in Ziarat on July 6. During that assault, armed attackers kidnapped and killed 27 police officers .

Later, security forces also launched Operation Al-Azm in the province after a shooting on a Karachi-bound coach coming from Quetta claimed three lives and injured five others last week.

A monthly security assessment released in early June by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS) said that after two consecutive months of improvement, Pakistan’s security situation deteriorated sharply in May, driven primarily by escalating terrorist violence in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

The report said Balochistan emerged as the most affected province during the month. The province recorded 71 terrorist attacks, compared with 34 in April, representing a 109pc increase.

The deteriorating security situation was further reflected in a surge in kidnappings, it said. Of the 54 abductions reported nationwide during May, 52 occurred in Balochistan alone, highlighting the growing operational reach and confidence of terrorist groups in the province, it said.

World.title: PM Shehbaz departs for Saudi Arabia on 3-day visit
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday left for a three-day visit to Saudi Arabia, where he will be accompanied by the Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.

In a post on X, the government said that the premier has left for the visit at the invitation of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

Apart from CDF Munir, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, and Special Assistant Tariq Fatemi will also accompany the premier on the visit.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Muhammad Ishaq Dar, who is currently in Saudi Arabia after concluding a visit to Jordan, will be part of the delegation as well.

The premier will also perform Umrah and visit Holy Prophet’s (PBUH) mosque in Madina during the visit, the government said.

Earlier, FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi announced the visit in a weekly briefing.

“During the visit, the prime minister will meet the Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and discussions will focus on consolidating the Pakistan-Saudi bilateral relationship and exchange views on areas of regional and international developments of mutual interests,” he said.

He stressed that the visit marked Pakistan’s “long-standing partnership” with Saudi Arabia, which he said was “anchored in decades of mutual trust, cooperation and brotherhood”.

Andrabi noted that while the visit was taking place amid heightened tensions in the Gulf, he said that “it will carry immense significance beyond the immediate crisis and short-term considerations”.

He added that the visit will “further strengthen bilateral relations, deepen strategic cooperation, enhance coordination on regional and international issues of mutual interest and also reinforce multilateral cooperation”.

Shortly after, an official statement regarding the visit was also issued.

The premier had last visited Saudi Arabia in April, meeting with the kingdom’s top leadership.

As the Middle East conflict has expanded across new fronts, Saudi Arabia has unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea region. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, have voiced support for the coalition.

In July, Pakistan also endorsed Saudi Arabia’s air strikes in Iraq as an exercise of its right to self-defence. The remarks came two days after Saudi Arabia and the US carried out coordinated strikes against installations of Iraq’s Popular Mobilisation Units, accusing elements within the umbrella force of launching attacks on Saudi oil facilities.

The remarks followed Pakistan’s earlier warning after Yemen’s Houthi rebels announced a maritime blockade targeting shipping linked to Saudi Arabia. Islamabad had then described attacks on Pakistani maritime interests as a “red line”, warning that any hostile action against Pakistani-flagged vessels or commercial shipping would be treated as an attack on Pakistan.

The country also simultaneously reaffirmed its commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security and the uninterrupted flow of lawful maritime commerce through the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb.

Last year, Islamabad and Riyadh concluded a Strategic Mutual Defence Agree­ment, which became operational earlier this year as Pakistan simultaneously embarked on a diplomatic effort to mediate between Iran and the United States.

World.title: FO slams India's remarks on AJK polls, says it has no 'standing or moral authority' to comment on process
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) said on Thursday that India had “neither the standing nor the moral authority” to comment on the elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), which are being held in phases amid security concerns and unrest in the region.

FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi made the remarks while addressing a weekly press briefing, where he was asked about the Indian External Affairs Ministry’s (MEA) “reaction” to the ongoing polls. While the question did not elaborate further, the Indian ministry had termed the polls a “farce” on Tuesday, saying that such “hollow exercises” could not hide the reality.

“Pakistan categorically rejects the baseless and politically motivated remarks of the Indian MEA regarding the ongoing legislative elections in the AJK,” Andrabi said on Thursday.

“It is unsurprising that India has chosen to issue such remarks on the eve of the 7th anniversary of its illegal and unilateral actions of August 5, through which it seeks to alter the internationally recognised disputed status of Jammu and Kashmir,” he said, adding that actions violated the relevant UN Security Council (UNSC) resolutions, international law, and India’s international commitments.

Andrabi held that elections in AJK were being conducted in a “peaceful, transparent and orderly manner” in accordance with the constitutional and legal framework governing the region.

He added that the ongoing elections reflected “democratic aspirations and political will of the people of AJK”.

Andrabi maintained that India, in view of its continued denial of fundamental political rights and democratic freedom in occupied Kashmir, “has neither the standing nor the moral authority to comment on the democratic process in AJK”.

He added that misinformation and propaganda could not change the status of occupied Kashmir, which remained a disputed territory.

“Its final disposition is to be determined in accordance with relevant UNSC resolutions as well as the freely expressed will of the Kashmiri people and through a UN-administered plebiscite,” he said.

He also held that India’s “attempt to invoke misleading casualty figures” cannot obscure its own actions in occupied Kashmir.

Andrabi said such statements were an attempt to deflect international attention away from India’s “continued violation of international human rights and humanitarian law and its persistent failure to fulfil international obligations”.

At this, he called on the neighbouring India to reverse its illegal actions of August 5, 2019 and “create an environment conducive to peaceful settlement in accordance with the relevant UNSC resolutions”.

The FO spokesperson was also asked about the Indian ministry’s response to comments made by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on the occasion of Youm-i-Istehsal wherein it had condemned Pakistan’s “desperate peddling of falsehoods”.

He held that the Indian MEA statement was a “self-serving eulogy” for its actions in the occupied Kashmir.

“The reality is that a prolonged and heavy military presence, coupled with draconian laws, continues to facilitate demographic change aimed at altering the territory’s Muslim majority character.”
